outlooksByWeek.1: CeeDee Lamb came on strong towards the end of the season for the Cowboys, but otherwise had a disappointing 2024 campaign, as he averaged the lowest yards per catch average of his career while also scoring just six times. Dallas figures to be involved in a lot of shootouts this season, though, given the jettison of Micah Parsons from the defensive side of the ball. That certainly bodes well for Lamb and the passing game.   Unfortunately, the Week 1 matchup against the Eagles is less than ideal. Philadelphia allowed the fewest passing yards in the NFL last season, just 174.2 yards per clash through the air.
outlooksByWeek.2: CeeDee Lamb crossed the 100-yard receiving mark in the season opener for the Cowboys, though the night will be remembered more for a couple of costly drops than for his overall stat line. Lamb could not corral two separate passes from Dak Prescott in the fourth quarter that ultimately stalled the comeback attempts in the 24-20 loss to the Eagles. Still, Lamb had just three 100-yard outings all of last season, so the production remains promising from a fantasy perspective. In Week 2, the Cowboys will face the New York Giants. The G-Men allowed only 212 passing yards and a single passing touchdown in Week 1 versus the Commanders. Lamb is also likely to draw coverage from one of the Giants stellar defensive offseason acquisitions, cornerback Paulson Adebo.
outlooksByWeek.3: CeeDee Lamb has gained at least 110 receiving yards in each of the first two games for the Cowboys. Lamb snagged nine passes for 112 yards in the 40-37 thrilling OT win over the Giants. Lamb has been targeted 24 times over the first two contests. Lamb should continue to see plenty of balls thrown his way in Week 3 versus a struggling Bears defense. The Bears have allowed the most points in the NFL through two games, including a league-worst seven receiving touchdowns.

player.seasonOutlook: Lamb is entering his sixth NFL season eyeing a bounce-back after missing two games and finding the end zone only six times in 2024. For many receivers, 101 catches and an eighth-place finish in fantasy points would be a career year, but it was a step back for Lamb after he led all receivers in yards, touchdowns and fantasy points in 2023. Despite Dak Prescott missing more than half the season, Lamb managed his third straight top-8 fantasy campaign and only two receivers accrued more touches. In his prime at age 26, Lamb remains one of the league's best receivers and he will get Prescott back this season. He's a solid WR1 option with elite upside who may come at a slight discount on draft day.

outlooksByWeek.1: De'Von Achane appears healthy and has minimal competition for touches in the Dolphins backfield ahead of a Week 1 matchup at Indianapolis. Achane nursed a calf issue throughout preseason but looks cleared for heavy usage in both the rushing and passing attack against a defense that allowed the 11th most fantasy points to running backs a year ago. Jaylen Wright (leg) is unlikely to play, leaving only rookie Ollie Gordon as a potential touchdown vulture to cap Achane's upside. He remains an elite option when healthy.
outlooksByWeek.2: De'Von Achane could face an uphill battle in Week 2 when the Dolphins host the Patriots. Achane logged an impressive 7.9 yards per carry last Sunday and scored on one of his three receptions, but Miami's offense looked lost in the passing game. The Patriots can stack the box, and they shut down Las Vegas rookie Ashton Jeanty last week, allowing just 2.1 yards per carry. Achane is arguably the best option in this dysfunctional offense, and his volume should keep the floor stable, and the ceiling is through the roof if something clicks with the aerial attack.
outlooksByWeek.3: De'Von Achane's versatility will likely again make him an asset in Week 3 for the Dolphins when they face the Bills Thursday night. He's coming off a 19-touch game where he again caught a touchdown, and with 14 target in two games, Achane won't be scripted out of the game if the Bills grab a early lead. The early yardage isn't elite, but Achne faces a defense he gashed in two meetings last year for 286 total yards on a large 49 touches, so he can be safely deployed in all formats.

player.seasonOutlook: One of the rising stars in fantasy, Achane is entering his third NFL season after an impressive 2024, in which he registered only the 12th instance over the last decade of a player producing 200-plus carries and 75-plus receptions in a single season. Achane has now scored at least 11 TDs in both NFL seasons and paced all RBs in routes, catches, yards and receiving TDs last season. He also put size concerns aside, appearing in 17 games and finishing ninth among RBs in snaps. Achane's play plummeted when Tua Tagovailoa was sidelined (9.8 fantasy PPG), but he was elite when his QB was under center (22.6), which is the more relevant number with Tagovailoa back for 2025. Achane's dual-threat ability locks him in as a solid fantasy RB1.

outlooksByWeek.1: Joe Burrow enjoyed a healthy 2024 season and led the league in both passing yards (4,918) and touchdowns (43), so it shouldn't come as a surprise that he was an excellent fantasy option. He'll also lead the Bengals into a Week 1 matchup against the Browns with his top pass catchers back, most importantly Tee Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase. Cleveland has a decent defense when healthy, though they've already lost corner Martin Emerson for the season due to an Achilles injury. Burrow also played in two of three preseason games in hopes of having a faster start to the season, making him a top-end quarterback option in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.2: Joe Burrow's trend of starting slowly continued in Week 1, as he averaged an abysmal 5.0 yards per attempt while accounting for only one touchdown against the Browns. However, he and the Bengals will likely have to open up the offense in a Week 2 matchup against the Jaguars, which should lead to more volume and better fantasy results for Burrow and his primary pass catchers. He isn't in the elite tier at quarterback with the likes of Josh Allen, Jayden Daniels, Lamar Jackson and Jalen Hurts, but Burrow is comfortably a top six option at the position. He should make fantasy managers forget about his poor Week 1 showing.

player.seasonOutlook: The reigning NFL Comeback Player of the Year, Burrow rebounded from an injury-plagued 2023 by proceeding to pace the NFL in pass attempts, completions, yards and TDs. He appeared in 17 games for the first time in his career and contributed enough with his legs to end up third among QBs in fantasy points. Burrow, who was off target on a league-low 11% of his attempts, has now finished eighth or better in fantasy points each season he's appeared in more than 10 games (fourth or better in the last two). He'll continue to benefit from the league's pass-heaviest offense, as well as the terrific Ja'Marr Chase/Tee Higgins duo. Burrow's limited rushing output is all that stops him from joining the elite fantasy QBs, but he's nonetheless a very good starting option.

outlooksByWeek.1: Marvin Harrison kicks off his second NFL season as Arizona takes on New Orleans in Week 1. Harrison played in all 17 games as a rookie last year and finished with a modest 62-885-8 line. He'll look to take a step forward in 2025 with mostly the same offense around him, including QB Kyler Murray and No. 2 wideout Michael Wilson. The Saints gave up the fifth-most receiving yards to wideouts last year, though New Orleans revamped its defense during the offseason and will have more new starters in the secondary than returning ones.
outlooksByWeek.2: Marvin Harrison had a promising performance for Arizona in the team's season-opening win and will look to build upon that in Week 2 versus Carolina. Harrison recorded five catches on six targets for 71 yards Sunday against the Saints, getting into the end zone on a one-yard TD catch. Harrison does face competition for targets with star tight end Trey McBride, who compiled a 6-61-0 line in the opener, though no other Cardinals pass catcher tallied more than 10 yards through the air. Carolina was gashed on the ground in a Week 1 loss to Jacksonville, so it wouldn't be surprising if Arizona looked to establish its running game more than its air attack this coming Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.3: Marvin Harrison will look to rebound from a rough Week 2 when Arizona takes on the 49ers in Week 3. After recording 71 yards and a touchdown on five catches in the season opener, Harrison totaled just 27 yards on two catches this past Sunday versus Carolina. In fact, no Cardinals WR managed more than two receptions in that latter game, as TE Trey McBride led the team in both catches (six) and receiving yards (78). The 49ers could offer an opportunity to rebound, as they've given up a 70.6 percent catch rate -- fifth-highest in the league -- through two weeks.

player.seasonOutlook: Harrison is a candidate for a Year 2 leap after he didn't quite live up to the "fourth overall pick" hype as a rookie. In some ways, Harrison was afforded plenty of opportunity -- he ranked third in the league in end zone targets (17) and ninth in air yards (1,518) -- but he was limited in other ways (zero designed screens and a deep-threat role that led to an ugly 54% catch rate and 22% off-target rate). Harrison scored eight TDs, but finished 37th in catches and 30th in both yards and fantasy points (41st in PPG). There's some obvious risk here, but Harrison was drafted with the expectation he'd be an elite player and it's only logical that he'll be treated that way in terms of usage in his second season. If that happens, the sky is the limit in terms of fantasy production. There's some projection here, but Harrison should be valued as a fringe WR2.

outlooksByWeek.1: Courtland Sutton is coming off a 2024 season in which he set new career highs with 81 catches on 135 targets as the Broncos' unquestioned top wide receiver, adding 1,081 receiving yards and eight touchdowns. The 29-year-old showed impressive chemistry with rookie QB Bo Nix as the campaign progressed, and over his last 10 regular-season games Sutton delivered a 60-804-6 line before adding a 5-75-0 line in a wild-card loss to Buffalo. While the team added to Nix's supporting cast in the offseason with tight end Evan Engram and a revamped backfield, Sutton's spot as the top target went unchallenged. He'll look to kick off his 2025 season in style with a Week 1 meeting at home against a Titans defense that was more vulnerable on the ground than through the air last year, allowing the second-fewest receiving yards to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.2: Courtland Sutton was the Broncos' top downfield option, as expected, in Week 1, turning a team-high nine targets into 61 receiving yards and a touchdown. The chemistry he established with quarterback Bo Nix last year carried forward into 2025, but Nix struggled when he wasn't throwing the ball to Sutton. That could lead to higher target volume for the veteran WR, but also more defensive attention unless someone like Marvin Mims emerges as a threat secondaries need to worry about. Sutton will take on a Colts defense in Week 2 that completely shut down a dysfunctional Dolphins passing game in its opener, but which finished in the bottom half of the league in yards and TDs allowed to wideouts in 2024.
outlooksByWeek.3: Courtland Sutton couldn't get anything going in Week 2 against the Colts, turning four targets into just one catch for six yards. The Broncos' passing game in general was productive as Bo Nix threw three touchdowns, but the team's top wideout couldn't get in on the action. Sutton may need some of his teammates to step up and take some defensive attention away from him, so Troy Franklin's 8-89-1 line, along with Marvin Mims' first TD of the year, were encouraging developments on that front. Sutton could struggle to contribute in Week 3 against a Chargers secondary that just held the Raiders' Geno Smith under 200 passing yards while picking him off three times.

player.seasonOutlook: Sutton is entering his eighth NFL season fresh off a career year in which he finished 17th or better among WRs in snaps, routes, targets, catches, TDs and fantasy points. Sutton ranked top 3 in both air yards and end zone targets and he's now finished in the top 10 in end zone targets three seasons in a row. Sutton has yet to finish a season in the top 25 in fantasy PPG, but he's emerged as the clear top target (25% target share last season) for a Broncos offense that is much improved with Bo Nix under center. Sutton, 29, is a solid WR3 option.

outlooksByWeek.1: Isiah Pacheco's 2024 season was ruined by a fractured fibula in Week 2, as the running back missed the next nine games and averaged just 3.4 yards per carry for the rest of the regular season and the playoffs once he returned. When he's healthy, his full-bore running style gives the Kansas City offense a physical element that matches well with its new defensive identity, but it also opens him up to further injury. Kareem Hunt proved to be a useful complementary piece in his return to the team last year, but at 30 years old he's not capable of handling a big, sustained workload without his own efficiency suffering. Pacheco will look to put on a show in Sao Paulo in Week 1 against the Chargers, but he'll be facing a defense that gave up a league-low four rushing touchdowns to RBs last year.
outlooksByWeek.2: Isiah Pacheco shared the workload in the Kansas City backfield equally with Kareem Hunt in Week 1. Both backs had five carries and two receptions on three targets, with Pacheco's 28 scrimmage yards just slightly besting Hunt's 26. Pacheco is younger and more explosive, but coming off an injury-plagued 2024, the team isn't likely to treat him like a bell cow any time soon, and he's likely to remain stuck in a timeshare. Pacheco will face an Eagles defense in Week 2 that gave up two goal-line TDs to the Cowboys' Javonte Williams in its opener, but only after star DT Jalen Carter got himself ejected immediately following the opening kickoff.
outlooksByWeek.3: Isiah Pacheco has struggled to get going to begin the season, averaging just 3.1 yards on 15 carries and adding only 10 receiving yards on three receptions while failing to get into the end zone. Kareem Hunt has only been marginally more productive however, and the duo will likely continue to split the workload in the Kansas City backfield, at least until one of them heats up. The entire offense has sputtered so far, but facing two tough defenses in the Chargers and Eagles likely contributed to that lack of production. Pacheco could break out in Week 3 against a Giants defense that just coughed up 97 rushing yards and a touchdown to Javonte Williams.

player.seasonOutlook: Pacheco enters 2025 as a tricky evaluation. He emerged as Kansas City's lead back in Week 10 of his rookie season (2022) and proceeded to average 17.6 touches, 86.0 yards, 0.6 TDs and 14.2 fantasy points per game over his next 32 outings, including the playoffs. A broken fibula suffered in Week 2 last season cost him nine games and he wasn't quite the same after that, averaging 8.8 touches and 4.2 fantasy points per game while rotating with Kareem Hunt and Samaje Perine. The 26-year-old has upside if he retakes clear lead-back duties, but that's far from certain with Hunt and Elijah Mitchell in the mix. There's some post-hype appeal here, but Pacheco should be viewed as a midround lottery ticket.

outlooksByWeek.1: David Montgomery and Jahmyr Gibbs will return as the league's most formidable one-two punch at RB as the Lions travel to Green Bay in Week 1. There's no guaranteed that Detroit's offense - which scored a league-high 33.2 points per game in 2024 - avoids a decline after having lost former OC Ben Johnson, as well as RG Kevin Zeitler to the Titans and C Frank Ragnow to retirement, but Montgomery's skill set remains crucial for coach Dan Campbell's philosophy of establishing the run. Gibbs thrived in a workhorse role after Montgomery went down to an MCL injury and could push for more than an even split touches, but Week 1 against a Packers defense that ranked third against the pass last season, but was average against the run, both ball carriers figure to be heavily involved.
outlooksByWeek.2: David Montgomery and the Lions will host the Bears in Week 2, with the aim to rebound after a sluggish Week 1 performance. In the season opener against the Packers, Montgomery rushed for just 25 yards on 11 carries (2.3 YPC) and added 18 receiving yards on six catches. Despite those underwhelming stats, Montgomery led the Lions' backfield (logging one more carry than Jahmyr Gibbs) and was the team's primary goal-line option. Gibbs, however, saw 10 targets in the passing game. His physical running style makes him the favorite to grind tough yards against Chicago's front seven, which struggled against the run last season, allowing 4.93 YPC to opposing running backs (third-worst in the league).
outlooksByWeek.3: David Montgomery and the Lions will travel to Baltimore in WeekaA� 3, coming off a 52-21 rout of the Bears. He carried the ball 11 times for 57 yards and a score versus Chicago, while also bringing in his only target for four yards, again taking a slight backseat to Jahmyr Gibbs. While the more explosive Gibbs appears the more definitive leader of the Lions' backfield, Montgomery is still the favorite for more physical duties and looks entrenched as a double-digit touch contributor on a weekly basis. Baltimore's front seven is a tougher matchup than Chicago's, but Montgomery's role as a reliable between-the-tackles runner and short-yardage target makes him a low-end RB2/high-floor flex, particularly if the Lions stay competitive and feed him consistent touches.

player.seasonOutlook: Montgomery is entering his seventh NFL season, including his third with Detroit. Jahmyr Gibbs' running mate played 13 full games last season, averaging 16.3 touches and 16.5 fantasy points per game. He had one of the highest floors in fantasy, posting at least 12.6 points in all but one of the outings. Montgomery's ceiling will be limited as long as Gibbs is in the mix, but he handles a solid workload as a rusher, including near the goal line (he's finished exactly fourth with 17 carries inside the 5 each of the last two seasons), and he saw a boost in receiving work last season (2.8 targets per game). Montgomery is now 28 years old and could cede a few more touches to Gibbs this season, but he's finished 16th or better in fantasy PPG each of the last two years and is a good bet to remain on the RB2/flex radar again in 2025.

outlooksByWeek.1: Tyler Warren will make his NFL debut in the Colts' Week 1 home game against the Dolphins. He was drafted 14th overall out of Penn State after recording 1,233 receiving yards and 15 total TDs in his final college campaign. While he shouldn't be expected to rewrite Brock Bowers' rookie records from last season, Warren's combination of skill and opportunity could allow him to be an immediate fantasy starter at TE, as he's already the clear No. 1 option at the position for the Colts. With a steady diet of short passes likely to come his way from QB Daniel Jones against a Dolphins defense that ranked in the middle of the pack at defending TEs last season, Warren's a low-end starter at the position for Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.2: Tyler Warren has already worked his way well into the starting fantasy TE range heading into a Week 2 home game against the Broncos. After a prolific final college season at Penn State, the 2025 first-round pick immediately established himself as a key part of the Colts' passing game, turning a team-high nine targets into seven catches for 76 yards in a Week 1 rout of the Dolphins. Denver's elite secondary limits WR production, which often results in more work for TEs, to whom the Broncos allowed the ninth-most catches in the NFL last season. Warren's primed for another busy outing in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tyler Warren followed up his 76-yard NFL debut with 79 yards in Week 2, and the rookie first-round pick looks like the most reliable option in the Colts' passing game heading into Week 3 against the Titans. Tennessee has been more vulnerable on the ground than through the air, but the Titans gave up a TD to Rams TE Davis Allen last week. Warren's significant involvement in Indianapolis' passing game puts him safely into the starting fantasy tight end range, though he's still searching for his first NFL TD after scoring 12 times in his last college season at Penn State.

player.seasonOutlook: Warren was selected by the Colts in the first round of April's draft. Much like Brock Bowers one year ago, Warren is an elite tight end prospect who could eventually emerge as one of the best in the game. He handled a 32% target share at Penn State last season, which allowed a 104-1,233-8 receiving line in 16 games. His 2.84 YPRR was second best in this TE class, and he added 26-218-4 as a rusher. He has the size, athleticism and receiving ability to post top-end numbers, though his stats could be limited in the short term as he works in a Colts offense that is unfriendly to pass catchers due to uncertainty at quarterback. Warren is a terrific dynasty hold, but is best viewed as a mid-to-late-round lottery ticket in 2025 drafts.

outlooksByWeek.1: Khalil Shakir is hoping to build on last season's career-best numbers. In Week 1, Buffalo hosts the Ravens and Shakir notched at least six targets in all of the Bills final 13 games last year, including the postseason, but topped 100 yards only twice. He posted 62 and 67 yards against Baltimore in two meetings, and while Shakir is still likely Josh Allen's safety valve in the passing game, there's a clear lack of yardage and scoring upside.
outlooksByWeek.2: Khalil Shakir will again look to provide the Bills with a safety valve in their passing attack in Week 2 against the Jets. Shakir had six catches for 64 yards in Week 1, collecting nine targets, eerily similar to his 2024 season that, garnering between six and 12 targets in each of his final 13 games, but topping 100 yards only twice. While the Bills are unlikely to throw as much in Week 2, Shakir's role is as clear as ever, making him a low ceiling, stable floor option at WR3 or flex.
outlooksByWeek.3: Khalil Shakir seeks a bounce back game in Week 3 when the Bills host the Dolphins on Thursday night. Shakir notched just two targets in Week 2, his lowest volume since Week 6 of 2024, snapping a 14-game stretch of recording at least six targets. Miami's secondary has shown more vulnerability on the outside this season, and Shakir posted 11 catches and 104 yards against them in two games last year. That's the expectation again, landing Shakir in WR3/flex territory as a stable yet unexciting option.

player.seasonOutlook: After two years in a situational role, Shakir emerged as Josh Allen's top target in 2024. The results were good in reality -- he caught 77% of his targets and was elite with the ball in his hands (7.9 RAC), both of which ranked fourth among WRs -- but not as much in fantasy. Shakir finished 35th in fantasy PPG and had little upside (his best weekly finish was 10th). He handled a 23% target share (an appealing number in a great offense), but most of it is in the short area (29% of his targets were screens) and he simply doesn't get much run near the goal line (seven career TDs and five career end zone targets). The 25-year-old's role drastically limits his ceiling and, especially with Keon Coleman and perhaps Dalton Kincaid ticketed for a leap forward, Shakir is best valued as a flex.

Brian Flores' defense surged early in 2025, scoring a league-leading 117 fantasy points through 11 weeks, before cooling off late. The offseason additions of DTs Jonathan Allen and Javon Hargrave should strengthen their interior, though as members of the competitive NFC North, and with four games against the NFC East, the Vikings have one of the toughest D/ST schedules. Early middling matchups (@CHI, ATL in Weeks 1-2) should hint at the level of matchups homework involved with this intriguing defense.

outlooksByWeek.1: Brian Robinson is slated for his first action with the 49ers in Week 1 versus Seattle. The ex-Commander is firmly behind Christian McCaffrey on the RB depth chart, though the incumbent starter's injury-marred 2024 season may influence San Francisco to reduce his workload to some extent. Robinson has proven capable in both the running and passing games in his career, but it would likely take a McCaffrey injury for him to get on the field enough to make a substantial impact in fantasy. The Seahawks represent a beatable Week 1 opponent having ranked middle-of-the-pack against the run last year.
outlooksByWeek.2: Brian Robinson and the 49ers will head to New Orleans in Week 2 after eking out a victory over the Seahawks in the season opener. Robinson got decent volume as the backup to Christian McCaffrey against Seattle, rushing nine time for 33 yards and adding one catch for four yards. He could again get a decent amount of work against the Saints, especially if Brock Purdy, who is iffy due to injuries to his shoulder and toe, doesn't play. Mac Jones would start behind center if Purdy can't suit up, but the 49ers could elect to lean on the run game heavily. Their Week 2 opponent, the Saints, surrendered 146 yards on 27 carries (5.4 YPC) to Arizona in Week 1, with Cardinals No. 2 RB Trey Benson going for 69 yards on just eight carries.
outlooksByWeek.3: Brian Robinson enters Week 3 against Arizona firmly entrenched as San Francisco's No. 2 running back behind Christian McCaffrey. Robinson hasn't yet been able to get going on the ground, totaling 53 yards on 15 carries (3.5 YPC) through two games. McCaffrey has logged a heavy workload during that span, so Robinson figures to continue to see a limited amount of touches per week. The 49ers' Week 3 opponent, Arizona, has held RBs mostly in check on the ground so far, allowing 3.68 YPC and one TD through two contests.

player.seasonOutlook: Robinson was traded to the 49ers in August after leading Washington in carries during each of his first three NFL campaigns. While working in a committee with Austin Ekeler last season (eight full games, including the playoffs), Robinson handled 12.8 carries and 1.9 targets per game while playing 51% of the snaps. In those eight games, Robinson dominated goal-line work (four TDs and eight carries inside the 5), but wasn't a great fantasy option (11.1 PPG). The 26-year-old has missed two-plus games in all three pro seasons and has yet to finish better than 24th among backs in snaps, touches or yards. He's now positioned as a clear backup to Christian McCaffrey and is likely to see only a few touches each game. Robinson has some insurance appeal, but even if McCaffrey were to miss time, he'd likely share the backfield with Isaac Guerendo and would thus max out as a flex.

outlooksByWeek.1: Marvin Mims took a step forward in 2024, setting modest career highs with 39 catches for 503 yards and six touchdowns. Most of his production came in the second half as rookie QB Bo Nix began to feel his oats, and Mims recorded two 100-yard performances in the last five regular-season games. The Broncos' second-round pick in 2023 offers field-stretching speed, making him a strong complement to top wideout Courtland Sutton. Seven of Mims 61 career receptions have gone for 40 yards or more. he could be headed for a true breakout, but first he'll have to get over a minor groin issue and past a stingy Titans secondary in Week 1 that allowed the second-fewest receiving yards in the NFL last year to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.2: Marvin Mims had a tough start to his 2025 campaign, catching three of four targets for a mere 12 yards and losing a fumble. The third-year wideout's struggles mirrored those of his quarterback Bo Nix, and the duo will need to turn things around quickly if the Broncos' passing game is going to rise to the next level. Mims remains firmly behind Courtland Sutton in the pecking order for targets, but he represents the team's biggest threat as a field-stretcher. Mims will try to bounce back in Week 2 against a Colts secondary that completely shut down a dysfunctional Dolphins offense in its opener, but which finished in the bottom half of the league in yards and TDs allowed to wideouts in 2024.
outlooksByWeek.3: Marvin Mims scored his first touchdown of the season in a Week 2 loss to the Colts despite limited volume, catching both his targets for 24 yards and a score. The third-year speedster is capable of stretching the field, but Courtland Sutton is entrenched as the Broncos' top wideout, while Troy Franklin, a college teammate of quarterback Bo Nix, may be emerging as the team's WR2. That won't leave much volume for Mims, despite his big-play potential. He's unlikely to make a splash in Week 3 against a Chargers secondary that just held the Raiders' Geno Smith under 200 passing yards while picking him off three times.

player.seasonOutlook: Mims is entering his third NFL season with breakout potential after a red-hot finish to 2024. After barely seeing work his first year and a half in the league (1.6 touches per game), the 2023 second-round pick handled 12 carries and 37 targets during Weeks 10-18 (eight games). He scored six TDs and averaged 13.0 fantasy PPG, which included three games with 19-plus points in his final five outings. On the negative side, Mims remained a part-time player during his heater, failing to play more than 48% of the offensive snaps in any game prior to hitting a career-high 69% in the playoff loss to Buffalo. With Courtland Sutton the only receiver clearly ahead of him on the depth chart in Denver, Mims is positioned for a Year 3 leap. He's a fine late-round lottery ticket.

outlooksByWeek.1: Trevor Lawrence and the Jaguars look to bounce back from a disappointing 2024 campaign in a Week 1 home matchup against the Panthers, who allowed a league-high 31.4 PPG last season but were worse against the run than the pass. After producing 30 total touchdowns in 2022 and 25 in 2023, Lawrence had only 14 in 10 games last season prior to having his season cut short by a concussion and injury to his non-throwing shoulder. Now healthy, the 2021 first overall pick has a new key target in rookie second overall pick Travis Hunter, who joins a WR room headlined by 2024 first-round pick Brian Thomas. Lawrence is in play out of the gate for superflex and two-QB formats, but managers in one-QB leagues might want to take a wait-and-see approach as Lawrence adapts to the system of new head coach Liam Coen, who was the Buccaneers' offensive coordinator for Baker Mayfield's 41-pass TD season in 2024.
outlooksByWeek.2: Trevor Lawrence will try to bounce back from an underwhelming season debut when the Jaguars travel to Cincinnati in Week 2. He threw for only 178 yards, one touchdown and one interception in Week 1 against the Panthers, though the Jaguars leaned predominantly on the running game while leading by double digits the entire second half. The Bengals tied for the seventh-most points allowed last season and surrendered 290 passing yards to Joe Flacco in Week 1, so Lawrence has a nice opportunity to pick up the pace while working with a talented WR room led by 2024 and 2025 first-round picks Brian Thomas and Travis Hunter. Lawrence is worth considering as a streamer in single-QB leagues this week and makes for a high-ceiling superflex option.
outlooksByWeek.3: Trevor Lawrence has four touchdown passes but also three interceptions heading into Jacksonville's Week 3 home game against a Texans secondary that allowed the third-most touchdown passes (31) but also notched the second-most interceptions (19) last season. There may be some extra bad blood between these AFC South rivals considering Lawrence was knocked out of their last meeting by a hit to the head from Houston linebacker Aziz Al-Shaair, which earned Al-Shaair a three-game suspension. Despite slow starts from top targets Brian Thomas and Travis Hunter, Lawrence has started decently as a passer in 2025 by spreading the ball around, making him a superflex option for Week 3. Lawrence is averaging just 11.3 rushing yards in 12 games since the start of last season, down from 19.3 over his first three campaigns.

player.seasonOutlook: Lawrence is entering his fifth NFL season eyeing a bounce-back after an injury-plagued 2024. Lawrence played the bulk of the snaps in nine games and averaged 16.1 fantasy PPG. That would've ranked 15th over the full season and is actually a slight step back from 17.4 in 2022 and 16.4 in 2023. The former No. 1 overall pick has yet to deliver a top-10 fantasy campaign (PPG) and that's despite finishing each of his first three NFL seasons in the top 10 among QBs in pass attempts, carries and rush yards. Lawrence is a solid player who adds just enough with his arm and legs to hang in the QB2 mix. His ceiling has obviously been low, but perhaps the presence of Brian Thomas Jr., Travis Hunter and new head coach Liam Coen can get him to the next level. He's a fine but unspectacular late-round pick.

outlooksByWeek.1: Harrison Butker is coming off one of his least productive seasons. The Kansas City kicker was a career-worst 2-for-5 on attempts from 50 yards or more, and his 25 FG attempts and 31 PAT attempts were each the second-lowest volume of his career, although missing four games with a knee injury helped account for that decline. The team's offense isn't what it once was, and the days of Butker routinely being among the league leaders in points are likely gone. He'll need to take advantage of his opportunities in Week 1 against a Chargers team that gave up just 6.6 points a game to kickers last year, tied for seventh lowest in the league.
outlooksByWeek.2: Harrison Butker uncharacteristically missed an extra point in Week 1, but he converted all three of his FG attempts, including an impressive 59-yarder right before halftime with Kansas City's kicking unit dashing onto the field incredibly efficiently when the team had no timeouts left. Butker hasn't been among the league leaders in volume in a few years, and last year's 84.0% conversion rate on field goals was the second lowest of his career, but the 30-year-old is still among the more reliable players at his position. He'll need to take advantage of every opportunity he gets in Week 2 against an Eagles squad that gave up just 5.7 points per game to kickers in 2024, the lowest mark in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.3: Harrison Butker missed his first field goal of the year in Week 2, a 58-yard attempt in the first quarter that wound up being costly in an eventual 20-17 loss to the Eagles. The Kansas City kicker also missed an extra point in the team's opener, continuing a trend that has seen him pooch at least one kick in five of the eight games in which he's had attempts since he suffered a knee injury in the middle of the 2024 season. The early struggles of the offense haven't been costing him opportunities as he's logged five FG attempts through two weeks. Butker could be even busier in Week 3 against a Giants team that just coughed up 40 points in an overtime loss to the Cowboys, including four field goals and four extra points by Brandon Aubrey.

outlooksByWeek.1: Chig Okonkwo is expected to get a QB upgrade in 2025, as rookie first overall pick Cam Ward will make his NFL debut under center in Week 1 against the Broncos. Okonkwo appears poised to begin the season atop Tennessee's TE depth chart, though he could be challenged by rookie fourth-round pick Gunnar Helm for that role down the line. After posting between 450 and 528 receiving yards in each of his first three NFL seasons, Okonkwo can't be trusted as a fantasy starter at TE until he demonstrates some meaningful chemistry with Ward, though there were encouraging reports on that front in training camp.
outlooksByWeek.2: Chig Okonkwo finished third on the Titans in targets and receiving yards and second in catches in Week 1, but he did so with just three catches for 19 yards on four targets. Tennessee will need substantial improvement from rookie QB Cam Ward for Okonkwo to be relevant in fantasy, as Ward completed just 12 of 28 passes for 112 yards in Week 1. Okonkwo's best left on the bench in Week 2 against the Rams.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chig Okonkwo is tied for the team lead with seven catches through two weeks and ranks third on the Titans with 54 receiving yards, trailing Calvin Ridley (84) and Elic Ayomanor (69). No other teammate has more than three catches or 29 receiving yards, so Okonkwo's a clear top three option, albeit in what has been the NFL's least effective passing offense so far. Okonkwo's fantasy value would increase if rookie first overall pick Cam Ward starts to improve at QB, but Ward has struggled early on, and that's unlikely to change in a tough Week 3 matchup against the Colts, leaving Okonkwo well outside the starting TE range in most fantasy formats.

player.seasonOutlook: Okonkwo has settled in as a consistent contributor in Tennessee, having finished each of his three seasons in the range of 450 to 528 yards and 5.7 to 6.7 fantasy PPG. The 2022 fourth-round pick has yet to finish a season better than 15th in targets, catches, yards or TDs. Scoring has been a clear issue, as Okonkwo has 10 end zone targets and six TDs in 51 career games. On the plus side, he saw a huge spike in work late last season, producing 199 yards on 23 touches during Weeks 15-17 (his 28 targets ranked first and 43.9 fantasy points second among TEs during the span). There aren't many mouths to feed in Tennessee, so it's possible the 25-year-old can carry that momentum into 2025, but he'll need decent play from rookie QB Cam Ward. Okonkwo is best viewed as a back-end TE2.

outlooksByWeek.1: Daniel Jones will start for the Colts in Week 1 against the Dolphins after beating out Anthony Richardson in Indianapolis' QB competition. Jones has 70 games (69 starts) under his belt with the Giants, with a 70:47 TD:INT and 15 rushing TDs. He's a game manager who will be asked to avoid mistakes and hand off to star RB Jonathan Taylor while occasionally getting the ball to WRs Michael Pittman and Josh Downs, and TE Tyler Warren on short and intermediate passes. Jones' poor deep ball will make it tough for WRs Alec Pierce and Adonai Mitchell to get involved consistently downfield. Facing a Dolphins defense that quietly allowed the fourth-fewest scrimmage yards in 2024, Jones' Week 1 fantasy appeal is limited to superflex and two-QB formats.
outlooksByWeek.2: Daniel Jones delivered a masterful performance in his Colts debut, leading the offense to points on all seven drives while throwing a passing TD and running in two more scores. Building on that strong start won't be easy in Week 2 against the Broncos, who boasted one of the league's stingiest defenses in 2024 and limited rookie first overall pick Cam Ward to 112 passing yards and no TDs in Week 1. Jones benefits from the best offensive line play of his career in Indianapolis and can make plays with his legs while keeping the offense on schedule with short passes, but his limitations pushing the ball downfield remain. Perhaps "Indiana Jones" is truly different from the version that posted an underwhelming 70:47 TD:INT and 15 rushing TDs in 70 games (69 starts) for the Giants over the previous six years, but it will take more than a one-game sample before Jones can be trusted as a starting fantasy option outside of superflex and two-QB formats.
outlooksByWeek.3: Daniel Jones threw for 588 yards and a 2:0 TD:INT while adding 28 rushing yards and three TD with his legs to lead the Colts to a 2-0 start. Indiana Jones' third adventure will be his first road game as a member of the Colts, traveling to Tennessee for his first taste of this AFC South rivalry. Jones' red-hot start makes him a viable Week 3 dart throw in single-QB fantasy formats, especially in deeper leagues, though the Colts will likely ride their defense and Jonathan Taylor-led running game against a Titans team that went 3-14 last season and has been outscored 53-31 while looking overmatched en route to a 0-2 start in 2025. Even if you don't start him Week 3, Jones is worth rostering unless you have an elite QB option.

player.seasonOutlook: Jones signed with the Colts and beat out Anthony Richardson for the team's starting job. The 2019 first-round pick struggled with injuries (zero full seasons) and ineffectiveness (career 6.5 YPA) during six seasons with the Giants. After throwing 24 touchdowns in 13 games as a rookie, Jones totaled 45 pass TDs in 57 games the following five seasons. He finished one season better than 15th in fantasy PPG and that eighth-place finish in 2022 was primarily a product of big-time rushing (120-708-7). The 28-year-old isn't going to move the needle as a passer, but he could land on the streaming radar due to his legs (60-plus carries in four of the last five seasons). Especially considering that early struggles could lead to a benching in favor of Richardson, Jones is, at best, a QB2 only worth drafting in superflex.

outlooksByWeek.1: Elic Ayomanor will make his NFL debut in Week 1 against the sturdy Denver defense. It's hard to pinpoint exactly where Ayomanor stands on Tennessee's WR depth chart. Calvin Ridley's locked in on top, but the ordering is murky between Ayomanor, Tyler Lockett, Van Jefferson and Chimere Dike, none of whom were on the team last season. Lockett and Jefferson are veterans, while Dike was selected earlier than Ayomanor in the fourth round of the 2025 NFL Draft. It may take Ayomanor a few games to separate from the pack, so he's hardly more than a bench stash for Week 1, but he has a chance to eventually emerge as the No. 2 option behind Ridley for rookie QB Cam Ward.
outlooksByWeek.2: Elic Ayomanor ranked second on the Titans with seven Week 1 targets but turned them into just two catches for 13 yards as rookie QB Cam Ward threw for just 112 yards. Ayomanor's usage was encouraging, as the rookie fourth-round pick looks like the No. 2 WR for Tennessee behind Calvin Ridley, but the team's whole passing game is probably best avoided in Week 2 against a Rams defense that held Houston without a TD in Week 1. Ayomanor's worth stashing on the bench in dynasty and keeper formats, and he could even provide some redraft value down the line if Ward improves.
outlooksByWeek.3: Elic Ayomanor caught Tennessee's only touchdown through two games on an ad-lib highlight from Cam Ward, and the pair of rookies have shown intriguing chemistry heading into a Week 3 home game against the Colts. Ayomanor ranks second on the team in both targets (13) and receiving yards (69), trailing only Calvin Ridley in both categories. The rookie fourth-round pick has worked his way into the deep-league flex conversation for Week 3, even against a Colts defense that has allowed only one WR to exceed 40 yards this season. Ayomanor should be rostered in dynasty and keeper leagues, though his redraft appeal remains limited to deeper formats for now.

player.seasonOutlook: Ayomanor was selected by the Titans in the fourth round of April's draft. He sports a solid size/speed combo, though he lacks some short-area burst (as shown by his class-worst 1.58 10-yard split at the combine). That didn't slow him from a huge workload at Stanford, as he handled a 32% target share and 47% air yard share (second highest in this class) last season. His efficiency was mostly below average, but there's potential here. Ayomanor will begin his career competing with Tyler Lockett and Van Jefferson (among others) for work behind Calvin Ridley. Ayomanor is only worth drafting in deep leagues and dynasty.

outlooksByWeek.1: Ja'Marr Chase's start to his career has been exceptional while serving as the Bengals' top pass catcher, but he took a leap forward in 2024 by posting 127 receptions, 1,708 yards and 17 total touchdowns. While those numbers may not be repeatable, Chase has at least 80 catches and 1,000 yards in all four of his pro seasons. He's tremendously safe heading into a Week 1 matchup the Browns to the begin the 2025 campaign and should be started without question.
outlooksByWeek.2: Ja'Marr Chase had arguably the most disappointing fantasy showing in Week 1, as the entire Cincinnati offense fell flat. However, neither his skill nor role is in doubt heading into a Week 2 matchup against Jacksonville, making him an easy choice to put together a bounce back performance. Chase is a must-start option despite his subpar start to the 2025 season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Ja'Marr Chase rebounded from a subpar Week 1 performance to power the Bengals' offense in a Week 2 win. The absence of Joe Burrow (toe) is a concern, but Chase managed 10 receptions for 128 yards once Jake Browning entered Sunday's game. He draws a tough Week 3 matchup against the Vikings, which will further limit the likelihood of Chase turning in another ceiling performance, but his talent and role in the offense keep him locked in as a solid WR1.

player.seasonOutlook: The reigning No. 1 fantasy receiver, Chase outscored second-place Justin Jefferson by a massive 85.5 points. His career year included nine top-10 fantasy weeks (three more than any other receiver), as well as the most routes, targets, receptions, yards, touchdowns and end zone targets (17) in the league. He has finished in the top 12 in fantasy PPG in all four of his NFL seasons, including top 5 in three of them. Chase became the league's highest-paid non-quarterback during the offseason and is a heavily targeted 25-year-old superstar on the league's pass-heaviest offense with an elite QB in Joe Burrow. He should be the first WR off the board and is a strong option with the No. 1 overall pick.

outlooksByWeek.1: Kyren Williams signed a three-year extension with the Rams in early August and is set to lead the team's ground game in Week 1 against the Texans. The fourth-year tailback rushed for a career-best 1,299 yards and 14 touchdowns last season, though his YPC fell a bit to 4.1. Williams should have a stranglehold on RB1 duties with Los Angeles, with Blake Corum slated to back him up. Houston presents a tough Week 1 opponent, as the Texans ranked fourth in the NFL by giving up 3.93 YPC to RBs during the regular season last year.
outlooksByWeek.2: Kyren Williams enjoyed a steady season opener for the Rams and will look to build upon that in Week 2 against Tennessee. Williams carried 18 times for 66 yards and a touchdown in Week 1 versus Houston, but he was quiet through the air with one catch for three yards. Williams was the clear workhorse for the Rams -- backup Blake Corum got just one carry -- and having that role gives Williams a promising weekly floor. The Titans' defense certainly seems exposable after giving up 133 rushing yards to Denver's running backs in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kyren Williams will look to build upon consecutive 66-yard rushing totals to begin the campaign when the Rams faces Philadelphia in Week 3. Williams' 66 yards came on 18 carries in Week 1 and on 17 carries in Week 2, so he's been the epitome of consistency so far. However, he's averaging a modest 3.8 yards per tote and has tallied just 17 yards on three catches, so he's still looking for his first big performance of the year. The Eagles have been just middle-of-the pack against the run early this season, yielding 4.26 yards per carry and two rushing touchdowns to running backs.

player.seasonOutlook: One of fantasy's most productive backs over the last two seasons, Williams has scored 31 touchdowns (tied for most among RBs) and averaged 18.8 fantasy PPG (fourth highest) during the span. Last season, he paced all backs in snaps and carries inside the opponent's 5-yard line (19), while ranking no lower than seventh in carries, rushing yards, touches and TDs. He had an extremely high floor (28th was his worst weekly finish) despite limited work as a receiver (outside the top 25 in receptions and yards for the second straight season). Williams' 610 touches over the last two seasons (third most) is a moderate concern, but he's in his prime at age 25 and well positioned as the Rams' feature back. He should be valued as a fringe RB1.

outlooksByWeek.1: Trey McBride will look to build on his 2024 breakout campaign as the Cardinals face New Orleans in Week 1. McBride ranked second among NFL tight ends last year in both receptions (111) and receiving yards (1,146). but he scored just two touchdowns. Positive regression in that category would boost McBride's stock even higher, though there's also a chance he could see fewer targets if Marvin Harrison makes big strides in his second NFL campaign. The Saints revamped their defense in the offseason, but they represent a good Week 1 matchup having given up 8.51 yards per target, fourth-most in the NFL, to tight ends last season.
outlooksByWeek.2: Trey McBride opened the regular season in fine fashion and will look to continue that when Arizona takes on the Panthers in Week 2. McBride led Cardinals pass catchers with six catches and nine targets in Sunday's win over the Saints while finishing second on the team (behind Marvin Harrison) with 71 receiving yards. McBride's Week 2 opponent, the Panthers, present a vulnerable matchup, as they gave up a 5-65-1 line to TEs in Week 1 against the Jaguars. However, Carolina was absolutely crushed on the ground in that matchup, so Arizona could look to focus more on its rushing attack than on its passing game Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.3: Trey McBride will look to continue his strong start to the campaign for the Cardinals in Week 3 against the 49ers. McBride led Arizona with six catches for 78 yards against Carolina in Week 2 and has tallied 12 receptions for 139 yards through two games, though he's yet to get into the end zone. He's been by far QB Kyler Murray's favorite option with 16 targets in the first two contests of the campaign, with only top WR Marvin Harrison (11 targets) also getting double-digit looks so far. The 49ers present a challenging Week 3 matchup though, as they've given up just seven receptions for 56 yards to tight ends through two weeks.

player.seasonOutlook: Since stepping into a starting role in Week 8 of the 2023 season, McBride has an enormous 28.4% target share (9.0 per game). He averaged 6.8 receptions, 69.3 yards and 15.4 fantasy points per game during the span. He was the poster boy for bad TD luck in 2024, totaling three scores (two receiving) despite finishing second at the position in targets, catches, yards, end zone targets (10) and fantasy points. McBride's TE-high 7.9 expected TD total speaks to his bad luck and, though he also didn't score much in 2023 (three TDs on 108 targets), he's a candidate for a big improvement in the area in 2025. McBride is a strong bet to lead all tight ends in fantasy points.

outlooksByWeek.1: After not getting the contract he wanted in Seattle, DK Metcalf was traded to the Steelers this offseason and was promptly extended. Pittsburgh traded George Pickens away shortly thereafter, leaving Metcalf as Aaron Rodgers' clear top target entering a Week 1 matchup against the Jets. It's reasonable to question the effectiveness of the Steelers' passing game, and Metcalf also failed to top 1,000 receiving yards for only the second time in his six-year career in 2025. Metcalf is still safe for fantasy lineups, but he's more of a low-end WR2 than the high upside pass catcher we've seen in the past.
outlooksByWeek.2: DK Metcalf had a successful Steelers debut, picking up the majority of his 83 yards on two long receptions of 31 and 23 yards -- both of which primarily relied on his ability to pick up yards after the catch. He led the team in both targets and yards, though he only outpaced Jonnu Smith and Calvin Austin by one opportunity. Metcalf has the big-play ability to make a fantasy contribution on limited receptions, though that will also lead to inconsistent results. He's a mediocre WR2 as he squares off against Seattle, his former team, in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: DK Metcalf has been Aaron Rodgers' favorite target in Pittsburgh through two weeks, though leading to mediocre results. Metcalf salvaged Week 2 with a leaping contested catch in the end zone for a two-yard score, but he has only 103 yards on 13 targets through two contests. Metcalf's Week 3 production against New England will be heavily dictated by the availability of CB Christian Gonzalez (hamstring), who would likely shadow Metcalf should he be healthy. Metcalf is a passable WR3, with the upside to be a WR2.

player.seasonOutlook: Metcalf was traded to Pittsburgh after spending his first six NFL seasons in Seattle. Metcalf has proven durable (he's missed three games in his career), but he hasn't quite lived up to lofty expectations. Despite leading the NFL (by 10) with 96 end zone targets since entering the league, Metcalf has finished one season in the top 20 among WRs in fantasy PPG (10th in 2020), though he has finished top 25 in four of his past five seasons. His vertical role has limited his catch total and his scoring has underwhelmed lately, as well (6.3 TDs per season since 2022). With minimal mouths to feed in Pittsburgh, Metcalf is assured of a big target share courtesy of Aaron Rodgers and has the look of a fringe WR2.

outlooksByWeek.1: D'Andre Swift will start at running back for the Bears heading into a Week 1 home game against the Vikings. He boasts familiarity with new head coach Ben Johnson's scheme from their time together in Detroit, though that history isn't entirely positive for Swift. Back in 2022, as the OC during Swift's final season with the Lions, Johnson only saw fit to allot him 99 rush attempts across 14 regular-season games, limiting him to a change-of-pace role. Swift has now operated as a workhorse in back-to-back years, with the Eagles and Bears respectively, and he faces minimal competition for snaps in Chicago's backfield - and with a much-improved O-line and better rushing scheme both working in his favor, he should now dominate touches in a three-down role for Johnson.
outlooksByWeek.2: D'Andre Swift will look for more efficiency after a quiet debut against the Vikings, with the Bears travelling to Detroit in Week 2. He handled 17 carries for just 54 yards and caught three passes (five targets) for 12 yards, working as Chicago's clear lead back but struggling behind an offensive line that generated little push. The matchup tilts slightly more favorably this week, as Josh Jacobs wore down the Lions for 66 yards and a score on 19 carries in Week 1, despite Green Bay's offense often telegraphing the run while nursing a lead. Swift's passing-game usage gives him a safe floor, though it's possible he could lose some work Week 2 if Roschon Johnson (foot) is cleared to retake the field.
outlooksByWeek.3: D'Andre Swift and the Bears host the Cowboys in Week 3, coming off a 52-21 loss to Detroit. Swift's efficiency was a bright spot versus the Lions, as he handled 12 carries for 63 yards and a rushing touchdown, and caught three passes for six yards. Still, with the Lions racking up over 500 yards of offense and seven total touchdowns, Chicago was forced to abandon the run almost entirely in the Week 2 loss. The success Swift found in limited action reinforces reasons for optimism that in a more normal game script, he should be a capable engine on offense for the Bears. Dallas doesn't present an easy challenge up front, but as long as Chicago can remain competitive he'll handle plenty of early-down volume and projects for fair red-zone usage.

player.seasonOutlook: Swift returns as the lead back in Chicago after a solid first season with the team. He appeared in every regular-season game for the first time in his five-year career, finishing 10th in carries and 14th in targets among RBs. Swift was effective as a pass catcher, but his rushing efficiency wasn't great (career-low 3.8 YPC) behind a shaky line and he struggled to find the end zone (six TDs). Incredibly, Swift has now finished between 15th and 21st among RBs in fantasy points in all five NFL seasons. He'll benefit from the arrival of new coach Ben Johnson and a much-improved line in 2025, so the dual-threat, 26-year-old remains squarely on the fringe-RB2 radar.

outlooksByWeek.1: Kyler Murray and the Cardinals will kick off the regular season with a Week 1 clash against New Orleans. Murray will have essentially the same pass-catching corps as last season, including wideouts Marvin Harrison Jr. and Michael Wilson along with dynamic TE Trey McBride. Murray finished with a modest 21:11 TD:INT over 17 games last season, but he boosted his stat line with 572 rushing yards and five rushing TDs. Arizona's Week 1 opponent, the Saints, gave up the sixth-most passing yards in the league last year but enter 2025 with a new-look defense that includes a new DC in Brandon Staley and multiple additions in the secondary, including starters Justin Reid, Isaac Yiadom and Julian Blackmon.
outlooksByWeek.2: Kyler Murray will look to lead the Cardinals to a 2-0 start against Carolina in Week 2. Murray logged a modest 163 passing yards Sunday against the Saints, but he threw two touchdowns and added 38 yards (on seven carries) on the ground to finish with a strong overall ledger. Murray was particularly in sync with top wideout Marvin Harrison and top TE Trey McBride, as the pair of pass catchers combined for an 11-132-1 line. Murray's Week 2 opponent, the Panthers, managed a good game against the pass in Week 1 against Jacksonville, holding Trevor Lawrence to 178 yards with one interception, though they didn't log any sacks.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kyler Murray and the Cardinals are 2-0 heading into a Week 3 matchup against San Francisco. Murray has completed 70 percent of his passes with a 3:1 TD:INT through two weeks, and though he's tallied a modest 383 yards through the air, he's added 70 rushing yards on 14 carries. Murray has leaned heavily so far on star tight end Trey McBride, who has notched 139 receiving yards through two weeks. The 49ers present a tough matchup on paper, having given up just 357 passing yards through two contests, though they have yet to pick off any passes.

player.seasonOutlook: Murray is back for his seventh NFL season, fresh off a 2024 campaign that may have been his best yet. Murray appeared in every regular-season game for the first time since 2020 and delivered as both a passer (top 13 in attempts, completions, yards and TDs) and rusher (top 8 in carries, yards and TDs). Murray finished 12th among QBs in fantasy PPG, which is actually the worst finish of his career. He completed a career-high 69% of his passes despite a bit of an underwhelming showing from Marvin Harrison Jr. It's fair to expect a leap from Harrison in his second season, so, along with the presence of Trey McBride, Murray has the tools he needs for another mid-to-back-end QB1 fantasy campaign.

outlooksByWeek.1: Jerry Jeudy broke out in his first season with the Browns in 2024, and he'll enter 2025 as the top pass catcher once again. Jeudy's outlook also improved when proven, if unspectacular, veteran quarterback Joe Flacco was named the starting quarterback to begin the season. Jeudy should also have the chance to start 2025 strongly thanks to a matchup against the Bengals, whose secondary is likely to be a weakness this season. Quarterback and the projected quality of the Cleveland offense are both negatives, but Jeudy overcame both in 2024 and is a solid WR2 in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.2: Jerry Jeudy narrowly led the Browns in receiving yards in Week 1, though his five catches and 66 yards were disappointing considering that Joe Flacco took to the air 45 times. In particular, Flacco distributed targets relatively evenly between several different pass catchers, leaving Jeudy unable to separate himself with volume in an inefficient offense. A Week 2 matchup against Baltimore isn't likely to help Jeudy's case, given the talent in the unit's secondary. He's still worth considering as a WR3 or FLEX option in the hopes he can command a higher rate of targets, but Jeudy is risky.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jerry Jeudy posted two nearly identical stat lines in the first two weeks of the season, most importantly recording eight targets in each contest. Despite the solid role, Jeudy struggled to post strong fantasy lines due to the Browns' subpar offensive efficiency. That's unlikely to change in a tough Week 3 matchup against the Packers, who have allowed the fifth-fewest fantasy points per game to opposing wide receivers through two games. As a result, Jeudy is relegated to a WR3 or FLEX option.

player.seasonOutlook: Jeudy is entering his sixth NFL season fresh off a career year in which he paced all wide receivers in snaps (1,006) and finished no lower than 12th in routes, targets, catches, yards and fantasy points (23rd in PPG). Jeudy's season may have been even better with improved early-season QB play, as, from Week 8 on (after Deshaun Watson's season-ending injury), Jeudy ranked sixth among WRs in fantasy points. Touchdowns continue to be a limitation for Jeudy, as he scored only four in 2024 and he has never cleared six in a single season. The 26-year-old has finished as a top-25 fantasy WR two of the past three seasons and is the clear No. 1 target in a Browns offense with some QB uncertainty. The output may be inconsistent, but he's well worth considering for your WR3 slot.

For all their talent up front, it was puzzling to see the 2024 Steelers total a middle-of-the-pack 40 sacks. DE T.J. Watt is one of the game's best at pressuring the quarterback, All-Pro DT Cameron Heyward rebounded as a 35-year-old, and DE Alex Highsmith further populates one of the game's deepest defensive fronts. The Steelers' early schedule sure looks good (@NYJ, SEA, @NE in Weeks 1-3), and potential growth in the sacks department buoys probable top-10 seasonal value.

outlooksByWeek.1: Ricky Pearsall heads into Week 1 against Seattle with a prime opportunity to shine in San Francisco's offense. Brandon Aiyuk (ACL) won't play until at least Week 5, and Jauan Jennings isn't certain to suit up due to a calf injury and contract dispute, so Pearsall could be the team's WR1 for the matchup. Even if Jennings does play, Pearsall should have plenty of opportunities in the first week of what many believe could be a breakout campaign for the talented receiver. Seattle's secondary was pretty good last year in holding wideouts to 7.41 yards per target (fourth-fewest in the league), though the unit did give up 19 TDs to WRs, tied for sixth-most.
outlooksByWeek.2: Ricky Pearsall could be San Francisco's clear-cut No. 1 wideout Week 2 versus the Saints if Jauan Jennings (shoulder) doesn't play. As it was, Pearsall shined in the 49ers' Week 1 win against Seattle, tallying 108 yards on four receptions. The absence of George Kittle (hamstring) and possible absence of Jennings could create even more opportunities for Pearsall, though his output could take a hit if QB Brock Purdy, who is questionable with shoulder and toe injuries, is unable to suit up. In Week 2, Pearsall will face a New Orleans defense that gave up a modest 163 yards through the air to the Cardinals in Week 1, though 71 of those went to Arizona's top wideout, Marvin Harrison.
outlooksByWeek.3: Ricky Pearsall has been San Francisco's most consistent receiver so far heading into a Week 3 matchup against Arizona. Pearsall has tallied four catches each of the first two weeks, though he went from 108 receiving yards Week 1 to 56 yards this past Sunday. Still, Pearsall saw almost the same amount of targets (six) with Mac Jones at QB in Week 2 as he did (seven) with Brock Purdy (toe/shoulder) behind center in the season opener, so he figures to remain a central part of the passing game regardless of which of the two QBs starts against the Cardinals. Arizona has given up the fewest yards per target (5.33) to wideouts through two weeks but also has given up the most catches (34) to the position.

player.seasonOutlook: Pearsall is entering his second NFL season positioned well for a breakout after a gunshot wound derailed a chunk of his rookie campaign. After debuting in Week 7, Pearsall had a few strong fantasy outings (17-plus points in three games), but was otherwise a nonfactor (3.6 PPG in the other eight games). The 2024 first-round pick finished strong (8-141-1 and 6-69-1 receiving lines in Weeks 17 and 18, respectively) and now has a much clearer path to consistent work with Deebo Samuel Sr. gone and Brandon Aiyuk (ACL) expected to miss part of the season. There are still plenty of mouths to feed in San Francisco, but Pearsall very well could lead this team in targets. He's well worth a midround flier.

outlooksByWeek.1: Jerome Ford's workload dipped in 2024, splitting carries with Nick Chubb and D'Onta Foreman. The Browns appear to be interested in further cutting his role after drafting both Quinshon Judkins and Dylan Sampson in the 2025 NFL draft, though Ford should have a role in the short-term with Judkins' status unclear. Cleveland will likely give both Ford and Sampson carries in a Week 1 matchup against Cincinnati, though it's unclear how many touches will result. With all teams in action and most starting running backs healthy, there should be better fantasy options.
outlooksByWeek.2: Jerome Ford was expected to have the chance to lead the Browns' backfield to begin the 2025 season, but he quickly ceded work to rookie Dylan Sampson. Sampson out-touched Ford 20-7 in Week 1, making Ford nearly impossible to trust for fantasy purposes in Week 2 against Baltimore. To make matters worse for Ford, Quinshon Judkins could be in the mix to add even more competition for touches.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jerome Ford totaled 11 touches in Week 2 despite the Cleveland backfield expanding to three running backs. Quinshon Judkins worked as the primary rusher, though Ford also mixed in on the ground and recorded five receptions. However, it would be reasonable to project Judkins' role to continue to grow as he ramps up heading into a tough matchup in Week 3 against the Packers. Both role and matchup are likely to work against Ford, which means he's best left on fantasy benches.

player.seasonOutlook: Ford returns for his fourth season in Cleveland with some uncertainty. He played six full games without Nick Chubb last season and was productive, averaging 14.0 touches, 78.0 yards and 14.0 fantasy points. He was also the team's lead back for most of 2023 and finished 16th among RBs in fantasy points (25th in PPG) while piling up 1,132 yards and nine TDs. Ford, who averaged a terrific 5.4 YPC last season, is capable as a rusher and receiver, and, with rookie Quinshon Judkins dealing with an off-field arrest, could the early portion of 2025 as the Browns' lead back. That would make Ford a viable RB2/flex, assuming he can fend off fourth-round rookie Dylan Sampson.

outlooksByWeek.1: Chase McLaughlin looks to stay solid for the Buccaneers in Week 1 against the Falcons. McLaughlin made 30 of 32 field goals last season and made all but two of his 56 extra-point tries. He's missed just four field-goal attempts and two PATs in his two seasons with Tampa Bay. With his squad playing against a shaky Atlanta defense, McLaughlin could get a lot of work in the season opener.
outlooksByWeek.2: Chase McLaughlin will look to be more accurate in Tampa Bay's Week 2 matchup at Houston. McLaughlin went 1-for-2 on field-goal attempts and 2-for-3 on his extra-point tries in Week 1 versus the Falcons. The veteran kicker never once missed both an extra point and a field-goal attempt in the 2024 season, so his accuracy could start to be in question if this continues. Luckily for McLaughlin, he'll take on a Texans defense that outright struggled in their season opener, so he could have plenty of opportunities to bounce back.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chase McLaughlin will look to bounce back as the Buccaneers take on the Jets in Week 3. McLaughlin missed his sole field-goal attempt in Week 2, putting him at 1-for-3 on field goals and 4-for-5 on extra-point tries this year. With a below-average performance in back-to-back weeks, the starting kicker will aim to regain his bearings in a home matchup. Luckily for McLaughlin, New York has given up 11 fantasy points per game to kickers so far this season.

outlooksByWeek.1: Justin Fields could start the year slowly when the Jets face the Steelers in Week 1. His preseason performance left plenty to be desired, and the Pittsburgh defense ranked 10th in points allowed to opposing quarterbacks last season. His rushing potential elevates the floor, and that he played with the Steelers last season could provide a slight edge in reading what they're bringing, but Fields profiles as a fringe option until he shows he can complete balls downfield.
outlooksByWeek.2: Justin Fields will hope for a repeat in pass efficiency when the Jets face the Bills in Week 2. Fields was an impressive 16-of-22 in Week 1 against the Steelers, often times keeping his eyes downfield rather than immediately taking off to run. The rushing keeps his floor very viable for fantasy, as two of his three touchdowns came via his legs. A shootout that both of these teams experienced last week seems unlikely, but Buffalo allowed ample rushing lanes to Lamar Jackson. Fields ability to run while mixing in timely passing lands him in back end QB1 territory in deep leagues.
outlooksByWeek.3: Justin Fields is uncertain to play for the Jets in Week 3 at Tampa Bay due to a concussion. Through two weeks, Fields has shown a very stable rushing floor, but his passing work has been uneven. Should he clear the league's concussion protocol, Fields will bring a volatile profile for fantasy managers against a defense that's allowed the 11th most fantasy points to opposing quarterbacks through two weeks.

player.seasonOutlook: Fields signed with the Jets and is expected to spend 2025 as the team's starter. Fields spent the first six games of 2024 as the Steelers' starter and, while his play wasn't good enough to avoid a benching in favor of Russell Wilson, the fantasy results were solid; he averaged 18.9 fantasy PPG during his six starts, which would've ranked eighth over the full season. He threw for only 1,106 yards and five TDs, but made up ground as a rusher, ranking top 5 among QBs in carries, rush yards and rush TDs (QB-best five) during Weeks 1-6. This was after he finished his first three NFL seasons top 5 at the position in rushing yards despite missing games each season. Fields' dual-threat ability and a solid group of targets in Garrett Wilson and Breece Hall will be enough to keep him in the weekly QB1 mix.

outlooksByWeek.1: Xavier Legette and the Panthers will take on the Jaguars in Week 1. Legette registered low totals in his rookie season with Carolina, but he did have to play with a volatile quarterback room. With Bryce Young now somewhat established under center, the situation could be steadier for Legette to see some improvement in his second season. Legette will also face a team that was shakier against wide receivers in 2024, which could be even better for his season-opener output.
outlooksByWeek.2: Xavier Legette faces an uphill battle for meaningful production as the Panthers travel to Arizona for Week 2. Legette saw seven targets in Carolina's season-opening defeat to the Jaguars, but he converted them into just three catches for 10 yards. The second-year receiver could continue to command a solid share of quarterback Bryce Young's attention, but rookie Tetairoa McMillan is the clear top option in the Carolina passing game. Legette will match up against a Cardinals defense that gave up 17 grabs for 126 yards to New Orleans wide receivers in Week 1, but the fact that the Cardiac Cats have such an untested offense makes Legette's chances for a breakout game very unlikely.
outlooksByWeek.3: Xavier Legette will aim to bounce back in Week 3 as the Panthers take on the Falcons. Legette caught just one of his eight targets for minus-2 yards this past Sunday versus Arizona. This puts the second-year wideout at just four catches for eight yards on the season, even with 90 passes attempted by Bryce Young across the two outings. Legette still is tied for the second-most targets on the team at 15 with Hunter Renfrow, so hopefully these will turn into some more output against an Atlanta squad that ranks middle-of-the-pack against wide receivers.

player.seasonOutlook: Legette is eyeing a second-year leap following a rookie campaign with mixed results. The 2024 first-round pick posted a route participation of at least 59% in 11 games in his first season. He handled a healthy 21% of the targets (6.4 per game) and 30% of the team's air yards, but was limited to 39.3 yards and 9.8 fantasy points per game, reaching 14 points only once. Legette was near the basement of the position in YPR, YPT, YPRR and RAC. Legette is positioned for an every-down role and there are plenty of targets available behind first-round pick Tetairoa McMillan after Adam Thielen was traded to Minnesota. With Legette's pedigree and after Bryce Young's strong finish to 2024, the 24-year-old is well worth a late flier.

outlooksByWeek.1: Tua Tagovailoa opens the 2025 campaign in a favorable matchup Week 1 when the Dolphins travel to face the Colts. Indianapolis allowed the ninth most fantasy points per game to quarterbacks, and the only real notable upgrade from a unit that had the ninth fewest sacks is new defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo. Perhaps a new scheme will cause early confusion, but with his full set of weapons healthy, Tagovailoa looks to be in a place to provide at worst a league-average return Sunday, putting him in back-end QB1 territory.
outlooksByWeek.2: Tua Tagovailoa looks for a bounce back game for the Dolphins in Week 2 against the Patriots. Tagovailoa threw for just 114 yards last week while recording two interceptions and losing a fumble in an offense that produced only eight points and looks disjointed. If there's a light at the end of the tunnel, Tagovailoa had 317 yards and four touchdowns against New England last year, and while it's a new regime, the Patriots allowed 362 passing yards last week to Geno Smith. It's likely a bold call to put Tagovailoa in your starting lineup, but he's got the arsenal and conceivably the matchup to exploit.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tua Tagovailoa should have ample opportunity to provide fantasy points in the Dolphins Week 3 matchup at Buffalo on Thursday night, likely being forced to throw from behind early and often. Miami's offense looked far more capable in their second outing after a dismal opener and with the Bills nearly a two-touchdown favorite and the game having an elevated total near 50 points, there's reasonable expectation of high volume. The Bills secondary has allowed 292 yards passing through two games, and Tagovailoa had a 3:3 TD:INT ratio against them last season so he'll need volume in a challenging road environment to provide a fantasy-worthy return.

player.seasonOutlook: Tagovailoa returns as the starter in Miami. With the Dolphins seeing two-high safeties on a league-high 56% of pass plays, he went super-conservative, posting a league-low 5.7 aDOT and completing a league-best 73% of his passes. He had a midseason stretch of four straight top-10 fantasy outings, but otherwise had one weekly finish better than 17th (eighth in Week 1). During the 11 weeks he was active, Tagovailoa averaged 16.5 fantasy PPG (14th best). He remains a nonfactor with his legs (below 75 yards three straight seasons, with zero rush TDs during the span), which is why he's never finished a season better than 10th in fantasy PPG. A decent supporting cast led by Tyreek Hill, Jaylen Waddle and De'Von Achane keeps Tagovailoa in the weekly streaming mix, but he has a low ceiling due to the limited rushing output.

outlooksByWeek.1: Zach Ertz reprises his role as the safety blanket for quarterback Jayden Daniels and the Washington Commanders in 2025. Ertz resurrected his career last year, snagging 66 passes for 654 yards and seven touchdowns. The touchdown total was his highest since 2018 with the Eagles. The Commanders brought in Deebo Samuel in the offseason, which will likely take away some looks from Ertz, and Ertz will turn 35 years of age in November. In Week 1, Ertz will also face a Giants defense that allowed just 227.6 passing yards per tilt in 2024, which was 10th in the league. Likewise, the Giants added Jevon Holland and Paulson Adebo to the secondary, so the unit may be even better this season.
outlooksByWeek.2: Zach Ertz once again proved an efficient safety valve and red zone target for quarterback Jayden Daniels. Ertz snagged three passes for 26 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 21-6 win over the Giants. Ertz had five targets for the game. Ertz looked rejuvenated with Daniels a season ago, scoring seven times and gaining 654 yards, his best total in five years. A new season resulted in the same stellar rapport, at least in Week 1. The task gets far more difficult in Week 2, though. The Commanders will face a Packers defense that allowed just 200 passing yards in a dominant Week 1 win of their own over the Detroit Lions.
outlooksByWeek.3: Zach Ertz has 13 targets and two touchdowns through two games for the Commanders, but in Week 3 he could be playing without his starting quarterback. Jayden Daniels is nursing a knee sprain, leaving his status in question for a clash with the Raiders. The only saving grace for Ertz, even if backup Marcus Mariota is lining up under center, is that Las Vegas has been suspect against the pass thus far in 2025. The Raiders are giving up 256 passing yards per tilt, which is 27th in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Ertz returns to Washington for his 13th NFL season after a very successful debut campaign with the team. One season after being waived by Arizona and failing to find his way to another 53-man roster, Ertz won the Commanders' starting TE gig and ended up in the top 12 at the position in routes, targets, catches, yards, TDs and fantasy points. His 10 end zone targets ranked second at the position. Ertz is now 34 years old and has added competition for targets with Deebo Samuel Sr. in town and Ben Sinnott entering Year 2, so a step back in production is probable, but he'll continue to benefit from playing a role in a Jayden Daniels-led offense. Ertz is best viewed as a low-ceiling TE2.

outlooksByWeek.1: DeMario Douglas looks set to play a possession receiver role for the Patriots entering Week 1 against the Raiders. Douglas provided 66 catches last year but failed to top 10.0 yards per reception, suggesting volume is his game rather than any big play potential. His opening week appeal is heavily tied to the availability of Stefon Diggs (knee), who if active, will garner a plethora of attention from Drake Maye.
outlooksByWeek.2: DeMario Douglas will look to be more than an afterthought in the Patriots passing game in Week 2 at Miami. He logged an encouraging seven targets in Week 1, but somehow managed negative-two yards on two catches. Kayshon Boutte is emerging as a viable top option for the Patriots, and Stefon Diggs should only get better as he builds chemistry with Drake Maye. New England is also unlikely to throw 46 passes again as they did in Week 1, keeping Douglas out of the fantasy picture.
outlooksByWeek.3: DeMario Douglas hopes to be a factor for the Patriots in Week 3 against the Steelers. After a 65% snap share in Week 1, Douglas garnered a meager 24% share in Week 2, playing just 13 snaps. His body of work is not fantasy friendly, just three catches for six yards.
