New England uses their running backs for dump offs over slot receivers, so it would be a huge leap of faith to trust Douglas in fantasy lineups.

player.seasonOutlook: Douglas is entering his third NFL season having paced the Patriots' WR room in targets during each of his first two years with the team. The 2023 sixth-round pick earned a significant offensive role early in his rookie season and took a slight leap forward last season, hitting career-best marks in targets, catches, yardage and TDs. One of the league's smallest receivers at 5-foot-8, 179 pounds, Douglas primarily works as a short-area slot receiver, which has severely limited his yardage, TDs and, of course, fantasy output. The 24-year-old has yet to deliver a top-55 fantasy campaign (PPG) and is a candidate for a lesser role in 2025 with Stefon Diggs now in the mix on what is likely to be a run-first offense under Mike Vrabel. Douglas has slight late-round appeal in PPR.

outlooksByWeek.1: Saquon Barkley is coming off one of the best seasons in NFL history for a running back, and the matchup of the Eagles versus the Dallas Cowboys in Week 1 of the 2025 campaign should have Saquon licking his chops.  The Cowboys allowed 137.1 yards per tilt on the ground in 2024, which was 29th in the league.  Barkley rushed for 167 yards in one of the two clashes with Dallas last season.  The Cowboys traded Micah Parsons and gained back run-stuffer Kenny Clark in the deal, though giving up one of the most dynamic players in the game today is unlikely to help the Dallas defense in the short term.
outlooksByWeek.2: Saquon Barkley was fairly quiet by his standards in the season opener for the Eagles. Barkley rushed 18 times for 60 yards and a touchdown, while also catching four passes for 24 yards out of the backfield. Barkley had just three games all of last season in which he failed to gain at least 100 yards from scrimmage. Saquon will look to get back on track in Week 2 in a Super Bowl rematch against Kansas City. The AFC powerhouse allowed just 90 rushing yards in its season opener, though was torched through the air by Justin Herbert of the Chargers. As a result, Barkley's involvement in the passing game may be more fruitful than his forays on the ground. Barkley caught six passes for 40 yards in last year's Super Bowl, while only averaging 2.3 yards per rush out of the backfield.
outlooksByWeek.3: Saquon Barkley has found the end zone in each of the first two games for the Philadelphia Eagles. Barkley rushed 18 times for 60 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's triumph over Kansas City. However, Barkley may have a more difficult time finding the promised land in Week 3 versus the Rams. Los Angeles has yet to allow a rushing touchdown this season. However, the Rams have only been mediocre in stopping the run overall, surrendering 111.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is tied for 18th in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Barkley's first season with the Eagles started with a three-touchdown debut and never lost steam en route to a Super Bowl LIX victory and NFL Offensive Player of the Year honors. Despite resting at times (including all of Week 18), Barkley led the NFL in carries, touches and scrimmage yards, which led to a position-best 22.2 fantasy PPG. Barkley, who averaged a career-best 5.8 YPC, does carry some risk, though, as he enters his age-28 campaign off a season with an absurd 482 touches (including the playoffs). He'll need to sustain his elite rushing output, as he isn't a big factor in the passing game (outside the top 25 in targets, catches and yards). He nonetheless remains in a great spot behind the Eagles' terrific offensive line and should be off the board in the first round of fantasy drafts.

outlooksByWeek.1: Chase Brown emerged as a workhorse back for the Bengals across the second half of the 2024 season and looks to be in line to repeat that role in 2025. He recorded at least 20 carries in half of Cincinnati's last eight games while registering at least three receptions in every game in that span. It's possible that Samaje Perine mixes in on third down and in hurry-up situations, but it's clear that Brown will lead the rushing attack heading into a Week 1 matchup against the Browns. He's a reliable RB1 thanks to being attached to one of the most explosive offenses in the league.
outlooksByWeek.2: Chase Brown had a mixed Week 1 performance against Cleveland. He averaged a very poor 2.0 yards per attempt, but he was the only Bengals running back to log a carry. Heading into a Week 2 matchup against Jacksonville, very few backs around the league project for volume similar to Brown, making him a must-start option. The entire Cincinnati offense was sluggish in the season opener, so Brown should also rebound in efficiency.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chase Brown has been among the biggest fantasy disappointments through two games, totaling only 116 yards from scrimmage on 41 touches. Despite that inefficiency, he continues to dominate opportunity out of the Cincinnati backfield, which should give him the chance to get on track in Week 3 against Minnesota. The Vikings have had mixed performances against the run this season, but Brown's locked-in volume should keep him in fantasy lineups. His outlook has been downgraded due to his lack of efficiency and the absence of Joe Burrow (toe), but Brown remains a decent RB2.

player.seasonOutlook: A fifth-round flier back in 2023, it's no surprise Brown was a committee back to begin his career. That changed when Zack Moss went down for the season in Week 8 last season. From Week 9 on (eight games), Brown played 88% of the Bengals' snaps, averaging 18.9 carries, 5.5 targets, 23.6 touches, 116.3 yards and 20.6 fantasy points per game (fourth highest). He ended up seventh or better among RBs in routes, targets and catches on the season. The 25-year-old is in a good spot as the top receiving back in a pass-heavy, high-scoring Bengals' offense, and he has minimal competition for touches with Samaje Perine and Tahj Brooks next up on the depth chart. Brown is safest as a good RB2, but there's upside for more.

outlooksByWeek.1: Tee Higgins' long-term future in Cincinnati seemed to be in doubt following the 2024 season, but he agreed to a four-year contract in March to remain with the team. His role behind Ja'Marr Chase is a mixed bag, as he'll never garner the same volume of targets as Chase and thus won't be as consistent. However, he draws less attention from opposing defenses, allowing Higgins to post multiple 100 receiving-yard performances in every season as a pro, while also scoring at least six times in all but one of his five campaigns. Higgins is a solid WR2 heading into a Week 1 matchup against Cleveland.
outlooksByWeek.2: Tee Higgins led the Cincinnati offense in receiving yards in Week 1, but he still mustered only 33 yards. The entire offense fell flat, but that should change in Week 2 against Jacksonville in a potentially high-scoring matchup. Higgins is likely to be out targeted by Ja'Marr Chase, but he should still have plenty of opportunity to put up fantasy points, particularly in the red zone. Higgins is a solid WR2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tee Higgins saw improved production in Week 2, thanks in large part to a 42-yard touchdown grab late in the third quarter. Despite the positive performance, there should be concerns about Jake Browning taking over as the leader of the Bengals' offense. Higgins caught only one of his five targets from Browning, while Browning also prioritized getting the ball to Ja'Marr Chase. Higgins is a decent WR2 heading into a Week 3 matchup against the Vikings, but he likely carries more significant risk than other pass catchers ranked in the same range.

player.seasonOutlook: Higgins signed an extension with the Bengals during the offseason and will return as Ja'Marr Chase's running mate. Higgins has struggled with injuries (he's missed action in four straight seasons), but he's been very impactful when healthy. In 12 games last season, Higgins posted career-high marks in TDs (10) and fantasy PPG (18.5), both of which ranked top 6 at the position. Higgins was a top-20 fantasy scorer in seven of his 12 active weeks. The 26-year-old may be the clear No. 2 behind Chase, but he also benefits from the league's pass-heaviest offense with an elite QB in Joe Burrow. Higgins is a good WR2 target.

outlooksByWeek.1: Davante Adams will kick off his 13th NFL season in a new uniform, as he'll feature with the Rams against Houston in Week 1. Adams has seen a drop in production over the past two years, but a late-career bounce-back could be in the works with Matthew Stafford now throwing balls to him. Puka Nacua remains the Rams' WR1, but Stafford has shown an ability to feed two top wideouts in the past when Cooper Kupp was on the club. The Texans gave up 21 receiving TDs to wideouts last year, second-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.2: Davante Adams will look to further establish chemistry with Rams QB Matthew Stafford in a Week 2 matchup against the Titans. Adams had a decent regular-season debut with Los Angeles, gathering four of eight targets for 51 receiving yards. However, it was clear that Puka Nacua remains Stafford's favorite target, as the pair connected for a 10-130-0 line on 11 targets. Nacua's target dominance could keep Adams' ceiling mildly limited, though Stafford has shown the ability to feed multiple wideouts when Nacua and Cooper Kupp were paired together in recent campaigns. The Titans were much better against the pass than the run in Week 1, giving up 151 yards on the ground to 176 through the air, so the Rams could look to expose that vulnerability in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Davante Adams had his first big game as a member of the Rams in Week 2, and he'll look to build upon that performance in a big NFC matchup against the Eagles in Week 3. After logging a modest four receptions for 51 yards in the season opener, Adams went off for 106 receiving yards and one touchdown on six catches against the Titans. Adams received 13 targets in the latter game, out-pacing fellow wideout Puka Nacua, who was productive on nine targets. It seems clear through two weeks that both Adams and Nacua can thrive with Matthew Stafford throwing them the ball, and in Week 3 they'll face an Eagles defense that has been middle-of-the-pack against wideouts by giving up a 62.9 percent catch rate and 7.80 yards per target through two weeks.

player.seasonOutlook: Adams signed with the Rams and figures to operate as the team's de facto Cooper Kupp replacement opposite Puka Nacua. Adams' age (32) is an obvious red flag, but he didn't show signs of slowing down last season. Despite missing three games and being traded, Adams delivered five top-10 fantasy weeks, which tied for fourth among WRs. Adams has now finished top 15 in fantasy PPG each of the past 10 seasons and, while he won't be the No. 1 target in Los Angeles, there are more than enough targets to go around in Sean McVay's scheme with Matthew Stafford under center (the Rams have led the NFL in WR targets each of the last two seasons). He's no longer an elite fantasy option, but Adams is a fine WR2 target with back-end WR1 upside.

outlooksByWeek.1: Sam LaPorta will kick off Year 3 on the road against Green Bay as the Lions look to get out to a strong start Week 1. While the 2023 third-round pick couldn't exactly match his outstanding rookie season in 2024, dipping from an 86-889-19 receiving line to one of 60-726-7, it's possible new OC John Morton deploys him as a clearer priority in the receiving game this season. Rather than talent, LaPorta's biggest hurdle to top-tier production is simply the presence of all of Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams and RB Jahmyr Gibbs as elite target earners.
outlooksByWeek.2: Sam LaPorta will look to keep up his momentum as the Lions host the Bears in Week 2. The starting tight end caught six of nine targets for 79 yards in Detroit's loss to Green Bay in Week 1, reinforcing his role as one of Jared Goff's primary security blankets in the intermediate and short-areas of the field. That RB Jahmry Gibbs drew 10 targets speaks to how effectively the Packers eliminated downfield looks for Goff, and while Chicago's defense will be unlikely to find similar success taking away Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams, the Bears have historically struggled to cover tight ends over the middle of the field. Chicago allowed the third-most yards per target to tight ends last season (8.57), making LaPorta a candidate to find success again in Week 2, while retaining high touchdown upside.
outlooksByWeek.3: Sam LaPorta will work to get more involved as the Lions prepare for a tough Week 3 test on the road against Baltimore. The tight end was disappointingly limited to three grabs for 26 yards on four targets despite Detroit dropping over 500 yards of offense and seven touchdowns on the Bears in Week 2, though in Week 1 he impressed with a 6-79-0 receiving line on nine targets, dissuading any reasons for panic. LaPorta remains a reliable intermediate target for Jared Goff, but when the Lions aren't required to sustain longer drives and can instead focus on explosive playmaking, he'll likely continue taking a clear backseat to offensive weapons like Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams and Jahmyr Gibbs. Baltimore presents a stiff matchup with athletic linebackers and safeties who excel in coverage, but LaPorta's route running and red-zone usage give him legitimate upside.

player.seasonOutlook: After pacing all tight ends in fantasy points as a rookie in 2023, LaPorta fell to eighth in 2024. His receiving line dipped across the board (from 86-889-10 on 121 targets to 60-726-7 on 84 targets), though it's notable he got back on track to some extent after a slow start. After averaging 2.8 targets (11% team share) and 7.1 fantasy points during his first six games, LaPorta leapt to 6.7 targets (21% share) and 13.6 fantasy points in his final 11 (including the playoffs). Those numbers are nearly identical to his rookie season and closer to what we should expect moving forward. Working in Detroit's elite offense, LaPorta is a solid TE1.

outlooksByWeek.1: Justin Herbert's production took a small step back last season as the Chargers transitioned to Jim Harbaugh's run-heavy offense. The 27-year-old quarterback passed for only 3,870 yards, the first time he'd failed to reach 4,000 during a year in which he didn't miss a game, and his 23 passing touchdowns was also short of his prior performances over a 17-game season. Ladd McConkey emerged as his top target, and maybe only reliable one, but the team did bring back Keenan Allen to try and provide a higher floor for the passing game, and first-round pick Omarion Hampton should also contribute as a receiver out of the backfield. Herbert and the Chargers travel to Sao Paulo in Week 1 to take on a Kansas City defense that ranked in the middle of the pack last year against the pass, including an 18th-place showing in passing yards allowed.
outlooksByWeek.2: Justin Herbert dazzled in the Chargers' season opener, tossing 318 yards and three touchdowns in a win over Kansas City. The 27-year-old quarterback hasn't topped 4,000 passing yards since 2022, and his volume was significantly reduced last year with Jim Harbaugh and Greg Roman in charge of the offense, but Herbert's Week 1 performance offers some hope the reins will be loosened on the passing game this time around. He was also aided by the return of Keenan Allen, giving him three downfield threats to choose from along with Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston. Herbert will look to rack up big numbers again in Week 2 against a Raiders defense that just gave up 287 passing yards to the Patriots' Drake Maye, and which allowed 29 passing TDs in 2024, tied for 26th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.3: Justin Herbert was productive and efficient once again in a Week 2 win over the Raiders. In both of the Chargers' 2025 contests, the quarterback has completed better than 70% of his passes with a yards per attempt of 9.0 or higher and multiple touchdown passes, a big factor in the team's 2-0 start. Herbert has also regained his mobility after an injury-plagued 2024, running for more than 30 yards in each game and using his legs to extend plays. He'll take on a Broncos defense in Week 3 that had no trouble containing rookie Cam Ward in its season opener, but which gave up 316 passing yards to the Colts' Daniel Jones in Week 2.

player.seasonOutlook: Herbert is entering his sixth NFL season following a solid but unspectacular fantasy campaign in 2024. Playing in Jim Harbaugh's and Greg Roman's slow-paced, balanced offense (as opposed to pass-heavy schemes of prior years), Herbert finished no better than ninth among QBs in pass attempts, pass yards, pass TDs, carries and rush yards. Herbert has now finished just outside the top 10 in fantasy PPG three seasons in a row, though he did improve in the second half of last season (24th during Weeks 1-7, but 10th in Weeks 8-18). Herbert's skill level, solid supporting cast and moderate rushing contributions are just enough to keep him in the fringe QB1 mix, but his ceiling is lower than in years past.

outlooksByWeek.1: Jaylen Warren has been an effective change-of-pace back for the Steelers in his three seasons as a pro, but he'll have the chance to expand his role after the departure of Najee Harris. Warren's volume could decrease as the season wears on and Kaleb Johnson becomes more involved in the offense, but Warren should be the lead back in a Week 1 matchup against the Jets. Still, he's never topped 15 carries in a game, so don't expect Warren to emerge as a workhorse. Warren should be considered a low-end RB2 or solid FLEX.
outlooksByWeek.2: Jaylen Warren led the Pittsburgh backfield in Week 1, but Kenneth Gainwell had a surprisingly large role in the rushing game. As a result, Warren was limited to 11 mostly ineffective carries, though he flashed pass-catching ability with a five-yard touchdown reception. Gainwell was also ineffective with his touches, so Warren is likely to maintain, and perhaps even improve, his volume in Week 2 against Seattle. Pittsburgh's inability to muster much on the ground remains a concern, but Warren is a reasonable RB2 or FLEX option.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jaylen Warren hasn't taken on a traditional lead-back role in Pittsburgh, but he's been effective. He caught a touchdown in Week 1 and then followed up with 86 yards as a receiver in Week 2. Warren heads into a Week 3 matchup against the Patriots, who just allowed De'Von Achane to tally 92 yards as a pass catcher. Warren should remain involved in all facets of the game and is a decent RB2 or very strong FLEX option.

player.seasonOutlook: Warren is entering his fourth NFL season in position for a larger role following the offseason departure of Najee Harris. Warren has thus far been limited to a situational role (11.3 touches per game since the start of 2023), though it hasn't helped that Harris hasn't missed a single game since Warren entered the league. Warren is primarily a passing-game specialist (his 99 receptions ranks seventh among RBs over the past two seasons) but, while he hasn't cleared 149 carries or four TDs in a season, he has run well (4.8 YPC, 2.0 YAC). Rookie Kaleb Johnson may eventually work his way into a significant role as a rusher, but Warren will be the main main the meantime. He's in the RB2 mix.

Fantasy football's best-scoring defense last season, the Broncos took a stout overall unit, led by Defensive Player of the Year CB Pat Surtain II and All-Pro pass rusher DT Zach Allen, and bolstered it with S Talanoa Hufanga, LB Dre Greenlaw and first-round CB Jahdae Barron. Few NFL defenses are as talented and have as favorable a schedule in Weeks 1 and 2 (TEN, @IND) as the Broncos, making them the rare D/ST unit worth paying up for and sticking with for the duration.

outlooksByWeek.1: Stefon Diggs' availability for the Patriots in Week 1 against the Raiders has been murky. He didn't appear in a preseason game after undergoing ACL surgery last October, and while reports are he's healthy and ahead of schedule in his rehab, there's been no clear-cut evidence. Assuming he's active, he'll be the clear top option for emerging QB Drake Maye and can be started in all formats, as volume seems highly probable.
outlooksByWeek.2: Stefon Diggs hopes to build on a steady opener when the Patriots travel to Miami in Week 2. After not playing the entire preseason, Diggs caught six of seven targets for 57 yards against the Raiders in Week 1. That's steady volume and minimal yards per target, setting Diggs up for solid yet unspectacular production against a defense that allowed a nearly similar 9.4 yards per target in Week 1. Diggs offers stable numbers, helping round out a lineup as he continues to gain chemistry with his second-year quarterback.
outlooksByWeek.3: Stefon Diggs will look to keep building reps for the Patriots in Week 3 against the Steelers. Diggs enjoyed a slight snap share uptick last week, being on the field for 51% of the plays as he works towards full health following ACL surgery last year. It's been a steady yet unspectacular start, averaging a mere 8.9 yards per reception, but further removed from injury, Diggs can only improve. He's a terrific WR3/Flex target that should elevate in the coming weeks.

player.seasonOutlook: Diggs signed with the Patriots after spending the first 10 seasons of his career with the Vikings, Bills and Texans. Diggs' 2024 stint with Houston started well (he had six-plus targets in all eight games and averaged 15.2 fantasy PPG), but ended with a torn ACL in Week 8. He has finished in the top 25 in fantasy PPG nine years in a row (17th or better in eight of them) and, at least in terms of target competition, has a clear path to a gigantic target share in a Patriots' offense led by impressive second-year QB Drake Maye. Of course, Diggs is now 31 years old and it's unclear if he'll be his usual self following the knee injury. A healthy Diggs could rise as high as the WR2 mix, but the uncertainty makes him a logical midround target.

outlooksByWeek.1: Brock Purdy and the 49ers head to Seattle in Week 1 to face a Seahawks defense that surrendered the 12th-most passing yards last year. Fresh off a massive contract extension he signed in the offseason, Purdy will have a different group of pass-catchers than a year ago, as Deebo Samuel is in Washington, Brandon Aiyuk (ACL) won't play until at least Week 5, and Jauan Jennings (calf) is questionable. However, Purdy still has plenty of weapons at his disposal, include one of the league's most productive tight ends in George Kittle, promising second-year wideout Ricky Pearsall, and verstaile RB Christian McCaffrey. Purdy will look to push the ball downfield against a Seattle secondary that remains largely unchanged from last season, when it gave up a middle-of-the-pack 90.9 QB rating.
outlooksByWeek.2: Brock Purdy will attempt to lead the 49ers to a second win in Week 2 against New Orleans, but his status is iffy due to injuries to his toe and shoulder. Purdy threw two interceptions Week 1 against Seattle, but he also completed 26 of 35 pass attempts for 277 yards and two touchdowns while coming up big when it counted most, leading San Francisco to a game-winning touchdown late in the fourth quarter. In Week 2, Purdy (if healthy) will square off against a Saints defense that held Kyler Murray to 163 passing yards in the regular-season opener, and though Murray did toss two TDs without any interceptions, New Orleans sacked him five times. George Kittle is on IR due to a hamstring injury and Jauan Jennings is questionable with a shoulder issue, while Brandon Aiyuk is on the PUP list while recovering from a knee injury, so Purdy will be dealing with a depleted pass-catching corps if he does play. If Purdy is ultimately unable to suit up, Mac Jones would presumably start under center for San Francisco.
outlooksByWeek.3: Brock Purdy isn't expected to take the field for San Francisco in Week 3 against Arizona despite his toe and shoulder injuries reportedly showing some improvement over the past week. If Purdy is able to surprise by suiting up, he'll face a Cardinals defense that allowed Bryce Young of the Panthers to throw for 328 yards and three touchdowns in Week 2. Purdy would be missing one of his top targets in tight end George Kittle (hamstring), while starting wideout Jauan Jennings is iffy due to an ankle injury. Should Purdy not be able to suit up, as expected, Mac Jones would again start at quarterback for San Francisco.

player.seasonOutlook: The 2024 season was a disappointment for the 49ers, but the good news is that Purdy still played at a high level. The 2022 seventh-round pick finished fifth in QBR and third in YPA after leading the league in both in 2023. Purdy missed two games and saw his passing TDs dip from 30 to 20, but he also took his rushing to a new level with career highs in carries, yards and TDs. By season's end, he was 10th among QBs in fantasy PPG, which was a slight dip from his eighth-place finish in 2023. Purdy has yet to finish a season better than 17th in pass attempts, but that could change in 2025 after several major defensive departures. With Kyle Shanahan calling the shots and a good supporting cast led by George Kittle, Christian McCaffrey and Trent Williams, Purdy is positioned well for another fringe-QB1 fantasy season.

outlooksByWeek.1: Keenan Allen was traded to the Bears last offseason, ending an 11-year stint with the Chargers, but the move didn't do the veteran wideout's production any favors. Over 15 regular-season games he managed a 70-744-7 line, solid numbers but still a significant step back from 2023, and his 6.1 yards per target was a career low. Allen elected to return to the Bolts in free agency, reuniting with quarterback Justin Herbert, but he'll be firmly behind Ladd McConkey in the pecking order for targets and working in Jim Harbaugh's run-heavy scheme, so he's unlikely to recapture his former level of production. In a Week 1 trip to Sao Paulo, Allen will face a Kansas City secondary that ranked sixth in receiving yards allowed to WRs, but tied for 24th in receiving TDs allowed to the position.
outlooksByWeek.2: Keenan Allen made an impressive return to the Chargers, turning a team-high 10 targets into seven catches for 68 yards and a touchdown. Ladd McConkey is still the team's no. 1 WR and Quentin Johnston remains arguably Justin Herbert's favorite option in the end zone, so most of Allen's damage seems likely to come between the 20s. That would limit his ceiling in a Jim Harbaugh/Greg Roman-helmed offense that still figures to prioritize the ground game. Allen will face a familiar foe in Week 2, taking on a Raiders secondary that ranked a respectable 10th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs last season, but which he has a 1,178 career receiving yards against, more than any other team in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.3: Keenan Allen is proving that you can go home again. After a tough 2024 campaign in Chicago, the veteran wideout returned to the Chargers this offseason and through the first two games of 2025 he's caught 12 of his team-leading 17 targets for 129 yards and two touchdowns. His chemistry with Justin Herbert has been immediately rekindled, and while Ladd McConkey remains the team's top receiver, Allen may be more of a 1B option than a clear No. 2. He may have to rely on volume more than scores in Week 3 against a Broncos secondary that has yet to allow a receiving touchdown to a WR this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Allen is back with the Chargers (the team he was with for his first 11 pro seasons) after spending last season in Chicago. During that 2024 campaign, Allen handled a hefty 26.9% target share (7.9 per game), which ranked 11th among receivers, during 15 active weeks. His efficiency took a big hit from his Los Angeles years (most Chicago pass catchers had this issue), but he did find the end zone seven times and has now scored between six and eight TDs in seven of his last eight seasons. Allen is now 33-years-old (ancient for an NFL receiver) and hasn't played a full regular season since 2019. He's no longer a fantasy WR1 (he finished 34th in PPG last season), but he has a real shot to trail only Ladd McConkey in targets in a solid Los Angeles offense. Allen is a fine late-round flier for your bench and has WR3/flex upside.

outlooksByWeek.1: Cedric Tillman enters his third season with the Browns as a potential breakout candidate. His 2024 season was cut short by a concussion, but in four full games following the departure of Amari Cooper, Tillman recorded 24 catches for 302 yards and three touchdowns. He'll enter the season as the third priority for targets behind David Njoku and Jerry Jeudy, a similar situation as 2024. A Week 1 matchup against the Bengals should also benefit Tillman, as Cincinnati is projected to have a weak secondary.
outlooksByWeek.2: Cedric Tillman accounted for the Browns' lone touchdown through the air in Week 1, connecting with Joe Flacco from five yards away. Tillman was otherwise involved in the offense, matching Jerry Jeudy with eight targets. A Week 2 matchup against Baltimore will likely be tough given the Ravens' talent in the secondary, but Tillman's close to the 2024 season, paired with his Week 1 performance, is enough to make him a low-end FLEX option.
outlooksByWeek.3: Cedric Tillman nearly matched Jerry Jeudy in targets through two games, with Tillman accruing 15 to Jeudy's 16. However, the Browns' poor offense has limited Tillman's fantasy appeal, as he's combined to record only 74 total yards paired with two touchdowns. A Week 3 matchup against the Packers isn't likely to help his cause, as Green Bay has allowed only 219 yards and two touchdowns to opposing wide receivers early this season. Tillman is a mediocre FLEX option in Week 3.

player.seasonOutlook: Tillman is entering his third NFL season after what appeared to be a breakout 2024 campaign was derailed by a Week 12 season-ending concussion. The 2023 third-round pick wasn't much of a factor during his first 20 NFL games, but that changed when Amari Cooper was traded prior to Week 7 last season. Over the next four weeks, Tillman would average 9.8 targets (eight-plus in all four) and 18.6 fantasy points (three with 18-plus points). His season ended the following week, but was enough to provide optimism about his future. Cleveland's QB situation is uncertain, but Tillman has a lock on No. 2 duties opposite Jerry Jeudy. Consider the 25-year-old in the late rounds.

outlooksByWeek.1: Rachaad White and the Buccaneers have a Week 1 home matchup against a Falcons defense that excelled against running backs last season. White eventually lost the top running back role to Bucky Irving in the 2024 campaign, and this hierarchy is set to stay in place for 2025. While that is slightly discouraging for the incoming third-year rusher, White does still appeal as a passing-down back that excels in open space. This makes him more of a change-of-pace backfield option behind Irving against Atlanta, but White has shown that he can still provide some value for Tampa Bay given the right situation.
outlooksByWeek.2: Rachaad White is set to be the supplementary option for the Buccaneers in a Week 2 away game versus Houston. White had next-to-no output against the Falcons in Week 1, logging two carries for 14 yards and one catch for two yards. These totals were worse than all but two of his appearances last season, which means he could be slowly getting fazed out of a meaningful role with Tampa Bay. He'll aim to carve out any type of involvement and possibly tap into his receiving upside against a Texans team that gave 68 rushing yards, 17 receiving yards, and one rushing touchdown to Rams running backs in their season opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Rachaad White could continue to eat into Bucky Irving's touches as the Buccaneers play the Jets in Week 3. White scored the game-winning touchdown for Tampa Bay in Week 2 versus the Texans and finished the game with 12 total touches, but he still was outpaced by Irving. White's role doesn't look to be diminishing any time soon, but he is still definitely behind Irving on the totem pole. This backfield share could benefit both of them, though, against a Jets defense that has given up the fourth-most fantasy points to running backs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: White enters his fourth NFL season no longer positioned as Tampa Bay's lead back. The 2022 third-round pick peaked when he finished top 5 among RBs in snaps, touches, carries, routes, catches, yards and fantasy points during a breakout 2023 season, but his pedestrian efficiency led to a reduced role in 2024. White still scored nine TDs and ended up in the top 10 among RBs in targets, catches and receiving yards, but he fell to 23rd in fantasy PPG. One of only two backs with 50-plus receptions in each of the past three seasons (Alvin Kamara is the other), White figures to sustain a pass-catching role in a good offense, but Bucky Irving appears to be the new lead back in Tampa. White is a fine late-round insurance flier.

outlooksByWeek.1: Jake Elliott tied for 11th in the NFL last season in terms of field goal makes, as he connected on 28 three-pointers for the Eagles, whose offense should show no signs of slowing down in 2025.  However, Elliott also missed eight kicks, posting one of the lowest field goal percentages among active starting kickers. Nevertheless, he does not appear to be in any jeopardy of losing his job, and a tasty Week 1 matchup with Dallas should help get his season off on the right foot.  Elliott connected on four field goals and nine extra points in the two clashes with the Cowboys last season, and Dallas just traded its best player, pass rusher Micah Parsons.
outlooksByWeek.2: Jake Elliott connected on a 58-yard field goal in the season opener for the Eagles. This is a notable development for the placekicker, as Elliott did not make a single field goal from over 50 yards during the 2024 regular season. Elliott also booted three extra points in the 24-20 win over the Cowboys. In Week 2, the Eagles clash with Kansas City in a Super Bowl rematch. Kansas City surprisingly allowed 27 points in the season opener, one of the higher opposing scores in Week 1. Likewise, the Eagles put up 40 in the Super Bowl last February, so this could be a sneaky good matchup for Elliott from a kicking standpoint.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jake Elliott appears to have gotten his groove back for the Eagles. In 2024, he missed eight field goals and did not connect on a single one from 50 yards or longer. Through two games in 2025, Elliott has already hit a pair of 58-yarders. He has also hit all five of his extra points on the young season. Unfortunately, points may be difficult to come by in Week 3 versus the Rams, who are allowing just 14 points per contest.

outlooksByWeek.1: Dylan Sampson was a fourth-round pick by the Browns in the 2025 draft and should immediately have a significant role heading into a Week 1 matchup against Cincinnati. For the time being, he will be joined by Jerome Ford in the backfield, and we're likely to see the duo split work relatively evenly in the short term. Sampson is a fine stash due to the uncertainty of Quinshon Judkins' status and Sampson's potential to take over the backfield, but he's best left on fantasy benches in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.2: Dylan Sampson wasted no time establishing himself as the lead back in Cleveland, as he out-touched Jerome Ford 20-7 in Week 1. The majority of Sampson's work came as a receiver, and he was highly inefficient as a rusher by averaging only 2.4 yards per carry. He'll face two primary challenges in Week 2, the first of which is a matchup with a Ravens defense that is projected to be among the better in the league despite getting exploited by the Bills in Week 1. Furthermore, Quinshon Judkins has the chance to be active, which would almost certainly cut into Sampson's volume. There are worse FLEX options, but he's ideally a player to stash on the bench until there's a better idea of how the Browns will allocate touches in the backfield.
outlooksByWeek.3: Dylan Sampson was heavily affected by the introduction of Quinshon Judkins into the Cleveland offense, as his total touches fell from 20 in Week 1 to seven in Week 2. He salvaged his day with an eight-yard touchdown reception late in a blowout loss to the Ravens, but that shouldn't fool fantasy managers into viewing him as a reliable fantasy option heading into a tough Week 3 matchup against the Packers. Sampson is fine as a bench stash, but he should not be slotted into fantasy lineups.

player.seasonOutlook: Sampson was selected by Cleveland in the fourth round of April's draft. He is one of the smallest and youngest RBs (20) in this class. He was an effective collegiate rusher (5.9 YPC), but wasn't used much in the pass game (1.5 targets per game). He's tough and makes plays, but his size could limit his touch ceiling. Sampson's fantasy outlook is less than ideal, as second-round rookie Quinshon Judkins is the team's short- and long-term lead back, with Jerome Ford possibly a factor in 2025 as well. Sampson is barely worth late-round consideration, but is a fine dynasty hold.

outlooksByWeek.1: Cade Otton is questionable for the Buccaneers heading into Week 1 against the Falcons. Otton has been battling a leg injury this offseason, but he should be good for Tampa Bay's season opener. The third-year tight end finished the 2024 season with career highs in most categories. He logged 59 catches for 600 yards and four touchdowns, proving to be an extremely reliable option for quarterback Baker Mayfield. Otton should provide some stability while the team breaks in rookie wideouts Emeka Egbuka and Tez Johnson.
outlooksByWeek.2: Cade Otton will look to register his first catch of the season as the Buccaneers take on Houston in Week 2. Otton failed to convert any of his three targets into catches against the Falcons in the Bucs' season opener, with Tampa Bay's wide receivers stealing the show in the close win. The starting tight end finished just one of his 15 games last season with zero catches, so his slow start could be turned around quickly. Otton will take on a Texans defense that gave up three catches for seven yards and a touchdown to Rams tight ends in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Cade Otton will look to expand on a bounce-back performance on MNF as the Buccaneers take on the Jets at home in Week 3. Otton failed to bring in a catch in Week 1, but he snagged three for 25 yards in Week 2. The starting tight end has been on the back burner for targets behind wide receivers Mike Evans, Emeka Egbuka, Sterling Shepard and running back Bucky Irving so far this season. Otton will need to start showing that he can command looks from quarterback Baker Mayfield moving forward if he hopes to escape a depth role. The fourth year will have the capacity to do so against a New York defense that's given up the ninth-most points to tight ends so far this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Following two solid but unspectacular seasons to begin his NFL career, Otton made a big leap in 2024, finishing in the top 15 among TEs in snaps, routes, targets, receptions, yards, TDs and fantasy points. Injuries around him were a factor, however, as he handled a solid 16% target share (4.8 per game) but was limited to a 29-307-1 receiving line (6.3 fantasy PPG and no games over 11.2) in 10 games with Mike Evans also in the lineup. Then, during Weeks 7-10 with Evans injured (Chris Godwin also missed most of this action), Otton handled a 25% target share (9.5 per game, 8-plus in all four) and posted a 30-293-3 receiving line (19.3 PPG with 18-plus three times). With Tampa Bay's loaded WR room and heavy reliance on its RBs, Otton figures to head back to low-ceiling TE2 production.

outlooksByWeek.1: Bijan Robinson will be the centerpiece of the Falcons' offense against the Buccaneers in Week 1. Last year, Robinson recorded 1,456 rushing yards and 14 touchdowns on 304 carries, along with 61 receptions for 431 receiving yards and one touchdown. Those numbers show that he was a force in the run and pass game in 2024, even in a shaky Atlanta offense, so a more stable squad led by Michael Penix could boost Robinson's production further. While Tampa Bay has proven to be a tough defense even against the best running backs in the NFL, Robinson should still have no trouble being the same star as last season, especially as a dual threat.
outlooksByWeek.2: Bijan Robinson will look to take a bigger command of the run game as the Falcons take on the Vikings in Week 2. Robinson still finished out Week 1 against the Bucs with an impressive stat line, as he grabbed six of seven targets for 100 yards and a touchdown, but he was shut down on the ground with just 12 rushes for 24 yards. The third-year star should continue to command the bulk of running-back reps ahead of Tyler Allgeier, and he'll look to do so against a Minnesota front that gave up 53 rushing yards to D'Andre Swift and 58 rushing yards to Caleb Williams. Robinson will definitely register more rushing attempts than quarterback Michael Penix. This gives the RB1 all the tools he needs for a dominant game, both on the ground and in the receiving game.
outlooksByWeek.3: Bijan Robinson should get a huge workload once again as Atlanta travels to Carolina in Week 3. Robinson's Week 1 performance was lacking in dominance on the ground, so he delivered this past Sunday with 143 rushing yards off 22 attempts. The third-year star has now topped 100 yards from scrimmage in back-to-back weeks, with each game being done so fully in one category. If he's able to combine his rushing and receiving skills moving forward, he could become an even bigger threat for opposing defenses. The Panthers have also ranked middle-of-the-pack against running backs so far this season, so the possibility of an all-out commanding performance is definitely in reach.

player.seasonOutlook: It took a minute, but Robinson finally made the leap to fantasy stardom last season. After a slow start, the 2023 first-round pick averaged 23.3 touches, 120.9 yards and 22.8 fantasy points (first at RB) from Week 6 on. He scored 14 TDs and had at least 18 touches in all but one game (a blowout) during the span. Robinson finished top 5 among RBs in snaps, carries, routes, targets, touches, yards and fantasy points. Entering his age-23 campaign and working in an Atlanta offense that was the third-run-heaviest in the league last season, Robinson is primed for another elite season and should be under consideration with the first overall pick of your draft.

outlooksByWeek.1: Brock Bowers battled through a chaotic offensive environment, catching passes from three different quarterbacks last year to put together a historic rookie campaign, posting a massive 112-1,194-5 line over 17 regular-season games for the Raiders. The 2024 first-round pick still has room to grow when it comes to his skill set and knowledge of how to handle NFL defenses, but in terms of raw receiving numbers, he may have already hit his ceiling in Las Vegas. The team brought in Pete Carroll as head coach and Chip Kelly as offensive coordinator, which will likely result in a very run-heavy offense with 2025 first-round pick Ashton Jeanty as its centerpiece. Bowers should still be the top option for new starting QB Geno Smith and a Week 1 matchup against a Patriots defense that finished 2024 in the middle of the pack in production allowed to TEs shouldn't present a big obstacle.
outlooksByWeek.2: Brock Bowers picked up where he left off in 2024 to begin his rookie season, hauling in five of eight targets for a team-high 103 yards in Week 1. The stud tight end showed immediate chemistry with new Raiders quarterback Geno Smith, with Bowers' longest gain going for 38 yards and his 10.1 aDOT being a significant jump up from his dazzling rookie season. A second-half knee injury caused him to leave the game early, but the team has downplayed the issue. Assuming Bowers suits up in Week 2, he'll take on a Chargers defense that ranked 20th in receptions allowed to TEs last season, but which gave up a league-low two receiving TDs to the position.
outlooksByWeek.3: Brock Bowers played through a minor knee injury in Week 2 and didn't seem to have his usual burst, catching five of eight targets for only 38 yards. His final line could have been much better, but Geno Smith missed him at the goal line in the fourth quarter. Bowers is still looking for his first touchdown of 2025, but a 10-141-0 line on 16 targets is elite production, with the promise of more once he gets on the same page with the Raiders' new QB. The second-year tight end could be headed for a ceiling game in Week 3 against a Commanders defense that just allowed a 6-124-1 line to the Packers' Tucker Kraft.

player.seasonOutlook: Bowers is fresh off a dominant rookie season in which he produced 262.7 fantasy points, easily the most by a first-year tight end. He was a featured player right out of the gate and went on to pace the position in routes, targets, receptions (112 is the most ever by a rookie, regardless of position), yards and fantasy points. Bowers' season could've been even better had he seen more goal-line work (he was limited to five TDs and six end zone targets). He is already an elite player and the 22-year-old figures to benefit from improved QB play now that Geno Smith is under center. Bowers should be one of the first two TEs off the board on draft day.

outlooksByWeek.1: Ladd McConkey got off to a slow start to his rookie season, but by the end he solidified his spot as the Chargers' top downfield weapon, and Justin Herbert's favorite target. The 2024 second-round pick broke out in Week 8 with a 6-111-2 line, and he recorded two other 100-yard games in the regular season before a stunning 9-197-1 performance in a wild-card loss to the Texans. McConkey's ceiling is somewhat limited by the team's run-heavy offensive scheme, but his speed and yards after the catch ability allow him to turn lower target volume into big numbers. He'll look to get his sophomore campaign off to a quick start in Sao Paulo for a Week 1 tilt against a Kansas City secondary that ranked sixth in receiving yards allowed to WRs but tied for 24th in receiving TDs allowed to the position.
outlooksByWeek.2: Ladd McConkey posted solid numbers in the Chargers' season opener, but he surprisingly didn't dominate looks from Justin Herbert. Keenan Allen led the team with 10 targets to McConkey's nine, and Allen and Quentin Johnston were on the other end of all three of Herbert's TD passes, leaving McConkey with a 6-74-0 line. That production may represent something close to his floor, and he should still be the team's No. 1 WR. McConkey will look to find the end zone for the first time in 2025 in Week 2's clash with a Raiders secondary that just got lit up by unheralded Patriots wideout Kayshon Boutte, but which ranked a respectable 10th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Ladd McConkey start to the season has been steady, catching 11 of 14 targets for 122 yards through two games. The second-year wideout remains the top option for Justin Herbert, but McConkey hasn't yet scored in 2025 even though the Chargers' QB tossed five touchdowns so far. McConkey could have a big performance coming soon, as his 3.21 yards per route run is well ahead of last year's 2.39 mark. He faces a tough test in Week 3 against a Broncos secondary that has yet to allow a receiving TD to a wide receiver this season.

player.seasonOutlook: McConkey is entering his second NFL season following an impressive rookie campaign in which he ranked in the top 20 among receivers in receptions, yards, TDs, catch rate, yards per target and yards per route run. Following a bit of an inconsistent start, McConkey heated up down the stretch and ended up 12th in fantasy points (18th in PPG). Including the playoffs, the 2024 second-round pick caught five or more passes in eight straight games to end the season. The 23-year-old has already emerged as Justin Herbert's top target and his short-to-intermediate role puts a 100-plus catch season in play in 2025. The arrival of Tre Harris and Keenan Allen could damper McConkey's upside a bit, but he's still a safe WR2 target.

outlooksByWeek.1: Kenneth Walker is set to lead Seattle's RB corps Week 1 against San Francisco. However, Zach Charbonnet could play a prominent role in the backfield as well, so it wouldn't be surprising if the two ball-carriers finished with something close to an even snap split. Even when healthy last year, Walker averaged just 3.7 YPC on 153 rushes, and he played in a career-low 11 contests. The 49ers -- who brought back Robert Saleh as the defensive coordinator in the offseason -- struggled against the run last year, giving up 18 rushing touchdowns to RBs (tied for most in the NFL) while yielding 4.3 YPC.
outlooksByWeek.2: Kenneth Walker will aim to bounce back from a poor season-opening showing when Seattle faces Pittsburgh in Week 2. In the first week of the regular season, Walker gained just 20 yards on 10 rushes while Zach Charbonnet carried 12 times for 47 yards. A similarly even workload split in Week 2 could signal that Walker isn't going to be used as a workhorse this season. The Seahawks' Week 2 opponent, Pittsburgh, allowed Jets RB Breece Hall to rumble for 107 yards on 19 carries this past Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kenneth Walker may have retaken the lead in Seattle's backfield heading into Week 3 against the Saints. Walker was out-carried by Zach Charbonnet while rushing for just 20 yards on 10 carries in Week 1, but he stormed back with 105 yards and a touchdown on 13 rushes (to Charbonnet's 10 yards on 15 totes) this past Sunday against Pittsburgh. The two tailbacks figure to continue splitting touches fairly evenly, so it will be important for Walker to make the most of the reps he gets. New Orleans has given up a hearty 4.69 yards per carry to RBs through two games this season, though the Saints have yet to allow a rushing touchdown.

player.seasonOutlook: Walker is entering his fourth NFL season eyeing a bounce-back after injuries limited him to career-low marks in touches, yardage and touchdowns in 2024. The good news is that the 2022 second-round pick remained Seattle's clear feature back and was productive when active. In those 11 games, he averaged 18.1 touches, 79.3 yards and a career-high 16.5 fantasy points per game. Despite the missed action, Walker hit career-best marks in targets, catches and receiving yards thanks to a hefty 14% target share (fifth highest among RBs). Still only 24 years old, Walker is a prime rebound candidate and the boost in receiving work (assuming that sticks under new OC Klint Kubiak) adds to his ceiling. Walker is a solid RB2 target.

outlooksByWeek.1: Bo Nix put together a very impressive rookie season in 2024, producing 33 total touchdowns including 29 through the air, good for sixth in the NFL. The 12th overall pick in last year's draft proved to be a good fit for Broncos coach Sean Payton's offensive scheme, with his accuracy and production both increasing significantly in the second half. Over his last eight regular-season games, Nix completed 70.3% of his passes for 2,022 yards and 21 passing TDs. Denver improved his supporting cast in the offseason with veteran tight end Evan Engram and the backfield duo of J.K. Dobbins and 2025 second-round pick RJ Harvey. Young wideouts Marvin Mims and Troy Franklin could take a step forward, supplementing established top target Courtland Sutton. Nix will begin his sophomore campaign with a Week 1 tilt at home against a Titans defense that gave up the fewest passing yards in the league in 2024.
outlooksByWeek.2: Bo Nix had an underwhelming start to his sophomore campaign, committing three turnovers  while throwing for 176 yards and a touchdown in a Week 1 win. The Broncos' young QB has a similarly slow start to 2024 before catching fire. Nix still has only one reliable downfield option in Courtland Sutton, especially with veteran tight end Evan Engram suffering a calf injury in Week 1, and he may need a younger wideout like Marvin Mims to break out if his numbers are going to rise to the next level. Nix will face a Colts defense in Week 2 that had no problem shutting down a dysfunctional Dolphins attack in its opener, but which finished 25th in passing yards allowed in 2024.
outlooksByWeek.3: Bo Nix quickly turned things around after a shaky Week 1, throwing three touchdowns in Week 2's loss to the Colts. The second-year quarterback also completed 73.3% of his passes, a performance more in line with his second-half breakout as a rookie, but he did toss another interception, his fourth turnover of the year. The Broncos' offense is still struggling to find consistency, but Troy Franklin is showing signs of emerging as a solid WR2 behind Courtland Sutton. Nix faces a tough test in Week 3 against a Chargers defense that just recorded three sacks and three INTs against the Raiders' Geno Smith in Week 2's Monday night affair.

player.seasonOutlook: Nix returns as Denver's starter after an impressive rookie campaign in which he produced 316.2 fantasy points, fifth most by a first-year QB. Nix improved as the season went on. After posting 5.7 YPA and five pass TDs during his first seven games, he leapt to a 7.4 YPA and 24 pass TDs in his final 10 outings. He finished the regular season sixth in pass attempts, completions and pass TDs, as well as fifth among QBs in carries. Nix's dual-threat ability and improved supporting cast (which now includes Evan Engram) have him on the QB1 radar, and there's upside for more.

outlooksByWeek.1: George Pickens brings his immense talent and ego to the Cowboys in 2025.  Pickens will operate as the No. 2 wideout and primary big-play option for Dallas alongside CeeDee Lamb; Pickens averages over 16 yards per catch for his NFL career. He will see plenty of single coverage too with Lamb on the other side, though his opportunities may also be slightly more limited than they were in Pittsburgh given the pecking order.  Dallas could be in plenty of shootouts or playing from behind in many contests as well this season.  The latter could be the case in Week 1 versus the defending champion Philadelphia Eagles. The Eagles allowed the fewest passing yards per game in the NFL last season, though, so the matchup is far from ideal.
outlooksByWeek.2: George Pickens had a mediocre debut for the Dallas Cowboys. Pickens caught three passes on four targets for just 30 yards in the 24-20 loss to the Eagles. While he did draw a 34-yard pass interference penalty, he was also penalized himself for unnecessary roughness, all but killing a potential game-winning drive. The mercurial Pickens will continue to prove unpredictable in Week 2 versus the New York Giants. The G-Men allowed just 212 passing yards and a single passing score to Washington in Week 1, though all the attention likely to be given to CeeDee Lamb could make Pickens a breakout candidate for his second game with America's Team, as the Commanders picked on underwhelming Giants starting cornerback Cor'Dale Flott in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: George Pickens found the end zone for the first time as a member of the Dallas Cowboys last game. Pickens collected five catches on nine targets en route to 68 yards and the score. If the Cowboys defense continues to struggle, Pickens and the rest of the offense could be in line for some mammoth performances, including in Week 3 versus the Bears. Chicago has allowed the most points in the NFL through two outings, including a league-worst seven receiving touchdowns.

player.seasonOutlook: Pickens was traded to the Cowboys after spending his first three seasons in Pittsburgh. Perhaps the change of scenery will get him to the next level, as he's thus far been an exciting playmaker but not yet a consistent fantasy option. Pickens handled a career-high 26% target share (15th among WRs) last season, but he missed three games and found the end zone only three times despite seeing 12 end zone targets (12th most). Pickens has finished 37th or worse in fantasy PPG all three seasons while playing a volatile field-stretcher role (top 15 in aDOT all three years). He will certainly benefit from improved QB play (Dak Prescott), but he now has legitimate target competition from CeeDee Lamb. We likely haven't seen Pickens' best work, but there's enough uncertainty here that the 24-year-old should be valued as a midrange WR3.

outlooksByWeek.1: Jameson Williams has drawn rave reviews throughout the offseason and will look to translate that momentum into on-field production as the Lions travel to Green Bay in Week 1. Fresh off the first 1,000-yard season of his career, the 2022 first-round pick still certainly has an untapped ceiling, though losing former OC Ben Johnson and two starters along the interior O-line do represent hurdles to his taking another step forward. It remains to be seen whether new OC John Morton will deploy Williams as creatively around the formation as Johnson did, but he remains the Loins' premier deep threat and is clearly one of the team's most explosive players, an honor he shares with RB Jahmyr Gibbs. Against the Packers, who ranked third against the past last season, though, it's possible Gibbs and David Montgomery are featured more heavily than the aerial attack.
outlooksByWeek.2: Jameson Williams and the Lions' offense will look to get right at home against the Bears in Week 2 after a disappointing season-opening loss to Green Bay. Versus the Packers, Williams recorded four receptions on five targets for 23 yards, with his longest reception being just 11 yards. That marks his lowest yardage total in a regular-season game since Week 7 of the 2024 campaign, though somewhat worryingly, in Detroit's most recent contest (an NFC divisional-round playoff loss to the Commanders), he only had one catch for 19 yards on four targets. Despite the underwhelming performance, Williams' role in the offense remains significant, and the Bears' defense presents an opportunity for a bounce-back game. If Jaylon Johnson shadows Williams, however, OC John Morton could simply opt to funnel the passing game through Detroit's plethora of other offensive weapons.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jameson Williams and the Lions will look to keep up their momentum Week 3 against Baltimore. In the team's tremendous 52-21 win over the Bears, Williams made the most of four targets, logging two grabs for 108 yards and a touchdown, finishing second on the team in terms of yardage behind Amon-Ra St. Brown (9-115-3). Williams' field-stretching abilities make him a weekly candidate for explosive plays, despite facing occasional bracket coverage, though Baltimore's coverage is faster and more disciplined than Chicago's by multiple degrees. Nonetheless, William's speed and ability to win 1-on-1 matchups keep him in line for WR2/flex upside.

player.seasonOutlook: The No. 12 overall pick back in 2022, Williams finally broke out last season after barely seeing the field his first two years in the league due to suspensions and injuries. The explosive playmaker was involved as both a rusher and receiver, which helped him to 1,062 scrimmage yards (18th among WRs) and eight TDs in 15 games. A top-7 finisher in YPR, YPT and RAC, Williams finished 25th at the position in fantasy PPG despite sitting outside the top 40 in targets and catches. A boost in volume will be important to Williams' consistency moving forward, but the 24-year-old will continue to benefit from Detroit's high-scoring offense. No lower than third in target priority, Williams is best valued as a fringe WR3 who very well could take another step forward in his second "full" season.

outlooksByWeek.1: Jakobi Meyers produced his first 1,000-yard season in 2024 despite catching passes from three different quarterbacks in a turbulent year for the Raiders offense. Things should be much more stable in 2025, as the team brought in head coach Pete Carroll and traded for Geno Smith to handle QB duties, but Meyers might create his own drama after failing to get a contract extension this offseason. He'll face additional competition for targets with second-year tight end Brock Bowers being joined by rookie running back Ashton Jeanty and, more importantly, late signing Amari Cooper, who presents a direct challenge to Meyers at the top of the WR depth chart. While Meyers should retain his spot early in the season as Cooper gets up to speed, he doesn't have a strong Week 1 matchup against a Patriots secondary that finished in the top half of the league in 2024 in receiving yards and TDs allowed to wideouts.
outlooksByWeek.2: Jakobi Meyers put his contract dispute with the Raiders behind him to deliver an 8-97-0 line on 10 targets in Week 1. The veteran wideout flashed some immediate chemistry with new QB Geno Smith, and with Brock Bowers coming out of Sunday's game nursing a knee injury, Meyers' volume could even grow if the tight end needs to miss time. Meyers also faces little competition for targets from an otherwise inexperienced Las Vegas receiving corps. He'll try to stay productive in Week 2 against a Chargers secondary that finished 10th in receptions allowed to WRs last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jakobi Meyers notched double-digit targets in back-to-back games to begin the season as he quickly establishes himself as a reliable option for new quarterback Geno Smith. The veteran wideout hasn't scored yet in 2025, but he's turned 22 targets into a 14-165-0 line, leading the Raiders in both catches and receiving yards. Star tight end Brock Bowers is playing through a minor knee issue, which has also helped Meyers' volume. Meyers could take a back seat to Bowers in Week 3 against a Commanders defense that couldn't contain the Packers' Tucker Kraft last week, but he should have a solid floor as Washington's secondary has allowed three different WRs to catch four or more passes.

player.seasonOutlook: Perhaps the most underrated player in fantasy, Meyers enters 2025 eyeing his fifth consecutive top-30 fantasy campaign. The veteran is one of 10 receivers with 67-plus receptions and 800-plus receiving yards in each of the past four seasons and he peaked with career highs in targets, catches, yards and end zone targets (11) in 2024. The 28-year-old has dealt with shaky QB play in recent seasons, but is in a better spot this season with Geno Smith under center and Pete Carroll coaching the team. Second only to Brock Bowers in target priority, Meyers figures to again push for WR3/flex numbers, but will likely be undervalued on draft day.

outlooksByWeek.1: Rhamondre Stevenson looks to prove his worth for the Patriots entering a Week 1 matchup with the Raiders. He's coming off a career-worst 3.9 yards per carry season and fumbles remain a concern, coughing it up a career-high seven times in 2024. The preseason hype for TreVeyon Henderson is real, but he was never a full workload guy at Ohio State. Stevenson should reprise his between the tackles, double-digit plus touches against a defense that allowed a fair 4.3 yards per carry last season, making him at minimum a fine flex play.
outlooksByWeek.2: Rhamondre Stevenson hopes for a bigger workload in Week 2 when the Patriots face the Dolphins. New England was surprisingly pass happy in Week 1, resulting in just seven carries for Stevenson, accounting for a mere 15 yards, adding two catches for 12 yards. Those nine touches were slightly less than rookie TreVeyon Henderson's 15, though neither shined. The Dolphins front seems to lack elite personnel but allowed only 3.6 yards per carry in Week 1, and with a limited carry share, Stevenson lacks much Week 2 potential.
outlooksByWeek.3: Rhamondre Stevenson looks like an unsung hero for the Patriots entering a Week 3 matchup with the Steelers. Stevenson collected five targets for 88 yards in Week 2 to go along with 11 carries for 54 yards, and while the masses want to tout TreVeyon Henderson's potential, it's just that. Henderson has failed to flash, and Stevenson is dominating this backfield, earning more than a 60% snap share in both outings. Facing a Steelers defense that's big in name only, allowing the fifth most points to opposing running backs, Stevenson is again in place to outperform his draft day value.

player.seasonOutlook: Stevenson returns for his fifth season in New England, but his role is not as secure as in years past after the team drafted TreVeyon Henderson in the second round and after fumbling issues (RB-high seven) led to a demotion during the 2024 season. Those issues aside, Stevenson was still fairly busy and effective despite New England's shaky offense last season, as he totaled 969 yards (the second most of his career) and a career-high eight TDs. The 27-year-old figures to benefit from the team's coaching change, as all six of Mike Vrabel's Titans offenses were run-heavy. Stevenson may remain the starter in New England, but there's a good chance he'll play a lesser role as the thunder to Henderson's lightning. Stevenson is a fringe flex option with limited upside.

A historically strong defense, the Ravens had 50-plus sacks in 2023 and 2024, the only NFL team to do that, and they roster two All-Pros (CB Marlon Humphrey and LB Roquan Smith) and second-team S Kyle Hamilton. The addition of first-round S Malaki Starks boosts their secondary, and the Ravens have a generally sound schedule including two games each against the Browns and Steelers. Watch out for that tough opening-week matchup (@BUF), however.

outlooksByWeek.1: Jake Bates will run it back as Detroit's starting placekicker Week 1 on the road against Green Bay. After a standout season in the UFL, Bates managed to win his first career NFL starting job with the Lions in 2024, with whom he converted an impressive 90 percent of his field goals. Somewhat paradoxically, Bates' production was to some extent inhibited by Detroit's elite efficiency on offense, as his field-goal attempts (29) ranked just 21st in the league, despite his number of extra-point (67) ranking No. 1. That makes Bates perhaps the only player on the Lions' offense who could actually stand to benefit if the team takes a step backward, especially in the red zone, due to the move from Ben Johnson to new OC John Morton.
outlooksByWeek.2: Jake Bates will look to continue his perfect start to the season as the Lions host the Bears in Week 2. In Week 1, Bates converted both of his field-goal attempts along with his lone extra-point attempt, totaling seven points in Detroit's 27-13 loss to the Packers. Despite the Lions' offensive struggles Week 1, the team will have an opportunity to bounce back to its usual high-scoring self against Chicago's defense, which gave up 27 points to the Vikings in J.J. McCarthy's first start. As a rookie last year, Bates went 26-for-29 on field-goal attempts over 17 regular-season games.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jake Bates and the Lions will travel to Baltimore in WeekaA�3. Coming off a 52-21 WeekaA�2 win over the Bears, Detroit's offense has proven that the departure of Ben Johnson didn't cause a limit to this team's ceiling, Bates missed one of his two field-goal tries. He did, however, convert all seven of his extra-point attempts. If the Lions' offense is able to log another high-scoring performance against Baltimore's stout defense, Bates will remain locked in as one of the NFL's highest-upside kickers. In what may shape up to be a close Week 3 game, however, Bates will need to be more reliable at converting field goals.

outlooksByWeek.1: Jayden Higgins is expected to start on the outside for the Texans in Week 1 against the Rams, though Nico Collins figures to collect the majority of targets among Houston's WRs while Higgins competes for looks with slot man Christian Kirk. Higgins was Houston's second-round selection in the 2025 NFL Draft out of Iowa State. He's a big target in a similar mold to Collins at 6-foot-4 and 215 pounds. The rookie's a risky flex play out of the gate, but he could gain value as the season progresses, especially if the oft-injured Collins gets hurt again.
outlooksByWeek.2: Jayden Higgins led Houston with 32 receiving yards in his NFL debut last week, but that stat is more of an indictment on the rest of the team's WR room than a point of praise for the 2025 second-round draft pick. The Texans' entire passing game has a nice opportunity to pick things up in Week 2 against a Tampa Bay secondary that allowed the fourth-most passing yards in the NFL last season, and Higgins is already operating as a starter on the outside. That said, he's likely to cede the majority of targets to Nico Collins, and Christian Kirk (hamstring) could also contend for attention from C.J. Stroud if Kirk suits up, leaving Higgins as a flex play at best for Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jayden Higgins is averaging 20.0 yards per catch through the first two games of the season, though he's not expected to continue posting those numbers. He's also likely to experience a severe drop in targets and workload with Christian Kirk (hamstring) set to return to the lineup. The second-round rookie was targeted just once in the Week 2 loss to the Buccaneers, and with Kirk back in the mix, chances are he's not going to be a factor in the passing game anymore. Higgins should be left on waivers for the Week 3 matchup against the Jaguars and should remain there until further notice. When the Texans are at full strength in their receiving corps, the former Iowa State standout wouldn't be anything more than the fourth or fifth option in a passing game that hasn't been very effective.

player.seasonOutlook: Higgins was selected by Houston in the second round of April's draft. He is one of the biggest receivers in this class at 6-foot-4, 214 pounds with an 80-inch wingspan. He tested well athletically at the combine and his 2.86 career YPRR ranked third best in this WR class. He handled a big-time target share at Iowa State and was a machine at converting catches into first downs (class-best 74% rate). With Tank Dell a long shot to play in 2025, Higgins will compete with Christian Kirk, Xavier Hutchinson and fellow rookie Jaylin Noel for No. 2 duties opposite Nico Collins. Flex production is possible if he wins that gig, but a lot has to go right. He's best viewed as a late-round lottery ticket.

outlooksByWeek.1: Jaydon Blue looks like a backup for the Cowboys at running back in Week 1 on Thursday, but the rest of the situation involving carries out of the backfield remains murky. Javonte Williams looks like the starter, but veteran Miles Sanders will also compete for touches, and all three could see work in the season opener. The Cowboys could also simply ride the hot hand in this committee approach. In Week 1, Dallas will face an Eagles defense that was rather stingy against the run in 2024. Philadelphia allowed just 104.2 yards per clash on the ground, which was 10th in the league. The Eagles also yielded just nine rushing scores last year, which second in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Blue was selected by Dallas in the fifth round of April's draft. Blue's workload was limited in crowded Texas RB rooms (214 carries in three years), but he was an effective rusher (his 3.83 career YAC is fifth best in this class) and he showed his receiving chops with a 42-368-6 receiving line in 2024. He's a bit on the small side (196 pounds) and has had fumble issues, but ran a strong 4.38 40 at the combine. Blue may open his career behind veterans Javonte Williams and Miles Sanders, but neither have played well in recent seasons so this depth chart is wide open. Blue will be on the RB2/flex radar if he wins the lead-back job, so he should be on your radar in the late rounds.

outlooksByWeek.1: Joe Mixon will begin the season on the NFI list due to a foot injury, ensuring he will miss at least the first four games, starting with Week 1 against the Rams. Houston's backfield mix will include some combination of Nick Chubb, Dameon Pierce, Woody Marks, Dare Ogunbowale and British Brooks in Mixon's absence, with Chubb likely to start against the Rams. Mixon remains without a timetable to return.
outlooksByWeek.2: Joe Mixon began the season on the NFI list due to a foot injury, ensuring he will miss at least the first four games. He'll remain sidelined in Week 2 against the Buccaneers. Nick Chubb led Houston's backfield in Week 1 and figures to get the bulk of carries again Week 2, with Dameon Pierce, Woody Marks and Dare Ogunbowale on hand in change-of-pace roles. Mixon remains without a timetable to return.

player.seasonOutlook: Mixon is back with Houston following a relatively successful debut campaign with the team, however he'll miss, at least, the first four games of the 2025 season due to injury. In 2024, Mixon also struggled with injuries, missing three games and leaving several early, but he was a heavily utilized force when active. During the 15 games he played at least 40% of the snaps (including the playoffs), Mixon averaged 21.4 touches, 101.1 yards and 18.1 fantasy points per game, scoring 14 TDs during the span. Mixon carries some risk as a 29-year-old back with 2,313 career touches and, though he has added competition in the form of Nick Chubb and rookie Woody Marks, he still has a path to substantial work as both a rusher and receiver, once healthy. Mixon's injury means he's only worth a late flier, but if he returns to action, he can find his way back to the RB2 mix.

outlooksByWeek.1: Brenton Strange is set to work as the Jaguars' top TE in 2025, starting with a Week 1 home game against the Panthers. The 2023 second-round pick had previously been the backup to Evan Engram, who signed with Denver in the offseason. Strange had 29 catches for 275 yards and two TDs on 39 targets in the eight games Engram missed due to injury, compared to just 11 catches for 136 yards on 14 targets in nine games playing with Engram. While there's a path to fantasy viability given QB Trevor Lawrence's affinity for throwing to the TE, Strange opens the season as a fantasy reserve, though it's worth noting that the Panthers allowed a league-high 11 TD catches to TEs last season.
outlooksByWeek.2: Brenton Strange has a second consecutive favorable matchup to begin his tenure as Jacksonville's starting TE, facing a Bengals defense in Week 2 that allowed the second-most touchdowns in the NFL (10) to tight ends last season. In Week 1, Strange failed to find the end zone against a Panthers defense that allowed a league-high 11 TDs to TEs in 2024, but he led the Jaguars with 59 receiving yards against Carolina. Cincinnati allowed Cleveland's TEs to combine for 10 catches and 100 receiving yards last week, so Strange could sneak into the fantasy TE1 range for Week 2 given the enticing matchup.
outlooksByWeek.3: Brenton Strange failed to score a TD in Jacksonville's first two games despite facing the two defenses that allowed the most touchdowns to TE in 2024. In Week 3, he draws a Houston defense that tied for the fifth-most TDs allowed to the position with eight. Consistency hasn't been Strange's strong suit, and that has remained the case so in 2025, as he had a team-high 59 receiving yards Week 1 but only 17 yards Week 2. He's a viable fantasy option as the Jaguars' top TE, but Strange's low floor makes him a low-end fantasy starter at best, and shallower leagues could have more appealing Week 3 alternatives on the waiver wire.

player.seasonOutlook: Strange is the new No. 1 tight end in Jacksonville following the release of Evan Engram. We got a preview of this last season when Engram was sidelined for eight games. In those weeks, Strange played 72% of the snaps and handled a solid 14.6% target share (4.9 per game). That led to one big fantasy outing (12-11-73-0 in Week 15), but he otherwise averaged 6.9 fantasy PPG and failed to clear 12.4 points in any of the other seven games. Perhaps Strange gets to another level in Year 3, but, especially with Brian Thomas Jr. and Travis Hunter set to be featured, the 2023 second-round pick seems likely to settle in as a low-ceiling TE2.

outlooksByWeek.1: Quentin Johnston took a step forward in 2024 after a disastrous rookie campaign, but the 21st overall pick in 2023 is still a long way from living up to the draft capital invested in him by the Chargers. The TCU product delivered a 55-711-8 line on 91 targets over 15 regular-season games, but he completely vanished in a wild-card loss to the Texans while rookie Ladd McConkey nearly single-handedly carried the team's passing game. Johnston's size gives him some red-zone potential, but issues with drops have plagued him in the NFL, and the team's decisions to bring back Keenan Allen while taking Tre Harris in the second round of the 2025 Draft weren't votes of confidence. Johnston will try to find paydirt in a Week 1 trip to Sao Paulo to face a Kansas City secondary that ranked sixth in receiving yards allowed to WRs but tied for 24th in receiving TDs allowed to the position.
outlooksByWeek.2: Quentin Johnston made a big contribution in the Chargers' season opener, striking for five catches, 79 yards and two touchdowns on seven targets. That target volume was only third on the team as Keenan Allen logged 10 looks from Justin Herbert and Ladd McConkey garnered nine. Johnston's fantasy value may be fairly TD-dependent once again after he delivered a 55-711-8 line on 91 targets over 15 regular-season games in 2024. He'll look to keep rolling in Week 2 against a Raiders secondary that just got lit up by unheralded Patriots wideout Kayshon Boutte, but which ranked a respectable 10th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Quentin Johnston continues to make regular trips to the end zone. The third-year wideout captured three of Justin Herbert's five passing touchdowns through two games, with Johnston posting a 3-71-1 line on seven targets in a Week 2 win over the Raiders. He only has eight catches in total on 14 targets, and perhaps no WR in the league relies more heavily on scoring to keep their fantasy value afloat. That could be a problem in Week 3, as the Chargers face a Broncos secondary that has yet to allow a receiving touchdown to a wide receiver this season.

player.seasonOutlook: The 21st overall pick back in 2023, Johnston had the look of a bust after struggling to a 38-431-2 receiving line as a rookie. Things improved under a new coaching staff in Year 2, with Johnston doubling his rookie-season target share (from 11% to 22%) and scoring eight TDs (12th most among receivers). His production was inconsistent, however, as 43% of his fantasy points came in three games and he had seven single-digit outings. He finished 39th or lower in snaps, routes, targets, catches, yards and fantasy PPG, so, if he's going to join the WR3/flex discussion, he'll need a volume boost in order to offset TD regression to the mean (4.8 xTD). That boost is unlikely, as he'll now have to battle Keenan Allen and rookie Tre Harris for work behind Ladd McConkey. Johnston is barely worth a late flier.

outlooksByWeek.1: The Vikings will count on Justin Jefferson to lead the aerial attack, as per usual, Week 1 on the road against Chicago. With Jordan Addison suspended the first three games of the year, Jefferson and TE T.J. Hockenson figure to handle expanded target volume as the clear top pass-catchers available for QB J.J. McCarthy, who will be effectively making his starting debut after a rookie year lost to an MCL tear.
