A left hamstring strain sidelined Jefferson the entire preseason, but all indications are that Minnesota was simply taking a cautious approach to the star wideout's recovery. It's entirely possible that McCarthy, last year's 10th overall pick, requires time to fully get up to speed as a starter, but considering both Jefferson's elite talent level and coach Kevin O'Connell proven scheme, it would take significant question marks to manufacture any concerns about the superstar's ability to produce. The return of Adam Thielen via trade provides Minnesota a useful ancillary complement to Jefferson even while Addison misses time early.
outlooksByWeek.2: Justin Jefferson will work to build further chemistry with new quarterback J.J. McCarthy as the Vikings prepare to take on the Falcons in prime time in Week 2. McCarthy and the passing game struggled mightily through three quarters in Week 1, but a fourth-quarter resurgence was enough for a comeback victory over Chicago. Jefferson scored his only touchdown in the fourth quarter, otherwise finishing with four catches for 44 yards on seven targets. He also rushed once for four yards. The star wideout is entrenched as McCarthy's top wideout, and will remain so even when Jordan Addison returns from his suspension in Week 4. If McCarthy can take a step forward and look like he did to close out the season-opener against the Bears, Jefferson will be positioned to return to his usual position as a weekly threat to exceed the 100-yard mark, but it's entirely conceivable that the second-year signal-caller will need more time to fully find his footing. At the very least, however, Jefferson will benefit from a favorable home matchup against Atlanta in Week 2, as opposed to the unfriendly road conditions of Week 1's narrow win.
outlooksByWeek.3: Justin Jefferson and the Vikings head to Cincinnati for a Week 3 matchup, looking to get right following their 22-6 loss to the Falcons. Versus Atlanta, Jefferson turned a team-high six targets into three catches for 81 yards, struggling to rack up production on a day that saw second-year QB J.J. McCarthy's vulnerabilities and inexperience highlighted. With McCarthy now a candidate to miss time due to an ankle sprain, Jefferson may now have to pivot to catching passes from veteran backup Carson Wentz. Jefferson remains locked in as the focal point of the Vikings' pass attack, but his usual high-end production totals may not return in the near future, or at least until such time as McCarthy gets healthy looks consistently comfortable under center. It won't be until Week 4 that Jefferson gets a chance to benefit from the return of Jordan Addison from his three-game suspension, at which point opposing defenses will at least have further playmakers to assign attention to. The Bengals' secondary is at least the weakest unit Minnesota has faced thus far.

player.seasonOutlook: Jefferson enters his sixth NFL season as one of the best in the league at his position. The 26-year-old has produced a league-high 7,432 receiving yards since his arrival in 2020, having put up at least 100 catches, 1,500 yards and eight TDs in his last three full seasons. Jefferson has finished four straight seasons as a top-5 fantasy receiver on a per-game basis and showed he was QB-proof in 2024, finishing top 5 in catches, yards and TDs with Sam Darnold under center. Darnold is gone, but 2024 first-round pick J.J. McCarthy could conceivably be an upgrade in Kevin O'Connell's pass-first scheme. Jefferson should be one of the first players off the board on draft day.

outlooksByWeek.1: Bucky Irving is set to lead the Buccaneers running game in a Week 1 home matchup against the Falcons. Irving had an impressive rookie campaign and was the only first-year RB in 2024 to surpass 1,000 yards. Tampa Bay will still have Rachaad White in the backfield mix, but it's clear that Irving will be the go-to guy for the team. Atlanta ranked 15th in rushing yards per game allowed last season.
outlooksByWeek.2: Bucky Irving should still get a big workload as he looks to bounce back in Week 2 as Tampa Bay travels to Houston. Irving struggled to get things going in an eventual season-opener win, logging 14 carries for just 37 yards and four catches for eight yards and a touchdown. The second-year rusher was still able to find the end zone, which saved what would've otherwise been a washout of a day. Irving luckily registered 18 touches compared to supplementary running back Rachaad White's three, showing who the Bucs should roll with as their workhorse moving forward. Irving will look to be a bit more efficient in his second game of the season against a Texans defense that let up 66 rushing yards and a touchdown to Kyren Williams in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Bucky Irving should continue to lead Tampa Bay's backfield in a Week 3 game versus the Jets. Irving finished Week 2 with 12 carries for 71 yards and six grabs for 50 yards. Although his backfield mate Rachaad White scored the sole rushing touchdown of the pair and still logged 12 touches, Irving still outpaced his teammate by seven carries and four targets. Irving should be able to leverage this high volume versus a New York defense that has given up the fourth-most fantasy points to running backs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Irving is a strong 2025 breakout candidate following an impressive rookie season. The fourth-round pick didn't play on over half the snaps in a game until Week 6, but was fantasy's No. 10 RB from that point on. He produced 15-plus fantasy points in nine of his final 12 games, with injury responsible for two duds. Irving's efficiency was elite, as his 5.4 YPC, 2.5 YAC, 90% catch rate and 7.5 RAC were all top 5 among RBs. Irving will defer some work to Rachaad White, and his 192-frame raises obvious durability questions, but he looked the part as a rookie and is well positioned for 15-plus touches per game in a good offense. At worst, he's a fringe RB1.

outlooksByWeek.1: Lamar Jackson finished second in the NFL MVP voting in 2024 and continues to cement himself as one of the best players in the league. He'll lead the Baltimore offense for the seventh consecutive season, coming off a career-best 4,172 passing yards and 45 total touchdowns in 2024. What makes Jackson truly special is his ability as a rusher, and he also racked up 915 yards on the ground in 2024. He'll head into a tough environment for a Week 1 matchup against the Bills, but Buffalo's secondary has questions at outside corner and free safety so Jackson should be in a good position to get off to a strong start. He's a locked-in fantasy starter.
outlooksByWeek.2: Lamar Jackson put together an impressive showing in Baltimore's Week 1 loss, averaging a very efficient 11.0 yards and two touchdowns on 19 pass attempts. He also showcased his dual-threat ability, racking up 70 yards on the ground with an additional score. Baltimore may not need to be so aggressive in a Week 2 matchup against Cleveland, but Jackson remains a must-start quarterback so long as he remains healthy.
outlooksByWeek.3: Lamar Jackson is already making his push for MVP, accounting for seven total touchdowns combined across Baltimore's first two games. He's attempted under 30 passes in both contests but has been extremely efficient (9.0 yards per attempt), and he'll likely be pushed into more explosive playmaking opportunities in a Week 3 matchup against the Lions. Jackson remains an elite fantasy option at quarterback and should be locked into starting lineups.

player.seasonOutlook: The reigning fantasy QB1, Jackson outscored QB2 Josh Allen by a hefty 51.3 points in 2024. He remained his usual elite self as a rusher (he's finished first or second among QBs in rushing yards all seven seasons), but also made a huge leap as a passer (career highs in pass attempts, completions, yards and TDs, as well as a career-low four INTs and a league-high 8.8 YPA). The only "knock" on Jackson that is relative to other top fantasy QBs is rushing TDs (he has 14 total over the last four seasons and had zero carries inside the opponent's 5-yard line last season), but he does more than enough otherwise to provide elite fantasy output. With an almost-identical supporting cast to 2024, we should expect more of the same from the 28-year-old this season.

outlooksByWeek.1: TreVeyon Henderson's hype train debuts for the Patriots in Week 1 against the Raiders. The rookie second-round pick showed big play potential throughout the preseason, and the only question that remains is his touch total, as Rhamondre Stevenson will still collect his fair share. It's best to proceed with caution, as pass protection for a rookie can lead to limited reps, but given the draft capital Henderson required, he can be deployed as an RB2 with managers in search of a big play.
outlooksByWeek.2: TreVeyon Henderson will look for more touches in Week 2 when the Patriots face the Dolphins. Henderson averaged a solid 5.4 yards per carry in Week 1, but only took five totes in his debut, adding a solid six catches but failing to break the big plays he showed during the preseason, finishing with just 24 yards. Miami allowed a mere 3.6 yards per carry last week, but Henderson's per touch average offers encouragement. If the Patriots don't pass 46 times here, there's reason for optimism.
outlooksByWeek.3: TreVeyon Henderson seeks his breakout performance in Week 3 for the Patriots against the Steelers. After a fantastic preseason, Henderson has only 16 touches through two weeks, playing around 30% of the New England's running back snaps. He's always a play away from shining, but Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel appears to favor the stability of Rhamondre Stevenson. Henderson is a buy low candidate or a stash rather than a Week 3 option against a defense that's surprisingly allowing the fifth most fantasy points to running backs through two weeks.

player.seasonOutlook: Henderson was selected by New England in the second round of April's draft. The Ohio State product paced this rookie RB class with 7.1 YPC last season and was effective as both a rusher and receiver throughout his collegiate tenure. His size could limit his carry total a bit in the pros, but he impressed across the board athletically at the combine and his elite pass-blocking skills and three-down ability will make him a terrific fit in the modern NFL. Henderson figures to share some work with Rhamondre Stevenson, but there's plenty of upside here and he can be valued as a RB2.

outlooksByWeek.1: Calvin Ridley is expected to benefit from better QB play in 2025 with rookie first overall pick Cam Ward under center for the Titans. That improvement may not be immediately apparent in Week 1, as the Titans face a Broncos defense that allowed the third-fewest points last season and includes star CB Patrick Surtain. The tough matchup coupled with uncertainty over how quickly Ward will acclimate to the NFL make Ridley tough to trust as anything more than a low-end WR3 in Week 1. Ridley's season-long outlook is more optimistic, though, as Tennessee's No. 1 WR is coming off back-to-back 1,000-yard receiving seasons and is likely to see a bump in efficiency after catching only 64 of 120 targets in 2024.
outlooksByWeek.2: Calvin Ridley dealt with a familiar struggle in Tennessee's season opener, as rookie first overall pick Cam Ward sprayed inaccurate passes reminiscent of the ones from Will Levis last season. Ward has significant long-term upside, but Ridley is once again being limited by poor QB play in the short term, despite working as the clear No. 1 option in Tennessee's passing game. Ridley turned a team-high eight targets into four catches for 27 yards as Ward threw for just 112 yards in Week 1, and converting volume to production could be challenging again in Week 2 against a Rams defense that just held Houston's Nico Collins to 25 yards. The possibility of Ward figuring things out quickly keeps Ridley in the Week 2 flex conversation, but benching Ridley should certainly be on the table if you have decent alternatives.
outlooksByWeek.3: Calvin Ridley leads the Titans with 14 targets and 84 receiving yards through two games, but that production is well below what his fantasy managers had been hoping for heading into a Week 3 home game against the Colts. Rookie first overall pick Cam Ward hasn't provided an upgrade compared to the lackluster QB play that held Ridley back last season, though Ward certainly has the potential to improve moving forward. Until that happens, Ridley will be an uninspiring flex option. The Colts have allowed only one wide receiver to exceed 40 yards through two games, so Ridley's far from a must-start Week 3 despite his perch atop Tennessee's WR depth chart.

player.seasonOutlook: Ridley is back for his second season as the Titans' top receiver. His first season was solid, especially considering the team's QB issues, and he's now produced just over 1,000 scrimmage yards two seasons in a row. Ridley led the NFL in air yards (1,849) last season, which allowed him a few big plays and somewhat offset a big usage dip near the goal line (he scored eight TDs and led the NFL with 25 end zone targets with Jacksonville in 2023, but fell to five TDs and four end zone targets in 2024). Ridley has finished one season better than 18th in fantasy PPG (two better than 24th) and, while his positioning atop the depth chart in Tennessee keeps him in the WR3/flex mix, his upside will be determined by the play of No. 1 pick Cam Ward.

outlooksByWeek.1: DeVonta Smith failed to go over the 1,000-yard receiving mark for the first time in three seasons for the Eagles last year, but he did catch a career-high eight touchdowns, with two of them coming against the Cowboys, the Week 1 opponent for the Eagles.  Dallas was mediocre at best against the pass in 2024, allowing 218.1 passing yards per tilt, which was 17th in the league.  Dallas also surrendered 28 passing scores last season, which was tied for 24th in the NFL. Dallas re-signed cornerback DaRon Bland but traded dynamic pass rusher Micah Parsons, so the defense is unlikely to be better overall in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.2: DeVonta Smith was incredibly quiet in Week 1 for the Eagles. Smith managed just 16 yards on three in the 24-20 win over the Cowboys. Meanwhile, Jahan Dotson was the surprise leading receiver for the squad, and Dallas Goedert notched the most targets. Expect the Eagles to get Smith involved early and often in Week 2 versus Kansas City, though. Kansas City was torched by Justin Herbert for 304 yards and three touchdowns through the air in its season opener. Smith also scored a touchdown against the AFC powerhouse in the Super Bowl last February and led the Birds in receiving for the game.
outlooksByWeek.3: DeVonta Smith led the Eagles in receiving yards in Week 2, and while that was an improvement from the season opener, his final stat line still left a lot to be desired. Smith caught four passes on six targets, but managed just 53 yards and did not find the end zone in the 20-17 win over Kansas City. Smith has a paltry 69 receiving yards through two games, and will look to get back on track in Week 3 versus the Rams. Unfortunately, the Rams have been stingy against the pass thus far in 2025, allowing just 147 passing yards per tilt, which is fourth in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Smith is entering his fifth NFL season having finished each of the past three in the top 20 among WRs in fantasy PPG. Smith has posted a target share of at least 22% in all four seasons, and the Eagles' high-scoring offense has allowed him seven-plus TDs in three straight campaigns. Smith's output is a bit volatile due to the presence of heavily targeted A.J. Brown in an offense that leads off with Saquon Barkley and Jalen Hurts, and leans heavily on them near the goal line, but there is just enough volume and scoring opportunity here to keep Smith in the weekly WR3 mix.

outlooksByWeek.1: Rashee Rice is still looking for a chance to build on the impressive chemistry he flashed with Patrick Mahomes when he was a rookie in 2023. Last year, a knee injury limited Rice to effectively three games, as he followed up a 12-110-1 line in Week 3 by playing just four snaps in Week 4 before being lost for the season. The 25-year-old appears to be fully recovered heading into the current campaign, but he'll need to serve a six-game suspension first before getting on the field. Rice will target a Week 7 game against the Raiders for his 2025 debut for Kansas City.
outlooksByWeek.2: Rashee Rice is still looking for a chance to build on the impressive chemistry he flashed with Patrick Mahomes when he was a rookie in 2023. Last year, a knee injury limited Rice to effectively three games, as he followed up a 12-110-1 line in Week 3 by playing just four snaps in Week 4 before being lost for the season. The 25-year-old appears to be fully recovered heading into the current campaign, but he'll need to serve a six-game suspension first before getting on the field, costing him a Week 2 clash with the Eagles. Rice will target a Week 7 game against the Raiders for his 2025 debut with Kansas City.
outlooksByWeek.3: Rashee Rice is still looking for a chance to build on the impressive chemistry he flashed with Patrick Mahomes when he was a rookie in 2023. Last year, a knee injury limited Rice to effectively three games, as he followed up a 12-110-1 line in Week 3 by playing just four snaps in Week 4 before being lost for the season. The 25-year-old appears to be fully recovered heading into the current campaign, but he'll need to serve a six-game suspension first before getting on the field, costing him a Week 3 clash with the Giants. Rice will target a Week 7 game against the Raiders for his 2025 debut with Kansas City.

player.seasonOutlook: Rice is undoubtedly one of the biggest wild cards in fantasy football this season. On one hand, he has been an absolute fantasy superstar since taking on a substantial role midway through his rookie season in 2023. During that span (nine regular-season games), Rice is averaging 19.5 fantasy PPG. In three full games last season, he handled a massive 36% target share (10.7 per game) and averaged 21.6 PPG (17-plus in all three). On the other hand, Rice is suspended for the Chiefs' first six games, he tore his LCL in Week 3 last season and, even when active, he now has legitimate target competition via Xavier Worthy, Hollywood Brown and Travis Kelce. The good news is that 25-year-old Rice is expected to be fully healthy upon his return and will be a featured target in a good offense. He has WR1 upside, but the suspension knocks him down to midround flier territory.

outlooksByWeek.1: Emeka Egbuka aims to be Tampa Bay's WR2 against the Falcons in Week 1. The rookie wide receiver has made some noise in the offseason as a top option for quarterback Baker Mayfield, and this noise could turn into some solid output especially since veteran Chris Godwin is likely to be out until October with an ankle injury. Egbuka is still set to be the number two option with Mike Evans healthy and ready to attempt another 1,000-yard campaign, but Atlanta's secondary is likely to put more emphasis on stopping Evans. This could pave the way for Egbuka to break out in his first NFL outing.
outlooksByWeek.2: Emeka Egbuka will look to build off a huge career opener as the Buccaneers travel to Houston in Week 2. Egbuka delivered on all the hype in Week 1 against the Falcons, bringing in four catches for 67 yards and two touchdowns. Both of the rookie receiver's end zone appearances came from 25-plus yard scores, meaning his big-play abilities could continue to set him apart in Tampa Bay's offense. The Texans also gave up 221 receiving yards to Rams' wide receivers in a disastrous season opener, so Egbuka will have the opportunity to tear up another secondary in his second career game.
outlooksByWeek.3: Emeka Egbuka will look to keep his touchdown streak alive as Tampa Bay takes on the Jets in Week 3. Egbuka finished the Bucs' close MNF win with just four catches for 29 yards, but he did help his performance with a touchdown. This puts him at a 7-96-3 stat line at this point in the season, which is more than satisfactory for the rookie. With Chris Godwin still sidelined, the first-round pick should continue to garner many targets from quarterback Baker Mayfield. The Jets have also given up the twelfth-most points to wide receivers so far this season, making it more likely Egbuka will deliver once again.

player.seasonOutlook: Egbuka was selected by Tampa Bay in the first round of April's draft. Whether it's size, age, 40 time or collegiate usage and efficiency, Egbuka falls right in the middle of basically every category relative to the rest of this WR class. The Ohio State product was primarily a slot (73%), short-range (8.6 aDOT) target in college, but was productive, catching 72% of his targets and posting a strong 2.64 YPRR. Also a rushing and return threat, Egbuka will have a role right out of the gate, but just how sizable it is will depend on the health of Chris Godwin (ankle). If Godwin is sidelined (and with Jalen McMillan also injured), Egbuka will be well positioned for a major early-career role that could vault him into the WR3 mix. Once Godwin is back, however, consistent fantasy output may be hard to find. Egbuka is worth a mid-round pick and is a terrific dynasty hold.

outlooksByWeek.1: Cam Skattebo comes to the New York Giants with some fanfare following an outstanding season at Arizona State. However, Skattebo missed extensive time during preseason due to injury, leaving him currently a distant third for touches out of the backfield behind Tyrone Tracy and Devin Singletary. Still, Skattebo brings a different element than either of those two rushers. If Skattebo sees touches in Week 1, a favorable matchup looms versus Washington. The Commanders were one of the worst teams in the NFL against the run in 2024, surrendering 137.5 yards per clash, which was 30th in the league. Washington also allowed 18 scores on the ground last season, tied for 18th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.2: Cam Skattebo made his presence felt on a couple of plays in the season opener for the Giants, but his opportunities were limited. Skattebo filled the hole to block a potential blitzer on one play, then broke a couple of tackles on a reception shortly thereafter. He also received a red zone carry, though was unable to find the end zone. All said, Skattebo had four touches for just nine yards in his professional debut, and remains behind Tyrone Tracy and perhaps even Devin Singletary on the depth chart. If he sees more touches in Week 2 against Dallas, he could find more room to roam, as the Cowboys allowed 158 yards and three touchdowns on the ground in their season opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Cam Skattebo found the end zone for his first NFL touchdown last game for the Giants. Skattebo finished the contest with 11 rushes for 45 yards and the score, while also catching two passes for 14 yards out of the backfield. Skattebo led all Giants running backs in touches, outpacing Tyrone Tracy (nine) and Devin Singletary (two). Skattebo already looks to be carving out a lead role in the backfield heading into a Week 3 clash with a Kansas City team that has had a tough schedule so far and is allowing 106 rushing yards per tilt, which is tied for 16th in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Skattebo was selected by the Giants in the fourth round of April's draft. He's one of the oldest RBs in this class (23), but that's not enough to offset his elite efficiency during two seasons at Arizona State. Skattebo's 3.1 forced missed tackle rate last season was best in this class (his career rate ranked second), as was his 15% target share and 11.1 yards per target. He's not super-fast, but he has good size and a three-down skill set, which supplies him with a solid long-term fantasy outlook. Of course, Skattebo is likely to split work with impressive sophomore Tyrone Tracy Jr., so his 2025 upside may be limited. He's a fine midround target.

outlooksByWeek.1: Bhayshul Tuten will make his NFL debut in Week 1 against the Panthers. The rookie fourth-round pick may not gather enough work behind Travis Etienne and Tank Bigsby to capitalize on facing a Carolina defense that allowed the most rushing yards in the NFL last season. The speedy Tuten could offer big-play potential if he cracks the rotation, as his 4.32-second 40-yard dash was the fastest in the strong 2025 RB draft class, but ball security was a major issue at Virginia Tech, as he had 10 fumbles on 428 touches the last two years. Until he earns consistent playing time, Tuten will be tough to trust in fantasy.
outlooksByWeek.2: Bhayshul Tuten's short-term fantasy potential may have gotten a significant boost after the Jaguars traded Tank Bigsby to the Eagles on Monday. Travis Etienne is the clear No. 1 RB for the Jaguars heading into a Week 2 matchup with the Bengals, but Tuten's only competition for the No. 2 role is fellow rookie LeQuint Allen. Tuten was a fourth-round pick in the 2025 NFL Draft out of Maryland, going three rounds ahead of Allen. In Week 1, Tuten had three carries for 11 yards, while Allen turned one carry and one target into 11 yards.
outlooksByWeek.3: Bhayshul Tuten has established himself as the 1B option in Jacksonville's backfield heading into a Week 3 home game against the Texans. Tuten turned 10 touches into 74 scrimmage yards and a touchdown in Week 2 against the Bengals, working behind Travis Etienne (16 touches) but well ahead of LeQuint Allen (two touches) following the trade that sent Tank Bigsby to Philadelphia. Houston has defended RBs well since the start of last season, but Tuten still makes for a passable Week 3 flex play thanks to his big-play ability. The rookie fourth-round pick out of Virginia Tech had the fastest 40-yard dash (4.32 seconds) among the 2025 RB draft class.

player.seasonOutlook: Tuten was selected by Jacksonville in the fourth round of April's draft. He struggled with negative runs (22%) and fumbles (class-high 2.5% rate) during his 24 games at Virginia Tech, but his efficiency was elite, as he ranked third in both YAC and forced missed tackle rate. He dominated the combine, posting RB-best marks in the 40 (4.32), speed score (118) and vertical (40.5). Tuten is fast, tough and has three-down ability, though his Year 1 opportunity is unclear with Travis Etienne Jr. and Tank Bigsby also on the depth chart. That could lead to a limited early-season role, but the uncertainty also allows him a chance to steal lead-back duties. Tuten is well worth a late pick, as he could eventually work his way into the RB2 discussion.

outlooksByWeek.1: Rashid Shaheed and the Saints will take on the Cardinals in Week 1. Shaheed aims to bounce back from a meniscus tear that limited him to six appearances in the 2024 season, and his speed and route-running as a healthy player should make that possible. He'll have second-year quarterback Spencer Rattler throwing the ball to him, who was unable to get things going last year. If Shaheed can stay healthy in his fourth season, he could be a consistent deep threat, contingent on whether New Orleans' quarterback room can successfully get the ball in his hands. Shaheed will start his campaign against a relatively tough secondary in the season opener.
outlooksByWeek.2: Rashid Shaheed will assume WR2 duties for the Saints in Week 2 versus the 49ers. Shaheed brought in six of his nine targets for 33 yards in New Orleans' Week 1 loss to Arizona, which ranked him third on the squad in catches and yards. The fourth-year pass catcher could continue to see high volume against San Francisco, especially with new coach Kellen Moore's pass-heavy scheme. Even though the Niners' defense was tough against wide receivers (139 yards) in their season opener, an air raid could favor Shaheed in the home game.
outlooksByWeek.3: Rashid Shaheed will continue to be a threat in the Saints' offense against the Seahawks in Week 3. Shaheed compiled four catches for 52 yards and a touchdown versus the 49ers in Week 2, putting him at 10 grabs for 85 yards and a touchdown on the year. The fourth-year wideout should continue to benefit from a New Orleans offense that has emphasized quarterback Spencer Rattler's growth as a passer. Shaheed will unfortunately take on a Seattle defense that has let up the least amount of fantasy points to wide receivers this season, but this doesn't mean he still can't be a deep threat in the away game.

player.seasonOutlook: Shaheed enters his fourth NFL season as a bit of a tricky evaluation after he was in the midst of a breakout 2024 campaign prior to suffering a season-ending knee injury in Week 6. Arguably the team's No. 1 WR to that point, Shaheed paced the Saints in targets (6.8 per game) and had also produced 29 yards on six carries. His 13.3 fantasy PPG ranked 34th among WRs and he hit the 15-point mark in four of his six games. One of the game's top deep threats and a contributor as a rusher and returner, Shaheed very well could find his way to weekly fantasy relevance in a similar way as Deebo Samuel Sr., albeit with more vertical work. Of course, he's yet to show that level of production over a full season and he'll need to fend off Chris Olave, Alvin Kamara and now Brandin Cooks for work in an offense that will have Spencer Rattler and/or rookie QB Tyler Shough under center. Shaheed is a fine late-round lottery ticket.

outlooksByWeek.1: Brandon Aubrey was one of the best kickers in the NFL last season for the Cowboys. Aubrey connected on 40 field goals; only Pittsburgh kicker Chris Boswell had more. Aubrey also hit 14 field goals of at least 50 yards, which was tops in the league. The Dallas offense returns its quarterback as well as all its playmakers on the outside, and also added the dynamic George Pickens as a deep threat. The Cowboys should be involved in their fair share of shootouts this season.  The Week 1 matchup is unkind, though; the Cowboys will face the defending champion Philadelphia Eagles on Thursday. The Eagles allowed just 17.8 points per tilt in 2024, which was second in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.2: Brandon Aubrey connected on two field goals and two extra points in the season opener for Dallas. Aubrey is an outstanding 25-of-28 on field goals of 50-plus yards for his career. Aubrey should remain busy in Week 2 versus the Giants. New York allowed 21 points in their season opener, and Aubrey connected on at least two field goals and two extra points in each of the two matchups with the G-Men last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Brandon Aubrey kicked the Dallas Cowboys to victory in Week 2. Aubrey's 64-yard field goal sent the game into overtime, while a mere 46-yarder clinched the victory over the Giants in a 40-37 thriller. Aubrey has made seven field goals thus far in 2025, five of which have come from 50-plus yards. Arguably the best kicker in football should be licking his chops ahead of a Week 3 clash with the bumbling Chicago Bears. Chicago is allowing the most points in the NFL through two contests.

player.seasonOutlook: The true shining star from the Eagles' Super Bowl LIX victory, Vic Fangio's defense features a stout secondary, All-Pro LB Zack Baun and first-round LB Jihaad Campbell, even if the unit suffered some key free agency losses (DE Josh Sweat, DT Milton Williams). After leading the league in fewest yards allowed, the Eagles will be a popular D/ST pick, but be mindful of their tough September schedule (DAL, @KC, LAR, @TB).

outlooksByWeek.1: Kayshon Boutte is flying under radars for the Patriots in advance of a Week 1 tilt with Las Vegas. New England features a crowded wide receiver room and clarity on roles is uncertain. He's a depth option for now, and facing a secondary that allowed the ninth fewest points to opposing receivers is unlikely how you'd want to set your lineup.
outlooksByWeek.2: Kayshon Boutte will look to keep a breakout campaign rolling when the Patriots head to Miami in Week 2. Boutte led the team with six catches on eight targets, finishing with 103 yards in Week 1. He closed 2024 with seven targets in two of three and 95+ yards at the same rate, and it's clear he has chemistry with budding QB Drake Maye. Maye isn't likely to throw 46 times again, but Boutte also has a high probability of being a waiver wire add this week rather than already being rostered. The floor remains low, but there are worse options than running Boutte out there as your WR3/flex option Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kayshon Boutte profiles as a volatile option in Week 3 for the Patriots against the Steelers. After shinning in his season debut, Boutte had only one target in Week 2, though it was converted for a touchdown. With Stefon Diggs continuing to gain health, Boutte seems likely to fade despite a strong snap share, suggesting he's at best a flex option against a defense that's already allowed three receivers to go for at least 90 yards against them.

outlooksByWeek.1: Harold Fannin was exceptionally productive in his final collegiate season at Bowling Green, and was selected by the Browns in the third round of the 2025 NFL Draft. There were some questions about his ability to translate his collegiate production to the pros due to him playing at a small school and questionable athleticism. However, Fannin reportedly impressed during the preseason and training camp, landing him on the radar for fantasy managers. His impact in Week 1 against the Bengals is likely to be minimal with David Njoku still ahead of him on the depth chart, but Fannin is a name worth knowing and monitoring.
outlooksByWeek.2: Harold Fannin drew strong reviews during training camp and the preseason, but it was still surprising to see him lead the Browns in targets in Week 1. He benefited from Cleveland often utilizing two tight ends, as Fannin was on the field for 72% of offensive snaps. Fannin is a must-add option, though it may be advisable to keep him on the bench for a Week 2 matchup against Baltimore to prove his showing in Week 1 was not a fluke.
outlooksByWeek.3: Harold Fannin has quickly emerged as a key contributor in the Cleveland offense, commanding 14 targets across his first two games as a pro. The state of the Cleveland offense limits his big play and touchdown upside, and a Week 3 matchup against Green Bay won't help the Browns' cause. Fannin should be a solid option due to his role, and he should be rostered in most leagues with the expectation his role and production will improve as the season progresses. In Week 3, Fannin is a borderline TE1.

player.seasonOutlook: Fannin was selected by Cleveland in the third round of April's draft. The 2024 Bowling Green offense ran through Fannin, as he handled a massive 39% of the targets and air yards. That allowed him a 117-1,555-10 receiving line on 155 targets, as well as a 3.83 YPRR. Every stat I've listed so far was the best among TEs in this class. He showed decent speed and athleticism at the combine, so along with his good hands, Fannin could emerge as a pass-catching threat in the pros. In the meantime, he'll battle for situational snaps behind starter David Njoku. Draft Fannin in dynasty leagues only.

outlooksByWeek.1: Troy Franklin was selected by the Broncos in the fourth round of the 2024 Draft, reuniting him with his college quarterback Bo Nix, but the duo's chemistry at Oregon rarely showed up as NFL rookies. Franklin struggled against the physicality of pro defenders and managed just a 28-263-2 line over 16 regular-season games, but he ended the campaign on a high note with a 43-yard TD grab in a wild-card loss to Buffalo. A Year 2 breakout is possible, but Courtland Sutton is entrenched as Nix's top option, and Franklin will face additional competition for targets on underneath routes from offseason additions Evan Engram at tight end and rookie back RJ Harvey. Franklin could struggle to make an impact in Week 1 against a stingy Titans secondary that allowed the second-fewest receiving yards in the NFL last year to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.2: Troy Franklin had an encouraging start to the season, turning six targets into four catches for 44 yards in a Week 1 win. That volume tied his highest single-game total from his rookie campaign in 2024 and suggested he's in line for a much bigger role in the Broncos' passing game as a sophomore. Franklin is still firmly behind Courtland Sutton in the pecking order for looks from quarterback Bo Nix. Franklin will look to build on his performance in Week 2's clash with a Colts secondary that completely shut down a dysfunctional Dolphins passing game in its opener, but which finished in the bottom half of the league in yards and TDs allowed to wideouts in 2024.
outlooksByWeek.3: Troy Franklin is coming off the best game of his brief NFL career, catching eight of nine targets for 89 yards and a touchdown in a Week 2 loss to the Colts. The second-year wideout has rekindled his college connection with quarterback Bo Nix while also looking more physical and capable of handling pro defenders, and a breakout campaign from Franklin would give the Broncos' passing game needed balance and depth behind Courtland Sutton. Franklin's 6.9 aDOT so far in 2025 highlights his usage primarily on underneath routes, but he did haul in a 42-yard reception on a play in which Nix bought time with his legs. Franklin isn't likely to repeat this performance in Week 3 against a Chargers secondary that just held the Raiders' Geno Smith under 200 passing yards while picking him off three times.

outlooksByWeek.1: Amon-Ra St. Brown and the Lions will kick off the season Week 1 on the road against Green Bay, who parted ways with top cornerback Jaire Alexander this offseason. Concerns about Detroit's efficiency on offense are valid - the team lost two of last year's starters along the O-line, as well as former OC Ben Johnson, but St. Brown has been one of the league's most consistent producers since entering the league as a fourth-round pick in 2021, with three consecutive 1,000-yard seasons under his belt, and back-to-back years with double-digit TDs. The Packers ranked third against the pass last season, though, and even without Alexander in the secondary, the addition of All-Pro pass rusher Micah Parsons presents a new challenge for Jared Goff and the aerial attack. As such, to start the year, it wouldn't be surprising for St. Brown, Jameson Williams and TE Sam LaPorta to take a slight backseat, while RBs Jahmyr Gibbs and David Montgomery lead the gameplan on offense.
outlooksByWeek.2: Amon-Ra St. Brown and the Lions will host the Bears in Week 2, as he aims to build on a modest Week 1 performance. He caught four passes on six targets for 45 yards in Detroit's opener, a quiet start but one that belies his central role in Jared Goff's passing game. St. Brown lines up predominantly in the slot, which gives him a potential mismatch against the Bears' less experienced interior corners, leaving Jameson Williams to contend more directly with Jaylon Johnson. With defensive attention further spread by Jahmyr Gibbs and David Montgomery in the backfield, St. Brown should be poised for a bounce-back performance with new OC John Morton extra motivated to prove the departure of Ben Johnson (to Chicago) hasn't left him outmatched.
outlooksByWeek.3: Amon-Ra St. Brown and the Lions travel to Baltimore in Week aA�3, coming off a monster 52-21 win over the Bears in Week 2 in which he hauled in nine receptions for 113 yards and three touchdowns. He also rushed twice for seven yards in the blowout win, while definitively leading the team in terms of catches, targets, receiving yards and scores. St. Brown dominated coverage with crisp route running and strong hands, showing his ability to be a true field-stretching threat even with the defense keying on him. Baltimore presents a more disciplined secondary, but St. Brown's volume and red-zone usage make him a high-end WR1, especially following a convincing demonstration that the departure of OC Ben Johnson hasn't detracted from his high-end upside.

player.seasonOutlook: St. Brown enters his fifth NFL campaign as the only player in the league with 105 or more receptions each of the past three seasons. Compared to 2023, St. Brown actually saw a decrease in targets, receptions and yards last season, but offset some of that with a career-high 12 touchdowns and still finished as the No. 3 fantasy WR for the second year in a row. He remains an elite, short-range target, having paced qualified wide receivers in catch rate (81%) in 2024 and having now ranked top 5 in first downs per route run for the third year in a row. The 25-year-old is a heavily utilized target in one of the league's best offenses and a clear top-5 fantasy wide receiver.

outlooksByWeek.1: Josh Jacobs and the Packers will kick off the 2025 season with a tough Week 1 home game against the reigning division champion Lions. Coming off debut season in Green Bay in which he scored a career-high 16 touchdowns, Jacobs remains entrenched in a workhorse backfield role, with returning backups Emanuel Wilson and Chris Brooks not a threat for more than change-of-pace touches, and MarShawn Lloyd (groin) on IR for at least four weeks. Jacobs topped 20 touches in more than half of his appearances last season (playoffs included) and is a leading candidate to be the centerpiece of coach Matt LaFleur's offensive gameplan for Week 1, given that wideouts Jayden Reed (foot) and Dontayvion Wicks (calf) missed significant time this preseason and may not be 100 percent even if they suit up versus Detroit.
outlooksByWeek.2: Josh Jacobs and the Packers will take on the Commanders in Week 2, as he looks to extend his rushing touchdown streak to 10 straight games. His three-yard plunge in Week 1 gave him nine consecutive games with a rushing score, setting a franchise record. Jacobs logged 66 yards on 19 carries plus one catch for four yards in Green Bay's opener, proving he's again entrenched the team's bell-cow back. Washington held the Giants' backfield to just 30 combined rushing yards last week, but that came more from penetration and game script than sheer run-gap control. Jacobs' usage and red-zone dominance keep him locked in as a high-end RB1 despite the matchup and short week of rest before Thursday Night Football.
outlooksByWeek.3: Josh Jacobs and the Packers head to Cleveland in Week 3, looking to stay undefeated after he handled a true workhorse role in the team's Week 2 win over the Commanders. Jacobs logged 23 carries for 84 yards and a touchdown, giving him rushing scores in 10 straight games dating back to last season. The Browns' defensive front is far stingier than Washington's, but Jacobs' volume remains matchup-proof as he's dominated nearly every backfield touch for Green Bay. No other running back got a chance to handle a carry versus Washington, though Chris Brooks contributed in the receiving game on third downs. It does cap Jacobs' ceiling, however, that he's now only been targeted once through two regular-season games.

player.seasonOutlook: Jacobs' first season in Green Bay was about as good as it gets, as the ex-Raider finished no lower than sixth among RBs in carries, rushing yards, carries inside the 5, touches, scrimmage yards, touchdowns and fantasy points. His season started somewhat quietly, but he dominated once temperatures dropped and went on to find the end zone in eight straight games to finish the regular season. Jacobs also contributed in the passing game (15th among RBs in receiving yards) and has now finished all six NFL seasons 18th or better in fantasy PPG. Green Bay's feature back remains in his prime at age 27 and makes for a solid fantasy RB1.

outlooksByWeek.1: George Kittle is healthy and wealthy for the 49ers' Week 1 matchup against Seattle after signing a big four-year contract extension in the offseason. Kittle's role as a pass catcher should be intensified early on with WR Brandon Aiyuk (ACL) on the PUP list to begin the campaign and Jauan Jennings (calf, contract) uncertain to suit up against the Seahawks. Kittle is coming off a 78-catch, 1,106-yard, eight-TD 2024 campaign, further cementing his place as one of the NFL's elite producers at tight end. The Seahawks were middle-of-the-pack against the position last year, giving up an average of 51.5 receiving yards per game.
outlooksByWeek.2: George Kittle won't play in San Francisco's Week 2 matchup against New Orleans due to a hamstring injury that landed him on IR. Luke Farrell and Jake Tonges, who caught a TD in Kittle's absence last week against the Seahawks, will be asked to step in at tight end for the 49ers.
outlooksByWeek.3: George Kittle will miss his second straight game for the 49ers in Week 3 against the Cardinals while he remains on IR due to a hamstring injury. Jake Tonges and Luke Farrell should continue to hold down the fort at TE for Kittle until the latter is able to return. Kittle won't be eligible to suit up again until Week 6.

player.seasonOutlook: Kittle has finished sixth or better in fantasy PPG each of the past seven years. That includes a first-place finish in 2024 (15.8 PPG), which was fueled by an incredible 13 weeks in the top 12 among TEs in 14 full games. Kittle has paced the position in yards per reception, yards per target and yards per route run each of the past two seasons and has finished exactly second in touchdowns three years in a row. With Deebo Samuel Sr. traded and Brandon Aiyuk (knee) expected to miss significant game action, Kittle has a case to be the top tight end off the board on draft day entering his ninth NFL season.

outlooksByWeek.1: Chuba Hubbard should command the lion's share of rushes in Carolina's backfield for Week 1 versus Jacksonville. Hubbard was a star for the Panthers last season, finishing the season with 250 rushes for 1,195 rushing yards and 10 touchdowns. His efforts netted him a contract extension, which should mean a prominent role once again. The Jaguars were also one of the worst teams against fantasy running backs last campaign, which gives Hubbard a path to a dominant season opener.
outlooksByWeek.2: Chuba Hubbard should be the workhorse running back once again as the Panthers travel to Arizona in Week 2. Carolina all-out struggled against the Jaguars in their season opener, but Hubbard's role in the backfield stayed consistent. The 26-year-old registered 16 carries for 57 yards and grabbed three of his five targets for 32 yards and a touchdown. The next closest running back to Hubbard was Rico Dowdle, who had just three carries for 12 yards and two catches for four yards. Hubbard ended the game with 14 more touches, showing that he no doubt has command of the backfield. The fifth-year RB should have a chance for a bit more output, at least on the ground, against a Cardinals defense that gave up 78 rushing yards and a touchdown to New Orleans running backs in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chuba Hubbard will look to command more carries with Carolina in a Week 3 tilt versus Atlanta. Hubbard rushed just 10 times for 38 yards this past weekend against Arizona, putting him at another sub-par rushing performance. The fifth year luckily salvaged his performance with a receiving touchdown just like in Week 1, but these end zone grabs won't be able to save him forever. Hubbard will still garner almost all of the Panthers' backfield carries again versus a Falcons defense that has given up the fifth-least fantasy points to running backs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Hubbard signed a contract extension with Carolina last season, which locked him in as the team's lead back for the near future. The 2021 fourth-round pick has amassed 275-plus touches in each of the past two seasons and, despite missing two games in 2024, he finished in the top 15 among RBs in carries, targets, touches, yards, touchdowns and fantasy points. He ran well (4.8 YPC) and was busy near the goal line (he ranked fifth with 17 carries inside the 5-yard line), but he struggled as a receiver (RB-worst 3.2 YPT). With Jonathon Brooks (ACL) out for the entire 2025 season, Rico Dowdle and rookie Trevor Etienne are Hubbard's primary competition for touches. The 26-year-old makes for a solid RB2 target.

outlooksByWeek.1: Baker Mayfield will look to expand on a career-best 2024 season as the Buccaneers take on the Falcons in Week 1. The veteran quarterback essentially saved his career in 2023 and only got better in 2024, with 4,500 passing yards and a 41:16 TD:INT. Mayfield will be facing one of the better defenses in the NFL against quarterbacks last year, but that shouldn't be too much of a problem given his tools. Even though he likely won't have veteran wide receiver Chris Godwin as a target, he'll add rookie wide receivers Emeka Egbuka and Tez Johnson to his pool of pass catchers. These new additions, along with a consistent Mike Evans, tight end Cade Otton, and a dominant run game, should give Atlanta's defense problems. The only worry is that Mayfield may not match his previous two seasons, but his supporting cast and continuous reliability should at least set him up for another productive season.
outlooksByWeek.2: Baker Mayfield will look to put together a more efficient showing as Tampa Bay takes on the Texans in Week 2. Mayfield was by no means bad in his season-opening win versus the Falcons, but he paired his impressive three touchdowns with just 167 passing yards and a 53 percent completion rate. The Bucs' pass catchers still showed flashes of greatness, though, with rookie Emeka Egbuka already establishing a connection with the starting quarterback and Mike Evans still being a consistent target. These flashes have the potential to give Mayfield all the tools he needs to succeed against a Houston defense that let Matthew Stafford throw for 245 passing yards and finish with a 72 percent completion rate last week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Baker Mayfield will look to put together his first consistent game of the year as the Buccaneers play the Jets in Week 3. Mayfield ended up with 215 passing yards and two touchdowns versus the Texans in Week 2, but this wasn't before struggling during all of the game except the fourth quarter. The veteran quarterback now has back-to-back games with volatile performances, even though both still ended up satisfactory. Mayfield will take his 60.0 completion percentage and 5:0 TD:INT into a home matchup versus a middle-of-the-pack New York defense against quarterbacks.

player.seasonOutlook: Mayfield may have enjoyed his career renaissance in 2023, but he had his fantasy breakout in 2024. After finishing 18th or worse in fantasy PPG during each of his first six NFL seasons, Mayfield leapt to fourth in 2024. He finished no lower than fifth in pass attempts, completions, yards and TDs, while also easily posting a career high in rush yards. Mayfield completed 71% of his passes (third best) despite missing Chris Godwin and Mike Evans for chunks of the season, and he may be in even better shape in 2025 with Evans back, Godwin hopefully healthy and youngsters Emeka Egbuka and Jalen McMillan also in the mix. Mayfield benefits from a Bucs offense that has scored a league-high 76.6% of its TDs through the air since Todd Bowles became head coach in 2022. With consecutive seasons of good play under his belt, the 30-year-old is well positioned for another solid QB1 fantasy campaign.

outlooksByWeek.1: Tetairoa McMillan is set to make his NFL debut for Carolina in Week 1 against the Jaguars. McMillan is currently dealing with a hamstring injury, but he should be able to make it onto the field for the season opener. The rookie wide receiver aims to be quarterback Bryce Young's top option this campaign. The wideout is unproven at the pro level with a quarterback that hasn't established himself yet, but a shaky Jags secondary could be all McMillan needs to start out his career with a bang.
outlooksByWeek.2: Tetairoa McMillan should be the top target in the Panthers' passing game once again versus the Cardinals in Week 2. McMillan was one of the only bright spots for Carolina in a tough season-opening loss to Jacksonville, reeling in five catches for 68 yards. The rookie wide receiver and quarterback Bryce Young looked to have some sparks of a connection, one of which can definitely be ignited against Arizona. McMillan's output for his second NFL game also looks more favorable, considering the Cards gave up 17 catches for 126 yards to Saints wide receivers in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tetairoa McMillan enters Week 3 against the Falcons as the top target in Carolina's passing game. In just his second game of his NFL career, McMillan already recorded a 100-yard performance. The rookie wideout has now led his team in targets and yardage in back-to-back weeks, making him Bryce Young's most trusted target. The Falcons also rank middle-of-the-pack against wide receivers so far this season, which could benefit McMillan in the upcoming home game.

player.seasonOutlook: McMillan was selected by Carolina with the eighth pick of April's draft. At 6-foot-4, 219 pounds, he is one of the biggest WRs in this class and his game has led to many Drake London comps. McMillan handled a massive 34% target share and class-high 52% air yard share last season at Arizona. His elite size and ball skills combo supplies him with big-time fantasy upside and, with Xavier Legette and Jalen Coker as his top competition for work, he's well positioned for a sizable rookie-season role. McMillan should be valued as a WR2/3.

outlooksByWeek.1: Jacory Croskey-Merritt, affectionately known as Bill, might be the surprise of the preseason in Washington. The Commanders traded last year's starting running back Brian Robinson, leaving Bill and Austin Ekeler as the primary beneficiaries. The rookie was a seventh round pick in the 2025 draft but impressed in camp, so much so that the Commanders felt confident to let Robinson go. In Week 1, Bill may still split touches with Ekeler against the Giants, though the latter should be used more in passing situations. In Week 1, the Commanders will face a Giants run defense that was gutted in 2024 on the ground to the tune of 136.2 yards per tilt, which was 27th in the NFL. However, the Giants drafted Abdul Carter at No. 3 to help shore up the defensive line, so that unit could be better this season.
outlooksByWeek.2: Jacory McCroskey-Merritt outperformed starter Austin Ekeler in Week 1 for the Commanders. Ekeler rushed six times for 26 yards, while McCroskey-Merritt racked up 82 yards and a touchdown on 10 carries. Naturally, Ekeler made more of an impact in the passing game, reeling in three passes for 31 yards, but it would not be surprising to see the rookie overtake Ekeler as the early-down back in Week 2 against the Packers. Unfortunately, the matchup is stiff for whomever touches the ball out of the backfield, as Green Bay allowed a league-low 46 yards rushing in their season opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jacory Croskey-Merritt was largely held in check in Week 2 for the Commanders, but many more opportunities could be coming his way. Austin Ekeler tore his Achilles in the loss to the Packers, while quarterback Jayden Daniels has been deemed day-to-day with a knee injury. This news could open the floodgates for Croskey-Merritt, who already looked ticketed for a decent role prior to both of these injuries. If Daniels is sidelined, the Commanders could rely even more on the running game, which would certainly aid the rookie affectionately called Bill. Unfortunately, in Week 3, the Commanders will face a Raiders defense that has been stout against the run this season, allowing just 70.5 yards per game on the ground, which is fourth in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Croskey-Merritt was selected by Washington in the seventh round after spending six seasons at the collegiate level. After four seasons at Alabama State, he had his breakout season at New Mexico in 2023 prior to appearing in only one game in 2024. Croskey-Merritt is an older back with limited recent playing time, but he posted elite efficiency in 2023 and showed so well during the offseason that Washington shipped lead rusher Brian Robinson Jr. to the 49ers in August. Despite being a late-round pick and the presence of passing-down specialist Austin Ekeler, "Bill" has a legitimate shot to lead Washington's backfield as a rookie, which presents plenty of fantasy appeal. He should be on your radar in the middle rounds.

outlooksByWeek.1: Travis Hunter is poised to play a key role in Week 1 against the Panthers after the Jaguars traded up to select him second overall in the 2025 NFL Draft out of Colorado. The unique talent will contribute on offense as a WR and on defense as a CB, though Hunter is expected to get more offensive playing time. The extra defensive reps create conditioning concerns and a higher risk of injury, but Hunter's offensive contributions could be significant nonetheless, and he projects to start at WR right away across from Brian Thomas. Carolina allowed 21 TD catches to WRs in 2024, second-most in the NFL, so Hunter is a viable fantasy WR3 for Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.2: Travis Hunter focused primarily on offense in his NFL debut last week, playing 39 snaps at wide receiver and only six defensive snaps. Working primarily as a wideout, Hunter has a high Week 2 ceiling against an underwhelming Bengals defense. The rookie second overall pick was held in check by an underrated Panthers secondary in Week 1, mustering only six catches for 33 yards on a team-high eight targets. His involvement in the Jaguars' offense was encouraging, and Hunter's a high-end fantasy WR3 for Week 2 as his role continues to come into focus.
outlooksByWeek.3: Travis Hunter ranks second on the Jaguars behind Brian Thomas with 14 targets through two games, but the rookie second overall pick has produced only 55 receiving yards with that volume. A Week 3 visit from the Texans could help Hunter break out, as Houston allowed the second-most receiving TDs to wide receivers (21) last season. Hunter's defensive responsibilities increased in the Week 2 loss to the Bengals after minimal usage on that side in Week 1, but he looks capable of handling a decent workload on offense despite playing both sides of the ball, so Hunter is in the fantasy WR3/flex mix for Week 3.

player.seasonOutlook: If your league counts his receiving stats as well, be aggressive in pursuing this unique playmaker whose potential for splash plays could reshape the landscape. If not, he's likely unusable as a part-time DB.

outlooksByWeek.1: Jordan Mason's debut in Minnesota's backfield will come Week 1 on the road against a Bears defense that ranked 30th against the run last season. At 223 pounds, Mason is better built for a workhorse between-the-tackles role than incumbent starter Aaron Jones, a 210-pound finesse runner fresh off a season in which he handled a career-high 225 carries. On paper, a backfield split in which Jones dominates pass-catching work and carries between the 20s, while Mason is favored in short-yardage areas and near the goal line,  seems an almost foregone conclusion. It's possible, though, that coach Kevin O'Connell also intends to deploy more power-running concepts than he did in 2024, a development that would suit Mason's skill set more than Jones'.
outlooksByWeek.2: Jordan Mason will figure to again lead Minnesota's backfield in a Week 2 primetime matchup against the Falcons. He rushed 15 times for 68 yards in the team's Week 1 win over the Bears, comfortably out-pacing veteran backfield mate Aaron Jones (eight carries for 23 yards). It was Jones, however, who thrived through the air, bringing in all three of his targets for 44 yards and a score, while Mason was limited to seven yards on his only target. The Vikings appear to be relying on Mason to grind out ugly yards while Jones handles a solid complementary role. Such a split will favor Mason in terms of production if Minnesota can get out to an early lead versus Atlanta, while Jones will have a clearer path to explosive games when the team has to embrace a high pace of play and chase a deficit, as was the case versus Chicago.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jordan Mason and the Vikings will travel to Cincinnati in Week 3 after a 22-6 loss to the Falcons. He carried the ball nine times for 30 yards and added two catches for eight yards (three targets) during the primetime loss to Atlanta, a game that saw Aaron Jones depart in the fourth quarter due to a hamstring injury. Already the favorite for early-down and short-yardage work, Mason will figure to inherit a workhorse role if Jones is forced to miss time, which seems to be the expectation for Week 3. With J.J. McCarthy (ankle) a candidate to sit out as well, Mason is facing a favorable matchup that could see Minnesota lean heavily on the ground game versus a Bengals defense surrendering the 20th-most fantasy points per game to opposing backfields (22.5).

player.seasonOutlook: Mason was traded to Minnesota and is expected to operate in a committee with Aaron Jones. The 2022 UDFA was terrific in limited work during his three seasons in San Francisco. His 5.31 YPC ranks fourth and his 2.49 YAC is the best among RBs with 200-plus carries since he entered the league. Mason is 26 years old with 250 career touches and is a nonfactor as a receiver (career 14-121-0 line on 18 targets), but he should push for roughly half of Minnesota's carries, with Jones handling the passing-down work. Mason doesn't figure to provide standalone fantasy value and is best valued as an insurance hold for your bench.

outlooksByWeek.1: Zach Charbonnet finished last season as Seattle's lead RB, but he'll likely be more of a 1B or No. 2 option Week 1 versus San Francisco. That's because Kenneth Walker is back in the fold after sitting out four of the last five games last year due to injury. Charbonnet was impressive while stepping in during that span, averaging 5.0 YPC and scoring three touchdowns, so he could be given an increased role even when Walker is healthy this season. In the Seahawks' regular-season opener, the duo will square off against a 49ers defense that surrendered 4.3 YPC to RBs last year.
outlooksByWeek.2: Zach Charbonnet could further push to work as the top RB option for Seattle against the Steelers in Week 2. On Sunday against San Francisco, Charbonnet actually outcarried presumed starter Kenneth Walker 12-10 while outgaining him on the ground by a 47-20 tally. Should Charbonnet similarly outshine Walker in Week 2, he could strengthen his case to see more work out of the backfield. The Steelers weren't effective against the run in their Week 1 win, yielding 182 yards on the ground the Jets, 107 of which was gained by starting RB Breece Hall.
outlooksByWeek.3: Zach Charbonnet will look to bounce back from a rough Week 2 when Seattle faces New Orleans in Week 3. Charbonnet managed just 10 yards on 15 carries against Pittsburgh on Sunday, and though he out-carried backfield mate Kenneth Walker, the latter was much more productive with 13 totes for 105 yards and a touchdown. Charbonnet and Walker seem likely to continue splitting touches fairly evenly, though one of the two could separate himself in time. The Saints held San Francisco's Christian McCaffrey to a modest 55 rushing yards on 13 carries in Week 2 but allowed him to go off for 52 yards and a touchdown on six catches.

player.seasonOutlook: Charbonnet is entering his third NFL season and is expected to remain the primary backup to Kenneth Walker III. Charbonnet got some run as Seattle's lead back last season and showed well. In the six games Walker missed, he averaged 18.3 touches and 19.2 fantasy points per game. Despite the success, Charbonnet was the clear No. 2 the 11 weeks Walker played, averaging 6.1 touches (10 max) and 6.5 fantasy points (12.1 max). Charbonnet is a young (24), high-pedigree (second-round) back who has played well, so perhaps new OC Klint Kubiak will give him more run. It is best to treat him as an elite insurance bench hold.

outlooksByWeek.1: Tyler Allgeier opens the 2024 season as Bijan Robinson's primary backup in a Week 1 matchup against the Buccaneers. Robinson had most of Atlanta's backfield touches and passing game involvement as a RB last season, and that is not set to change this campaign. Allgeier did still prove to be a skilled back when needed last year, but the skills of his teammate have been shown to be more effective against defenses in the NFL. This makes Allgeier not likely to have a huge impact fantasy-wise this season or against a tough Tampa Bay front, unless Robinson were to suffer an injury.
outlooksByWeek.2: Tyler Allgeier will aim to register meaningful carries for the Falcons in Week 2 against the Vikings. Allgeier finished with just two fewer carries than star rusher Bijan Robinson against the Buccaneers in Week 1, but Robinson outpaced his backfield mate with seven more targets in the passing game. This makes it very likely that Allgeier's role moving forward will be as a supplementary rusher. He should still register a solid number of carries in Minnesota, against a defense that gave up 119 total rushing yards to the Bears in Monday Night Football.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tyler Allgeier will look to eat into carries once again as the Falcons travel to Carolina for Week 3. Atlanta led Minnesota during all of their Week 2 win, so Allgeier got an uptick in carries and ended the game with 16 rushes for 76 yards and a touchdown.  The fourth-year running back was the only rusher to score a touchdown in the whole game, but he did so likely because of the nature of the game. Allgeier still appears to be levels behind star Bijan Robinson at this point in the season, both as a ball carrier and pass catcher. This means a game script similar to the dominance over Minnesota will be needed for Allgeier to be relevant against a middle-of-the-pack Panthers defense.

player.seasonOutlook: Allgeier is entering his fourth NFL season, including his third straight as Bijan Robinson's backup/running mate. With Robinson taking on a larger role in 2024, Allgeier hit career-low marks in snap share (28%), carries (137) and targets (13). He cleared 12 touches only once (an 18-point win in Week 6), which was also his only game with more than 12.3 fantasy points. The 25-year-old clearly has no standalone fantasy value and, though he's limited as a pass catcher, he'd certainly be positioned for a hefty chunk of Atlanta's carries in the event of a Robinson injury. Allgeier is a fine late-round insurance flier.

outlooksByWeek.1: Ray Davis' volume is questionable entering Buffalo's Week 1 matchup against Baltimore. Davis has shown flashes when given a full set of snaps but remains the second option behind James Cook when both are healthy. He handled just 11 touches in two meetings with the Ravens last season and is facing a defense that allowed a mere 3.6 yards per carry a year ago, there's unlikely to be enough work for Davis to have flex appeal.
outlooksByWeek.2: Ray Davis faces an uncertain role when the Bills visit the Jets in Week 2. Davis had just one touch to open the season, while co-backup Ty Johnson turned four touches into 78 yards, with Johnson featured in passing situations. Davis is best considered more of an insurance policy to James Cook than even a deep fantasy option.
outlooksByWeek.3: Ray Davis' usage appears minimal for the Bills entering a Week 3 matchup with the Dolphins on Thursday night. He logged just two touches in their nail-biting opener, and collected nine carries in a Week 2 blowout, averaging just 2.7 yards per carry. While arguably one of the better backups to roster, Davis has minimal weekly appeal so long as James Cook remains healthy.

player.seasonOutlook: Davis is entering his second season after soaking up 130 touches as a rookie last season. The fourth-round pick essentially split change-of-pace duties with Ty Johnson behind lead back James Cook. Davis played 24% of the snaps on the season and averaged 7.6 touches per game. He cleared 12 touches only twice (Cook was out or limited for both) and was impressive (152 yards in Week 6, 65 yards and one TD in Week 18). The 25-year-old was effective as both a rusher and receiver and, as we saw in a small sample last season, he'd likely be Buffalo's lead back (with Johnson also plenty involved) in the event of a Cook injury. That makes him a valuable insurance back worth consideration in the late rounds.

outlooksByWeek.1: Evan McPherson and the Bengals agreed to an extension ahead of the 2024 season, but he went on to endure his worst campaign as a pro. He converted only 73% of his field-goal attempts, including just six of 13 from 40 yards or more. McPherson reportedly went back to his original kicking motion this offseason, and he'll be an elite option if he can regain his accuracy thanks to Cincinnati's explosive offense. McPherson is a risky starting option in Week1 against Cleveland, but he is a viable low-end starter.
outlooksByWeek.2: Evan McPherson was asked to do a limited amount in Week 1, but he did provide the game-winning kick for Cincinnati with a 35-yard field goal in the third quarter. After making only 73% of his field goals in 2024, it was an encouraging start to the new campaign for McPherson. He should be considered as a decent fantasy option in Week 2 against Jacksonville, because the Cincinnati offense should get back on track to create more opportunities for him.
outlooksByWeek.3: Evan McPherson has been accurate to begin the season, making a pair of field goals and all six of his extra points. However, he has yet to be tested from distance, with both of his field-goal attempts coming from between 30 and 39 yards. The Cincinnati offense is likely to take a step back with Jake Browning under center, in turn limiting McPherson's opportunity. McPherson has decent floor heading into a Week 3 matchup against Minnesota, but there should be better kicking options available.

outlooksByWeek.1: Will Shipley will battle with AJ Dillon for backup touches behind Saquon Barkley as the Eagles ring in the new football season in Week 1 versus the Dallas Cowboys.  Dallas was one of the worst teams in the NFL last year against the run, allowing 137.1 yards per tilt on the ground, which was 29th in the league. In addition, Dallas allowed 25 rushing scores, which was the worst mark in the NFL. This game has the chance to get out of hand quickly, especially with Dallas recently trading Micah Parsons, meaning Shipley could see a few extra opportunities.
outlooksByWeek.2: Will Shipley carried the ball three times for 26 yards in the season opener for the Eagles. Unfortunately, he also suffered a rib injury, leaving his status in doubt as Saquon Barkley's backup for Week 2 against Kansas City. If Shipley cannot suit up, AJ Dillon would slide into the No. 2 role, and the Eagles acquired Tank Bigsby from the Jaguars to provide additional backfield depth as well. Dillon rushed three times for 10 yards in his Eagles debut. Kansas City has been stingy against the run the last few seasons, and allowed just 90 yards rushing in Week 1 versus the Chargers.
outlooksByWeek.3: Will Shipley missed Week 2 for the Eagles due to an oblique injury, and given the nature of the ailment, it would appear unlikely he will be able to suit up in Week 3 versus the Rams either. In Shipley's absence, AJ Dillon handled backup duties to Saquon Barkley, though managed just three carries for 19 yards in the 20-17 win over Kansas City. If Shipley defies the odds and appears in uniform, he would be facing a Rams defense allowing 111.5 rushing yards per contest, which is tied for 18th in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Shipley is entering his second NFL season in position to earn the primary backup role behind Saquon Barkley. With Barkley dominating the touches and Kenneth Gainwell second in line for work, the 2024 fourth-round pick was limited to 34 touches in 16 games as a rookie, 14 of which came with the starters resting in Week 18. Granted it was a small sample, but Shipley wasn't overly effective (2.7 YPC), which aligns with his underwhelming collegiate efficiency. Still, with Gainwell now in Pittsburgh, Shipley has an opportunity to lock down one of the league's best insurance jobs. Should Barkley miss time, the 23-year-old would likely see enough work behind an elite line in a high-scoring offense to allow RB2/flex production. Shipley makes for a fine late-round dart throw.

outlooksByWeek.1: Amari Cooper is coming off his worst NFL season, playing 14 regular-season games between the Browns and Bills but managing just a 44-547-4 line on 85 targets. The 31-year-old could be approaching the end of his career, but the Raiders elected to give him a chance to bounce back, signing him to a one-year contract late in August after contract extension talks with Jakobi Meyers failed to go anywhere. Cooper will need to some time to ramp up, but a return to something close to his prior form would give Las Vegas the option to trade Meyers if necessary. Cooper will likely have a small role in Week 1 against a Patriots secondary that finished in the top half of the league in 2024 in receiving yards and TDs allowed to wideouts.

player.seasonOutlook: Cooper reunited with the Raiders in August. The 10-year vet came out of the gate averaging a career-high 27.5% target share (8.8 per game) with Cleveland last season, but Deshaun Watson's struggled allowed Cooper one showing over 10 fantasy points. He was then traded to Buffalo and his playing time and production were all over the map (three games with 14-plus fantasy points, but fewer than 8.0 in the other six). Prior to what was essentially a lost 2024 season, Cooper had finished no better than 14th and no worse than 32nd in fantasy PPG in his first nine seasons. Now 31 years old, it's possible he has another year of fantasy relevance left in the tank, but he'll be no higher than third in target priority behind Brock Bowers and Jakobi Meyers. Cooper is an acceptable late round flier in deeper leagues.

outlooksByWeek.1: Juwan Johnson is set to lead New Orleans' tight end room in Week 1 against Arizona. Johnson delivered career highs in targets (66), catches (50) and receiving yards (548) last season but he only found the end zone three times. Johnson faces little competition for snaps with Foster Moreau and Taysom Hill both sidelined to begin the season and could be a top target for starting quarterback Spencer Rattler, especially if deeper throws aren't available against a solid Cardinals secondary.
outlooksByWeek.2: Juwan Johnson will look to be a top option in the Saints' passing game in a Week 2 matchup versus the 49ers. Johnson ended up being the leading receiver for New Orleans in a season-opening loss to the Cardinals, with eight catches for 76 yards. This yardage eclipsed all but one of his outings last season, showing that he could be poised for a big role in new coach Kellen Moore's pass-heavy offense this season. San Francisco did give up just two receptions for seven yards to Seahawks tight ends in Week 1, but Johnson's looks from quarterback Spencer Rattler could still keep him relevant in the upcoming home game.
outlooksByWeek.3: Juwan Johnson should be a top target in the Saints' offense once again at Seattle in Week 3. Johnson amassed five catches for 49 yards and a touchdown this past week versus the 49ers, putting him at 13 grabs for 125 yards and one touchdown on the year. The starting tight end has been a safety outlet so far for quarterback Spencer Rattler, and the team doesn't look to be slowing down the pass attack any time soon. The Seahawks also gave up seven receptions for 58 yards to Steelers tight ends in Week 2, which could give Johnson another big effort in the away matchup.

player.seasonOutlook: Johnson returns for his sixth season in New Orleans after a solid 2024 showing in which he set career highs in catches and yardage while appearing in every regular-season game for the first time in his career. The converted wide receiver has finished between 18th and 26th in fantasy PPG each of the past three seasons, though it's notable that he saw a boost in usage and production following Taysom Hill's injury late last season (12-plus points in three of his final five games). Hill is a long shot to play in 2025, though the team will be in better shape at wide receiver with a healthy Chris Olave and Rashid Shaheed, as well as newcomer Brandin Cooks. Playing with rookie QB Tyler Shough and/or Spencer Rattler, Johnson, 28, is no more than a fringe TE2.

Lou Anarumo comes over from the Bengals to serve as the defensive coordinator for a Colts team that has the beginnings of a strong defensive front with DT DeForest Buckner and DE Laiatu Latu, and added free agents S Camryn Bynum and CB Charvarius Ward to bolster what was a weak secondary. There's enough talent here to make the Colts a decent matchups play, and bear in mind that they have one of the position's more favorable schedules. Watch their performances in the first two weeks and consider adding them for Week 3 (@TEN).

outlooksByWeek.1: Jahmyr Gibbs and co-starter David Montgomery will work to reprise as the league's most effective backfield duo, beginning Week 1 on the road against Green Bay. New OC John Morton spent the offseason emphasizing Gibbs' pass-catching abilities, even splitting him out wide at practices, and after the 2023 third-round pick's truly dominant performance as a workhorse from Week 13 onward last season, when Montgomery went down to an MCL injury, Detroit could be motivated to feature him more heavily than in an actual even split. While the loss of Ben Johnson figures to detract from the Lions' overall efficiency on offense, and the offseason retirement of C Frank Ragnow will be difficult to overcome, Gibbs remains in prime position to repeat as one of the league's most productive ball carriers. He and Montgomery could be the feature of the Lions' gameplan Week 1, as Green Bay ranked third in the league against the pass last season but middle-of-the-road against the run.
outlooksByWeek.2: Jahmyr Gibbs and David Montgomery will work to return to their usual form as a dominant Lions backfield duo in Week 2 versus the Bears. Detroit's offense as a whole will be working to bounce back after an embarrassing Week 1 showing against the Packers' defense, though it was particularly surprising to see Gibbs turn nine carries and 10 targets into just 50 scoreless yards. His 31 receiving yards were, in fact, an NFL record as the lowest total yardage a player has managed on 10 or more targets, and his 2.1 YPC mark was worse than any single game of his 2024 season, playoffs included. Gibbs and Montgomery split carries essentially evenly, and while Gibbs projects for more work in the receiving game, he's only logged double-digit targets on one other occasion in his career. He'll need to return his usual hallmark efficiency versus Chicago in order to return on his expectations as a top-five fantasy draft pick.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jahmyr Gibbs and the Lions travel to Baltimore in Week aA�3, coming off a big 52-21 win over the Bears in WeekaA�2 where he totaled 12 carries for 94 yards and one touchdown, adding three receptions for 10 yards through the air. The electric running back showcased his usual dynamic playmaking ability, an encouraging development after he (along with the rest of Detroit's offense) was held in check by Green Bay in Week 1.
