The Ravens' front seven is more stout than Chicago's, but Gibbs' versatility and playmaking skills give him a clear path to RB1 value, particularly in PPR formats if the Lions are forced to rely on him more on early downs versus a Baltimore secondary better capable of containing Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams.

player.seasonOutlook: The reigning No. 1 fantasy RB, Gibbs scored a position-high 20 TDs while dominating as both a rusher (fifth in yards) and receiver (top six in targets, catches and yards) last season. The with/without David Montgomery splits are notable here, however, as Gibbs averaged 16.3 touches and 18.2 fantasy points per game (sixth best) in 13 games with a healthy Montgomery, but 22.5 touches and 31.5 points per game (first) without. Montgomery is back, so Gibbs' touch ceiling may be slightly lower than a few other top backs, but with his skill set and Detroit's high-powered offense, he's undoubtedly a strong fantasy RB1. The 23-year-old should be one of the first players off the board on draft day.

outlooksByWeek.1: James Cook's 2025 season could begin slowly with the Bills hosting the Ravens in Week 1. Baltimore's defense allowed just 3.6 yards per carry last season, and Cook gained just 106 yards on 26 carries while failing to score a touchdown against them despite leading the league in rushing scores. Touchdown regression is likely coming for Cook and Josh Allen is always a threat to vulture scores, perhaps slotting Cook more into flex territory rather than a solid RB2 option.
outlooksByWeek.2: James Cook will look to build on his solid opener when the Bills face the Jets in Week 2. Cook averaged just 3.4 yards per carry in Week 1, but he added five catches for 58 yards and got into the end zone, which was his leading fantasy appeal last season. The Jets defense held up well against the Steelers last week, allowing just 2.8 yards per carry, but Pittsburgh lack a dynamic running option. Cook's involvement in the passing game is encouraging, and he remains locked in a near every down role and strong RB2 play even if the Bills' game doesn't shoot out like it did last week.
outlooksByWeek.3: James Cook will look to continue his scoring prowess Thursday when the Bills host the Dolphins in Week 3. Cook has already rushed for three scores after doing so an NFL-leading 16 times last season and averaged a robust 6.3 yards per carry on 21 totes in Week 2. Miami has yet to allow a rushing touchdown, but Cook found paydirt against them three times last year, including once through the air. Relying on touchdowns is a risky proposition, but Cook has proven his worth and his potential involvement in the passing game bodes well as Miami allowed 119 yards receiving to running backs in Week 2.

player.seasonOutlook: Cook enters his fourth NFL season as one of the trickiest evaluations in fantasy. On one hand, Cook operates in a three-headed committee (albeit as the starter), which limited his carries (19th among RBs last season), targets (34th), touches (22nd) and total yardage (21st) last season. On the other, he's an explosive playmaker (4.87 YPC) in an elite offense who tied for the NFL lead 16 rushing touchdowns in 16 regular season games last season. Cook is obviously a strong bet for touchdown regression to the mean (especially considering he had nine TDs during his first two seasons), but the 25-year-old gets enough run in a great offense to produce starting-caliber fantasy numbers. Value him as a fringe top-15 back.

outlooksByWeek.1: Xavier Worthy had an up and down season as a rookie, but it began and ended on high notes. After scoring two touchdowns on only three touches in his NFL debut, the undersized speedster erupted for an 8-157-2 line in a Super Bowl loss to the Eagles. Worthy's ability to blow by defenders and threaten big gains was reminiscent of Tyreek Hill, but it took most of the year for him to earn a large role in the Kansas City passing game and establish some trust from Patrick Mahomes. With Rashee Rice set to miss the first six games of the 2025 season, Worthy has little competition to be the team's top downfield target out of the gate, and he could make a splash in Sao Paulo during a Week 1 contest against a Chargers secondary that finished in the bottom 10 in touchdowns allowed to WRs in 2024.
outlooksByWeek.2: Xavier Worthy headed into Kansas City's season opener with another golden chance to further establish himself as a top option for Patrick Mahomes. Instead, the second-year wideout got knocked out of the game after only three snaps due to a shoulder injury sustained in a collision with Travis Kelce. With Rashee Rice suspended into October, the team needs Worthy in the lineup, and he'll attempt to avoid surgery via rehab and wearing a brace. He's unlikely to suit up in Week 2 against an Eagles secondary that finished third in receiving yards allowed to WRs in 2024.
outlooksByWeek.3: Xavier Worthy sat out a Week 2 loss to the Eagles due to a dislocated right shoulder he suffered in Kansas City's opener, but the second-year wide receiver could make a rapid return as he attempts to play through an injury that may eventually require surgery. Worthy was a limited participant in practice leading up to Week 2's game, setting him up to increase his activity ahead of Week 3. If he is able to suit up, he could contribute even with a limited snap count against a Giants defense that just got torched for 361 passing yards by the Cowboys.

player.seasonOutlook: The Chiefs selected Worthy in the first round last year and the speedster was a major difference-maker right out of the gate. He was involved as both a rusher and receiver, dominating with the ball in his hands (his 7.0 RAC was ninth best among WRs). Perhaps the most notable nugget pertaining to Worthy is his late-season emergence. He handled a hefty 26% target share (8.7 per game) in his final six games (including the playoffs) and scored at least 19 fantasy points in five of those games. Working with a QB (Patrick Mahomes) who has finished top 10 in passing yards and TDs seven straight years, as well as with Travis Kelce aging and Rashee Rice facing a six-game suspension after missing most of 2024, the 22-year-old Worthy is well positioned for a big breakout. He's an intriguing WR2 target.

outlooksByWeek.1: Zay Flowers took a step forward in his second season and became the clear top pass catcher in the Baltimore offense. He specifically increased his ability to deliver big plays, with 19 of his 74 receptions going for 20 or more yards with four gaining more than 40 yards. Not much has changed among the pass-catching corps for the Ravens, with a declining DeAndre Hopkins the only major addition. That sets up Flowers for a big role in Week 1 against the Bills, and he's a solid WR2 to plug into fantasy lineups.
outlooksByWeek.2: Zay Flowers kicked off the 2025 season in encouraging fashion, blending together volume and efficiency as a key part of the Baltimore offense. His nine targets were his highest mark since Week 8 of the 2024 season, and four of his seven receptions went for more than 20 yards. Flowers won't replicate those numbers every week, but it was impressive that he out-targeted every other Raven by five. He should be considered a solid WR2 heading into a Week 2 matchup against Cleveland.
outlooksByWeek.3: Zay Flowers has differentiated himself from the rest of Baltimore's pass catchers, more than doubling any other receiver or tight end in receptions, targets and yards. He's been more consistent with his production through two weeks, tallying seven receptions in each game while also recording at least 75 receiving yards. That gives Flowers a solid floor heading into a Week 3 matchup against Detroit, a secondary that has allowed four touchdowns and one 100-yard performance to opposing wide receivers through two games this season. Consider Flowers a solid WR2.

player.seasonOutlook: Flowers is back for his third NFL season after posting very similar numbers in each of his first two campaigns. He was utilized downfield more in 2024 than he was as a rookie, which boosted his yardage total, but he saw a dip in catches and TDs. He's finished outside the top 20 receivers in receptions, TDs and fantasy points in both seasons and simply didn't have enough quality fantasy outings last season, as he scored 18-plus points five times (all prior to Week 10) and fewer than 12 points in 11 games. The 24-year-old is the No. 1 receiver in Baltimore's elite offense, but the scheme simply limits his fantasy ceiling. He's best valued as a good WR3.

outlooksByWeek.1: DJ Moore will kick off what he hopes is a bounce-back season with the Bears at home versus Minnesota in Week 1. After falling short both of expectations, and the 1,000-yard mark, during his first season with quarterback Caleb Williams last year, Moore now looks primed to benefit from what should be a drastically improved offensive scheme. In 2024, Moore's average depth of target (7.5) and yards per catch (9.9) were career-low marks, but just the year prior he set career-high marks essentially across the board with a 96-1,364-8 receiving line while Justin Fields was under center. The stage appears set in 2025 for Moore to put up similar numbers to 2023, and though Rome Odunze, Luther Burden and Colston Loveland represent intriguing young target competition, Moore is clearly the most proven pass-catcher among Chicago's receivers and will open the year in prime position to take advantage of a Vikings defense that ranked second-worst against opposing WRs last season.
outlooksByWeek.2: DJ Moore remains positioned as the Bears' de facto WR1 heading into a road Week 2 matchup against the Lions. Coming off a disappointing but narrow 27-24 loss against the Vikings, both Chicago and Detroit will be desperate for a Week 2 win to avoid failing to fourth in the NFC North. Moore hauled in three of five targets for a team-high 69 yards versus Minnesota, while also rushing three times for eight yards. He did, however, lose a key fumble, without which the Bears may have been able to escape Week 1 with a win. Still, Moore is positioned well to keep up his momentum in Week 2, especially after the Lions showed vulnerability to the deep ball versus Green Bay in Week 1, getting burned by Romeo Doubs for 68 yards on two grabs (a long of 48 yards). Moore's skillset as an outside, chunk-play threat and candidate for designed, pre-snap motion plays that make use of his YAC abilities provide him a real ceiling versus Detroit.
outlooksByWeek.3: DJ Moore and the Bears will host the Cowboys in Week 3, coming off a lopsided 52-21 loss to the Lions. He managed five receptions on six targets for forty-six yards versus Detroit, retaining solid efficiency but trailing Rome Odunze (7-128-2 on 11 targets) notably in terms of involvement. In back-to-back weeks to begin the season, the Bears' passing game has sputtered with Caleb Williams struggling against pressure. Dallas' pass rush is a step down from either the Vikings or Lions, and the team's secondary has been vulnerable to big plays, potentially setting up Williams the passing game to bounce back. Moore's role as Williams' most reliable outlet should keep him firmly in the WR2 mix, but it's worrying he struggled to tally notable production in a game script that forced Chicago to play catch-up and lean on the passing game.

player.seasonOutlook: Moore has emerged as one of the league's most reliable and consistent players, having missed only two games in his seven-year career while finishing each of the past six seasons as a top-25 fantasy receiver. Working in a crowded Chicago WR room with a rookie QB last season, Moore did see a dip in fantasy output (from ninth in PPG in 2023 to 28th in 2024), but he was still very productive, finishing ninth among WRs in targets and receptions. Moore did improve dramatically in the second half of the season (11.1 fantasy PPG during Weeks 1-10, but 17.3 in eight games once OC Shane Waldron was fired), which is notable as Ben Johnson takes over the offense. Entering his age-28 season, Moore is a fine WR2 target and a career year is very possible if Caleb Williams makes a Year 2 leap.

outlooksByWeek.1: David Njoku missed six games in 2024 due to a combination of ankle and hamstring injuries, but he enters 2025 healthy and ready to serve as the Browns' primary tight end. He was a reliable target in the Cleveland offense last season, logging at least five catches in eight of his 11 contests, and should be one of Joe Flacco's primary targets alongside Jerry Jeudy. Njoku should have the chance to start the season strong in a Week 1 matchup against the Bengals, who could be relying heavily on rookie Demetrius Knight in coverage.
outlooksByWeek.2: David Njoku posted a disappointing three-reception, 37-yard performance in Week 1, but his usage in the Cleveland offense was even more concerning. He was on the field for a solid 84% of snaps, but he was out targeted 9-6 by rookie tight end Harold Fannin. While there's plenty of time for Njoku to regain his role, his reliability in a Week 2 matchup against Baltimore is fair to question. He's passable as a low-end starting tight end, but Njoku is suddenly a very risky start.
outlooksByWeek.3: David Njoku remains a mainstay in the Cleveland offense, but his target volume dipped due to the emergence of rookie Harold Fannin. Njoku earned 11 total targets while combining to record 77 yards, primarily as a short-area target. His suddenly uncertain opportunity hurts his fantasy outlook, as does a Week 3 matchup against a tough Green Bay defense. Njoku is a low-end starting option, but there are potentially superior streaming candidates.

player.seasonOutlook: Njoku is entering his ninth NFL season following a 2024 campaign in which he missed six games but was terrific when active, averaging a career-high 13.5 fantasy points per game. He was a top-10 scorer in seven of 11 games and finished top 5 at the position in targets for the second season in a row. Njoku has rarely been very productive in the scoring department (his career high is six touchdowns), but he found the end zone five times last season and has now led the position in end zone targets two years in a row. Despite Cleveland's never-ending QB issues, Njoku has finished 11th or better in three consecutive fantasy campaigns (top 8 in PPG) and the 29-year-old remains a midrange TE1.

outlooksByWeek.1: Tyrone Tracy was among the bright spots for the Giants as a rookie, coming from virtual anonymity to rush for 839 yards and five touchdowns. Devin Singletary remains with the squad, though, and fan favorite Cam Skattebo is already making a play for more touches. Tracy averaged 4.4 yards per tote as a rookie, but his rope may be short with other options on the roster. Fortunately for him, a favorable matchup lurks in Week 1 versus Washington. The Commanders were one of the worst teams in the NFL against the run in 2024, surrendering 137.5 yards per clash, which was 30th in the league. Washington also allowed 18 scores on the ground last season, tied for 18th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.2: Tyrone Tracy could muster only 35 scrimmage yards in Week 1 for the Giants. The entire offense struggled as a whole, gaining under 250 total yards in the 21-6 loss to Washington. The Giants failed to score a single touchdown. Tracy performed better than backup Devin Singletary and rookie Cam Skattebo, though, as the latter duo combined for just six rushing yards. Tracy should remain the starter heading into Week 2 versus the Dallas Cowboys. The Cowboys run defense scuffled in Week 1, allowing 158 yards and three touchdowns on the ground to the Eagles.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tyrone Tracy found himself on the losing end of a timeshare with rookie Cam Skattebo in Week 2 for the Giants. Tracy rushed just five times for 15 yards, though he did catch four passes for 36 yards out of the backfield. Meanwhile, Skattebo rushed 11 times for 45 yards and a touchdown, while also catching two passes for 14 yards out of the backfield. The rookie appears to have the upper hand on Tracy heading into a Week 3 matchup with a Kansas City defense that has been mediocre against the run thus far in 2025, allowing 106 yards per tilt on the ground, which is tied for 16th in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: A fifth-round flier in last year's NFL draft, Tracy took over as the Giants' de facto lead back in Week 5 and went on to play 11 "full" games with Devin Singletary also active. During that span, Tracy played 67% of the snaps and handled 13.2 carries and 3.5 targets per game. He reached 65 yards in nine of the 11 games and averaged 12.2 fantasy PPG, which ranked 23rd among RBs. Tracy's efficiency and TD total suffered in New York's struggling offense and, while they figure to improve with better QB play in 2025, he's now likely ticketed for a timeshare with fourth-round rookie Cam Skattebo. The 25-year-old is a fringe flex option.

outlooksByWeek.1: J.J. McCarthy will make his first career regular-season start for the Vikings in Week 1 on the road against Chicago, after having missed his entire rookie campaign due to a torn MCL. Minnesota, by all accounts, is confident in McCarthy's ability to hit the ground running, as evidenced by the team's decision to let backups Sam Howell and Brett Rypien depart, instead bringing in Carson Wentz just days prior to Week 1. Much is working in McCarthy's favor - head coach Kevin O'Connell is a demonstrably beneficial play caller, whose presence did wonders for Sam Darnold last season, as did the presence of the elite pass-catching trio of Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison (suspended three games) and TE T.J. Hockenson. Since Darnold's resurgence, the Vikings have additionally hugely upgraded the O-line, which will position McCarthy well to make use of his underrated athleticism on the ground, having racked up 632 rushing yards and 10 scores during his time at Michigan.
outlooksByWeek.2: J.J. McCarthy and the Vikings will look to continue compiling reasons for optimism against the Falcons on Sunday Night Football in Week 2. In the second-year pro's regular-season debut, he led an impressive primetime comeback win over the division-rival Bears after falling down by 21 points through the first three quarters. On the night, McCarthy completed 13 of 20 passes for 143 yards with two touchdowns and one interception, connecting with Justin Jefferson and Aaron Jones for the pair of fourth-quarter scores. He also tossed a two-point conversion to Adam Thielen and rushed twice for 25 yards and another score. In terms of lowlights, however, McCarthy was sacked three times and threw an ugly pick-six in the third quarter. With his debut jitters in the rearview, a matchup against Atlanta's vulnerable secondary in Week 2 will provide McCarthy an opportunity to build on his highlight-reel plays, particularly his dual-threat ability, while hopefully cleaning up some of the mistakes he put on tape Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: J.J. McCarthy looks set to sit out with a high-ankle sprain as the Vikings travel to Cincinnati in Week 3, leaving Carson Wentz in position to start. A rest will at least provide McCarthy time to get his head straight after a choppy Week 2 loss against the Falcons, in which the second-year QB completed 11 of 21 passes for 158 yards, was sacked six times for 38 yards, threw two interceptions and added five carries for 25 yards, looking more like the player that was featured during the first three quarters of Week 1's win over the Bears than the clutch signal-caller who led a fourth-quarter comeback. Cincinnati's defense is fresh off surrendering 27 points to a struggling Jaguars offense and represents a nice opportunity for McCarthy to bounce back if he does manage to suit up, but Minnesota's protection (and pocket management) will dictate his fantasy ceiling - especially with No. 2 WR Jordan Addision out one more game due to his suspension.

player.seasonOutlook: McCarthy is entering his de facto rookie campaign after a knee injury cost the 2024 10th overall pick his entire first season in the pros. McCarthy is expected to start in a QB-friendly Kevin O'Connell scheme loaded with targets (Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison, T.J. Hockenson) that helped Sam Darnold and Kirk Cousins to top-12 fantasy campaigns (PPG) during each of O'Connell's three seasons in Minnesota. All three offenses were pass-heavy and scored at least 80% of their TDs through the air. A 22-year-old with no NFL experience, McCarthy is an obvious unknown, but he can add some value with his legs and is well positioned for a productive first season. He's an attractive late-round sleeper target.

Bills general manager Brandon Beane was a man of his word this offseason, going all-in on a defensive line that finished 2024 with only 39 sacks. In addition to signing five-time Pro Bowl DE Joey Bosa, the Bills drafted defensive linemen in Rounds 2 through 4 (and six defenders overall), bolstering a roster that has finished eighth or better in fantasy points in four straight seasons. If you're speculating on a fifth straight, merely be patient through their treacherous Week 1 matchup (BUF).

outlooksByWeek.1: Trey Benson and the Cardinals will take on New Orleans in Week 1. The Florida State product got a limited look as a rookie last season but averaged a healthy 4.6 YPC on 63 carries. James Conner remains the projected workhorse in Arizona's backfield, though the team could look to spell him more often this season if Benson continues to develop. The Cardinals could look to attack on the ground in Week 1 against a Saints defense that gave up 18 rushing TDs -- tied for most in the NFL -- to RBs last year.
outlooksByWeek.2: Trey Benson will look to build upon a standout Week 1 performance for the Cardinals in a Week 2 matchup against Carolina. Benson led Arizona with 69 rushing yards on eight rushes in Week 1 against New Orleans while ripping off a game-long 52 yard carry in the second half. Meanwhile, starter James Conner notched just 39 yards on 12 carries, though he did score a TD through the air. If Benson is able to maintain that level of split work in the backfield moving forward, he could emerge as an intriguing fantasy RB to roster. He'll certainly have a prime opportunity to build upon his season-opening performance, as the Panthers gave up a league-high 173 yards on 25 carries to RBs in Week 1 versus Jacksonville.
outlooksByWeek.3: Trey Benson will try to continue to be a factor in Arizona's Week 3 game against the 49ers. After emerging with 69 rushing yards on eight carries in Week 1, Benson logged just three rushes for 14 yards against the Panthers in Week 2, but he also caught four balls for 30 yards in that latter contest. James Conner remains atop Arizona's RB depth chart, but he's struggled to be efficient this season, so Benson could eventually cut into the veteran's workload if he continues to produce. San Francisco was strong against the run in Week 1 versus Seattle but gave up 99 yards on 21 rushes to Alvin Kamara in Week 2.

player.seasonOutlook: Benson is entering his second season after playing a minimal role as a rookie. The 2024 third-round pick never truly pushed James Conner for work and instead was limited to 69 touches in 13 games while sharing change-of-pace duties with Emari Demercado. Benson was effective (4.6 YPC, 2.1 YAC), and though it's logical to expect a larger role in his second season, Conner remains the team's lead back after signing an extension in November. Benson won't have standalone value early on, but he's an intriguing insurance target considering Conner is entering his age-30 season having never played a full regular season.

outlooksByWeek.1: Dalton Kincaid aims to bounce back in his third season in Week 1 when the Bills host the Ravens. Kincaid caught 44 balls a season ago, 29 fewer than his rookie year, while missing three games due to injury. He's scored only four touchdowns in his career and faces a defense that allowed opposing tight ends to post fewer than seven fantasy points per game a season ago. Buffalo has no clear lead receiver, but competition for targets remains vast in a deep unit, likely keeping Kincaid's volume too low to be trusted as a starting option at the position out of the gate.
outlooksByWeek.2: Dalton Kincaid will look to score in consecutive weeks when the Bills face the Jets in Week 2. Kincaid hauled in all four of his targets last week, scoring for just the fifth time in 30 career games. The four targets were light in a game where Buffalo threw 46 passes, but he was routinely open downfield but just didn't get the opportunity. Looking fully healthy, there's cautious optimism against a Jets defense that allowed tight ends to catch eight balls and score in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Dalton Kincaid has enjoyed a consistent start to his campaign into Week 3 when the Bills host the Dolphins on Thursday night. Kincaid caught four balls in each of Buffalo's first two games, but the yardage has been minimal at 85 yards. Though he scored in Week 1, it was just his fifth touchdown in two-plus seasons, so there appears to be minimal upside, but there should be a decent floor against a Miami defense that's allowed 12 catches to opposing tight ends thus far.

player.seasonOutlook: Kincaid failed to clear 13.1 fantasy points in a single game last season, which is pretty hard to believe when you consider he handled a 20.3% target share (5.8 per game) in a Josh Allen-led offense that averaged 3.6 touchdowns per game (the highest ever by an Allen offense). Kincaid got seven-plus targets in six of 13 regular-season games, but never cleared 53 yards in a single outing and found the end zone only twice. He finished 15th at tight end in targets despite four missed games, but was 26th in catches and 28th in yards thanks to an ugly 59% catch rate and 6.0 YPT. Kincaid's pedigree (2023 first-rounder), heavy usage and the strong Buffalo offense provide hope for a Year 3 leap, but he's risky after such an underwhelming 2024. Consider him a fringe TE1.

outlooksByWeek.1: Wan'Dale Robinson garnered almost nine targets per game for the Giants last season, dominating the shorter routes as a possession receiver to complement Malik Nabers. Robinson finished the season with 93 catches for 699 yards and three touchdowns.  Russell Wilson is the new quarterback under center, but Robinson should continue to figure prominently in the passing attack, as the Giants did not bring in any other wideouts as compared to last season to compete for looks. In Week 1, though, Robinson will face a tough task against Washington on Sunday. The Commanders boasted a stellar pass defense in 2024, allowing only 189.5 passing yards per outing, which was third in the league.
outlooksByWeek.2: Wan'Dale Robinson picked up where he left off last season in Week 1 for the Giants.  The possession receiver snagged six passes for 55 yards on eight targets, though the Giants fell by a score of 21-6 to the Commanders. New starting quarterback Russell Wilson struggled, passing for just 168 yards for the game and failing to lead a single touchdown drive. Robinson could be catching passes from rookie Jaxson Dart sooner than anticipated, though the switch is not likely to occur in Week 2 versus the Cowboys. Dallas held up surprisingly well in Week 1 versus the Eagles, allowing only 144 yards passing and zero touchdowns through the air.
outlooksByWeek.3: Wan'Dale Robinson posted a career-high 142 receiving yards for the Giants last game. Normally a possession receiver, Robinson got free for several large chunk plays en route to the best numbers of his brief career. Robinson has 14 catches on 18 targets through just two games. In Week 3, the Giants will face a hungry Kansas City squad that is also 0-2 to start the season, with a defense was picked apart by Justin Herbert in Week 1, but bounced back in Week 2 by allowing just 101 passing yards and zero throwing scores to the Eagles.

player.seasonOutlook: Robinson is entering his fourth NFL season following a breakout 2024 campaign. The 2022 second-round pick was limited to 838 yards and three TDs on 94 touches during his first two seasons (21 games), but made the leap to 717 yards and three TDs on 96 touches in 17 games while playing alongside Malik Nabers in 2024. Despite handling a hefty 25% target share (which helped him to top-10 finishes in both targets and receptions), Robinson finished outside the top 40 receivers in yardage and fantasy PPG due to a WR-low 4.9 aDOT and horrific 5.0 YPT. The 24-year-old is strictly a short-area option and, though having Russell Wilson (and perhaps Jaxson Dart) under center will help, Robinson is a very low-ceiling PPR depth receiver.

outlooksByWeek.1: Matthew Stafford has been declared good to go for the Rams' Week 1 matchup against Houston. Stafford dealt with a back injury during training camp, though he was able to start practicing in mid-August. The veteran QB will no longer have Cooper Kupp -- who is now with Seattle -- at his disposal, but he gained another veteran with a history of strong production when Los Angeles signed Davante Adams in the offseason. The Texans were up-and-down against the pass last year but allowed an 83.7 QB rating, fourth-best in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.2: Matthew Stafford will look to lead the Rams to a second straight win in Week 2 against Tennessee. Stafford was solid in the season-opening win over Houston, completed 21 of 29 pass attempts for 245 yards and a touchdown. Not surprisingly, he did his best work with reliable WR Puka Nacua (10-130-0), though Stafford also showed some chemistry with newcomer Davante Adams (4-51-0). The Titans could be a formidable opponent after holding Denver's Bo Nix to 176 passing yards and picking him off twice in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Matthew Stafford heads into the Rams' Week 3 NFC clash against the Eagles with two strong games under his belt to start the campaign. Stafford completed 23 of 33 passes for 298 yards and two touchdowns in Week 2 against Tennessee, though he did toss his first interception of the year. The veteran quarterback has unsurprisingly connected well with top wideout Puka Nacua, but he also fed new passing partner Davante Adams to the tune of six catches for 106 yards and a touchdown. The Eagles present a tough matchup, however, having surrendered a 74.5 passer rating to QBs -- the second-lowest mark in the league -- through two weeks.

player.seasonOutlook: Stafford returns for his fifth season in Los Angeles. The 37-year-old continues to play good football (11th in QBR last season), but that hasn't translated to much fantasy success (27th in fantasy PPG last season and his last top-10 season was with Detroit in 2019). Stafford has finished each of the last two seasons just outside the top 10 in attempts, completions, pass yards and pass TDs, while also continuing to offer almost zero with his legs (39.5 rushing yards per season and one total rush TD since joining the Rams). A solid line and elite Puka Nacua/Davante Adams WR duo could help boost Stafford's passing numbers in 2025, but the lack of rushing will limit him to nothing more than a bye-week streamer.

outlooksByWeek.1: Santos and the Bears will host the Vikings at home to kick things off Week 1. As is the case for most of Chicago's offensive players, Santos is working to bounce back from a disappointing 2024 campaign. Not only did the Bears' underwhelming offense cap Santos' scoring opportunities, but his 84 percent conversion rate on field-goal tries was the worst of his five-year stint in Chicago. The 32-year-old will work to return to form, as he's usually one of the league's more accurate kickers, but he may not get the benefit of the doubt for long should things get off to a rough start in 2025. If he can return to form, though, Santos should benefit significantly from new coach Ben Johnson's offense, which promises significant improvements compared to 2024.
outlooksByWeek.2: Cairo Santos will look to get back on track as the Bears prepare for a Week 2 road game against the Lions. His missed kick Week 1 against the Vikings looms large, as the Bears lost the divisional contest 27-24, by the breadth of a field goal. In all, Santos went 1-for-2 on field-goal tries and made all three PATs, accounting for six points, but he'll need to be steadier in a high-pressure Week 2 matchup, as a loss would send the Bears down to fourth place in the NFC North. He dropped down to an 84 percent conversion rate in 2024, his worst mark since signing with Chicago back in 2020.
outlooksByWeek.3: Cairo Santos and the Bears will work to bounce back versus the Cowboys in Week 3, coming off back-to-back rough losses. He was limited to just three extra-point tries (no field goals) during Chicago's blowout loss to the Lions in Week 2, all of which were converted. Despite offensive struggles across the board for the Bears thus far, Santos remains a relatively reliable option at the kicker position, who simply needs more consistency on offense to capitalize on scoring opportunities. A Week 3 matchup against Dallas' vulnerable secondary represents a solid get-right opportunity for Chicago.

outlooksByWeek.1: JuJu Smith-Schuster produced a meager 18-231-2 line over 14 regular-season games in his return to Kansas City last season, but over half of that production came in Week 5, when he erupted for a 7-130-0 line on eight targets. That was enough to convince the team to bring the 28-year-old wideout back on a one-year contract. Smith-Schuster is purely a depth option in the passing game at this stage of his career, but he could be pressed into duty early with Rashee Rice suspended for the first six games and Hollywood Brown nursing an ankle injury that kept him sidelined for the entire preseason. If Smith-Schuster's volume increases significantly during a trip to Sao Paulo in Week 1, he could produce against a Chargers secondary that finished in the bottom 10 in touchdowns allowed to WRs in 2024.
outlooksByWeek.2: JuJu Smith-Schuster took advantage of an opportunity in Week 1, catching all five of his targets for 55 yards. Kansas City was already missing Rashee Rice due to a suspension and then lost Xavier Worthy to a shoulder injury in the first quarter, moving Smith-Schuster up to the team's No. 2 WR role behind Hollywood Brown. Worthy is likely to be sidelined in Week 2, leaving the veteran duo at the top of the depth chart for Patrick Mahomes. Smith-Schuster faces a tough test in Week 2 against an Eagles secondary that finished third in receiving yards allowed to WRs in 2024.
outlooksByWeek.3: JuJu Smith-Schuster did little in a Week 2 loss to the Eagles, catching one of three targets for five yards. Despite the absences of Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy, Smith-Schuster has still taken a back seat in the Kansas City passing game to Hollywood Brown and Tyquan Thornton, posting a 6-60-0 line on eight targets through two games, and his path to production could get even narrower if Worthy is able to return from his shoulder injury in Week 3. If Smith-Schuster does retain a significant role in Week 3, he may not need many targets to make some noise against a Giants defense that just got torched for 361 passing yards by the Cowboys.

outlooksByWeek.2: Matt Prater seeks a second-straight double-digit scoring effort for the Bills in Week 2 against the Jets. Elevated from the practice squad with Tyler Bass placed on IR prior to Week 1, Prater nailed three field goals and two PATs in his team debut. The Jets allowed 10 points to the Steelers kicker last Sunday, and while distance may not provide scoring boosts for your team, Prater's opportunities should remain plentiful in one of the top offenses in the league.
outlooksByWeek.3: Matt Prater has been productive heading into Week 3 for the Bills on Thursday night against the Dolphins. Prater made all 11 of his attempts through two weeks, nailing three field goals in both games and five total PAT. The Dolphins have allowed the third most fantasy points to opposing kickers in the early going, Buffalo is heavily favored and there's a healthy point total to this game, all pointing towards another solid scoring day from Prater.

outlooksByWeek.1: Josh Allen begins his 2025 campaign with a potentially challenging Week 1 matchup Sunday night when the Bills host the Ravens. Baltimore's defense was surprisingly vulnerable to opposing quarterbacks last season, allowing the eighth most fantasy points per game, but they also held Allen to just 307 yards and no touchdowns in two meetings, including the playoffs. Allen's rushing ability makes him an every week starter, but expectations can be somewhat tempered out of the gate.
outlooksByWeek.2: John Allen will seek a repeat of a monster outing in Week 2 when the Bills travel to face the Jets. Allen accounted for 424 total yards and four touchdowns and now takes aim at a defense that allowed four touchdown passes in Week 1, and one that he put up six touchdowns against in two meetings last season. While you wouldn't expect this game to be as much of a shootout, Allen remains locked in as a top quarterback option that's highly likely to produce the majority of his team's scoring.
outlooksByWeek.3: Josh Allen is is a favorable spot to rebound in Week 3 when the Bills host the Dolphins on Thursday night. After carrying his team in Week 1, Allen was marginal in Week 2, throwing for 148 yards while rushing for 59 and not scoring. He always has elite upside, and it's encouraging that he logged 20 rushing attempts to date, but Week 3 could be a blowout where the Bills protect their star. It's also worth noting that in two matchups last season, Allen ran four times for nine yards. Tempered expectations are advised.

player.seasonOutlook: The reigning NFL MVP is back for his eighth season, having finished each of the last five as the No. 1 or No. 2 fantasy QB. Though he wasn't asked to throw as often last season (482 attempts ranked 14th and marked his fewest since 2019), Allen substantially cut down on turnovers (career-low five INTs) and remained a major force with his legs (he's finished top 5 among QBs in carries and rush TDs in all seven seasons). Still in his prime at age 29, Allen's dual-threat ability and a solid, slightly improved supporting cast sets him up for another elite fantasy campaign in 2025.

outlooksByWeek.1: A.J. Brown has gone over 1,000 yards receiving in five of his six NFL campaigns, and he should be poised for another banner year as the Eagles open the season at home in Week 1 against the Cowboys. Dallas was mediocre at best against the pass in 2024, allowing 218.1 passing yards per tilt, which was 17th in the league.  Dallas also surrendered 28 passing scores last season, which was tied for 24th in the NFL. Dallas re-signed cornerback DaRon Bland but traded dynamic pass rusher Micah Parsons, so the defense is unlikely to be better overall in 2025. Brown had either a touchdown or 100 yards receiving in both games versus Dallas a season ago.
outlooksByWeek.2: A.J. Brown was virtually non-existent in Week 1 for the Eagles. Brown garnered one catch for eight yards on a single target in the 24-20 win over the Cowboys. Meanwhile, Jahan Dotson was the surprise leading receiver for the squad, and Dallas Goedert notched the most targets. Expect the Eagles to get Brown involved early and often in Week 2 versus Kansas City, though. Kansas City was torched by Justin Herbert for 304 yards and three touchdowns through the air in its season opener. Brown also scored a touchdown in the Super Bowl last February.
outlooksByWeek.3: A.J. Brown led the Eagles in receptions and targets in Week 2, and while that was an improvement from the season opener, his final stat line still left a lot to be desired. Brown caught five passes on eight targets, but managed just 27 yards and did not find the end zone in the 20-17 win over Kansas City. Brown has a paltry 35 receiving yards through two games, and will look to get back on track in Week 3 versus the Rams. Unfortunately, the Rams have been stingy against the pass thus far in 2025, allowing just 147 passing yards per tilt, which is fourth in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Brown is entering his fourth season with the Eagles after finishing each of his first three no lower than 13th in fantasy PPG. Last season, Brown missed four games and saw a dip in targets (from 9.8 in 2023 to 7.5 in 2024), with the latter a product of the Eagles leading so often. Brown actually posted a career-high 34.6% target share and averaged 3.3 yards per route run (both were second highest among WRs, and he's finished five straight seasons in the top 8 in both categories). Brown was extremely boom/bust, as he posted six top-10 fantasy outings (second most) but was held below 13.5 points in six of his other seven games. The 28-year-old is once again positioned as Jalen Hurts' top target and can be viewed as a fringe WR1.

outlooksByWeek.1: Drake London will aim to expand on his third-year breakout with the Falcons, starting in Week 1 against Tampa Bay. The 23-year-old wideout ended up with career highs in just about every category in the 2024 season, and this was done even with an extremely volatile quarterback room. Second-year Michael Penix will now lead Atlanta's offense, which could be huge for London if the quarterback can play even a little better than Kirk Cousins did last year. London will match up against one of the shakier defenses versus wide receivers last season as well.
outlooksByWeek.2: Drake London will head into the Falcons' Week 2 matchup versus the Vikings with a questionable tag as he works back from a shoulder injury. London suffered a shoulder sprain late in Atlanta's Week 1 loss to Tampa Bay, but not before bringing in eight catches for 55 yards. The star pass catcher did have to miss his team's final drive of the game and is deemed day-to-day, with his initial reports looking encouraging. If London is able to play against Minnesota, he could take advantage of an early connection with Michael Penix against a Minnesota secondary that gave up 68 receiving yards to DJ Moore and struggled early on against quarterback Caleb Williams.
outlooksByWeek.3: Drake London will hope to have a more pass-heavy game script in Week 3 as Atlanta travels to Carolina. London garnered just four targets during a run-heavy win over the Vikings in Week 2, but he didn't need to be utilized given that the Falcons were up the whole game. London should hopefully have more chances to showcase his superstar abilities this upcoming week. The Panthers have let up the fourth-least fantasy points to wide receivers so far this season, but London's qualities as a pass catcher should allow him to still be dominant in the conference matchup.

player.seasonOutlook: London is entering his fourth NFL season having handled an enormous 27% of the targets and 35% of the air yards in Atlanta during his first three campaigns. London ranked eighth or better among receivers in targets, receptions, yards, TDs, end zone targets and fantasy points last season, but his production was very boom/bust. The only two games in which he reached 20 fantasy points were 33-plus-point efforts (and one was in Week 18). London's ceiling and consistency are impacted by Atlanta's run-heavy scheme, but his hefty share of the targets should be enough to allow borderline-WR1 numbers, especially if Michael Penix Jr. makes a Year 2 leap.

outlooksByWeek.1: Terry McLaurin went over the 1,000-yard receiving mark for the fifth-straight season in 2024, but there are some red flags heading into the 2025 campaign. McLaurin missed all of training camp while waiting for a new contract. Though the deal ultimately came through, it remains to be seen if he will be rusty in Week 1 versus the Giants. Moreover, the Commanders dealt for Deebo Samuel in the offseason, giving Washington a surefire No. 2 wideout perhaps for the first time in McLaurin's career. Samuel's presence could take pressure off of McLaurin, though may also lead to fewer targets. Washington will face a Giants defense that was solid against the pass in 2024, allowing 227.6 passing yards per tilt, which was 10th in the NFL. The Giants also added No. 3 pick Abdul Carter to the pass rush, as well as Jevon Holland and Paulson Adebo to the secondary, so the unit has the chance to be even better in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.2: Terry McLaurin was rather quiet in the season opener for Washington.  McLaurin managed just two catches for 27 yards on four targets as the Commanders pummeled the hapless Giants. In the past, wideouts who have missed a significant chunk of camp due to a contract dispute have started slow. McLaurin could be headed down that path as well, as a difficult matchup lurks in Week 2 against the Green Bay Packers. The Packers mauled the Lions in their opener, allowing just 200 yards passing in the process.
outlooksByWeek.3: Terry McLaurin has managed just 75 yards combined through two games for the Commanders, and in Week 3 he could be playing without his starting quarterback. Jayden Daniels is nursing a knee sprain, leaving his status in question for a clash with the Raiders. The presence of Deebo Samuel may also be eating into McLaurin's opportunities, though the latter was targeted nine times last game. The only saving grace for McLaurin, even if backup Marcus Mariota is lining up under center, is that Las Vegas has been suspect against the pass thus far in 2025, allowing 256 passing yards per tilt, which is 27th in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Many benefited from the arrival of Jayden Daniels in Washington last season, but perhaps no one more than McLaurin. The six-year vet caught 13 touchdowns (second most) after totaling 24 during his first five seasons and finished a career-best seventh (15th in PPG) in fantasy points. Despite the success, there is some "sustainability" concern here, as McLaurin's volume didn't change much from years past and he finished outside the top 30 in routes and target share. He's finished exactly 19th among WRs in targets three seasons in a row and has never finished higher than 15th in catches or ninth in yards. McLaurin will require a boost in usage to offset TD regression to the mean in order to sustain WR1 numbers. He's best valued as a mid-to-back-end WR2.

outlooksByWeek.1: Breece Hall will seek to prove doubters wrong in Week 1 when the Jets face the Steelers. Constant offseason talk has this backfield looking like a split between Hall and Braelon Allen, but it's still going to remain a run-based offense with mobile, passing game raw Justin Fields under center and a lack of receiving depth. Hall's stock has fallen throughout draft season, but his ability to catch passes in addition to handle double-digit carries will keep the floor of an RB2 safe.
outlooksByWeek.2: Breece Hall will look to build on an impressive debut when the Jets host the Bills in Week 2. Hall averaged an impressive 5.6 yard per carry in Week 1, logging his first 100-yard rushing effort since Week 6 of 2024, which conveniently came against Buffalo. The Bills were exploited by Derrick Henry, allowing 7.6 yards per carry, and while Hall is a vastly different runner, lanes figure to be available. Mix in that Hall was the team's second leading Week 1 receiver and there's a lot to like. Touchdowns appear to be a negative, with Braelon Allen and Justin Fields featured in close, so volume and chunk gains will need to keep Hall's value afloat.
outlooksByWeek.3: Breece Hall and the Jets prepare to face a stingy Buccaneers run defense in Week 3. Hall's 2025 start has been up and down, and now he squares off against a defense that's allowing just 2.8 yards per carry, but has been vulnerable to pass catching running backs, surrendering 166 yards through two weeks. Hall remains the team's lead back and could experience increased volume if Justin Fields (concussion) misses Sunday's game. Workload keeps Hall in RB2 range.

player.seasonOutlook: The 2024 season was a major disappointment for the Jets and that also applies to Hall's fantasy output. The 2022 second-round pick was a clear-cut fantasy RB1 during his first two seasons (eighth in PPG in 2022, sixth in 2023) prior to falling to 17th in 2024. Hall remained a clear lead back (only four RBs played more snaps) and was a force as a receiver (top 5 in routes, targets, catches and yards for the second season in a row), but pedestrian efficiency and rushing volume kept him outside the top 12 RBs in touches, yards and TDs. Hall is a good back and in his prime at age 24, so there's certainly so post-hype appeal in a new scheme with Justin Fields in at quarterback, but it's also likely that he'll share more work with Braelon Allen. Hall is best as a mid-range RB2.

outlooksByWeek.1: Tony Pollard is set to lead Tennessee's backfield in Week 1 against the Broncos. With the team's co-lead running back Tyjae Spears (ankle) on IR for at least four weeks and the Titans integrating a rookie QB in first overall pick Cam Ward, Tennessee will likely lean heavily on Pollard in the running game. That was the case when Spears missed time last season, as Pollard averaged 22 carries in five games without Spears compared to just 13.6 carries in 11 games together. A tough matchup against a Broncos defense that gave up the third-fewest rushing yards and third-fewest points last season makes it hard to get too excited about Pollard in Week 1, but he should get enough volume to reach the fantasy RB2 range.
outlooksByWeek.2: Tony Pollard led the Titans in both rushing yards (60) and receiving yards (29) in Week 1 while piling up 19 touches. He's primed for another busy workload against the Rams in Week 2 in the continued absence of Tyjae Spears (ankle), as Pollard averaged 22 carries in games Spears missed last season. Scoring opportunities could be limited with Titans rookie QB Cam Ward struggling, but Pollard's high touch floor keeps him in the fantasy RB2 discussion for Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tony Pollard remains the most reliable member of Tennessee's offense heading into a Week 3 home game against the Colts, and he's likely to garner another heavy workload even if the 0-2 Titans fall behind early against their 2-0 opponents. Pollard logged 89 yards on 19 Week 1 touches and 92 yards on 20 Week 2 touches, so he's a high-floor fantasy RB2 for Week 3, even though his ceiling is capped on a Titans offense that has produced only one touchdown through two games. Backup Julius Chestnut has handled just two touches through two games in the absence of Tyjae Spears (ankle), who remains on injured reserve.

player.seasonOutlook: Pollard returns for his second season as the Titans' lead back. He was busier than expected in 2024, when he finished eighth among RBs in carries and 10th in targets. He managed to produce his third consecutive season with 1,000-plus rushing yards and 1,300-plus from scrimmage, but didn't get much goal-line work (five carries inside the 5) and was limited to five TDs (one fewer than Tyjae Spears). Pollard reached 19 fantasy points only once (Spears was out that week) and has finished just one season in his career better than 22nd in fantasy PPG (2022 in Dallas). Entering his age-28 season, Pollard is again expected to lead Tennessee's run game, but Spears will be involved once back from injury, especially in passing situations. Pollard is a solid flex.

outlooksByWeek.1: Evan Engram is coming off a disappointing and injury-plagued final season in Jacksonville, managing just a 47-365-1 line in nine regular-season games before being released in March. He's just two years removed from a career-best 2023, in which he hauled in 114 passes for 963 yards on 143 targets. The tight end could be a good fit in a Sean Payton offense that turned Jimmy Graham into a star in New Orleans, but at 30 years old, Engram's best days are likely behind him, and he'll face plenty of competition for looks from Courtland Sutton and the Broncos' young wideouts, as well as rookie running back RJ Harvey. In Week 1, Engram will take on a stingy Titans defense that allowed the second-fewest receiving yards in the NFL last year to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.2: Evan Engram had a modest start to his Broncos tenure, catching three of four targets for 21 yards in Week 1. The 31-year-old tight end also suffered a calf injury in the fourth quarter, an ominous sign after he was healthy enough to play only nine games for the Jaguars last season. Engram was signed this offseason to provide second-year QB Bo Nix with a reliable chain-mover, but he'll need to stay healthy to fill that role. His status is questionable heading into Week 2's clash with a Colts defense that finished in the bottom seven in catches, receiving yards and touchdowns against TEs in 2024.
outlooksByWeek.3: Evan Engram continues to be eased into the Broncos' offense, playing just 25 snaps in a Week 2 loss to the Colts and catching one of two targets for 12 yards. A shoulder injury over the summer and a minor calf issue in Week 1 have slowed Engram down, but he's also losing work to Adam Trautman as the latter offers superior blocking skills. Engram has significantly more upside as a pass-catcher, and with quarterback Bo Nix still looking for reliable secondary options behind Courtland Sutton, there's a clear path for Engram to get consistent target volume. The veteran tight end will try to make a difference in Week 3 against a Chargers defense that was able to bottle up a less-than-100% Brock Bowers in Week 2, but which did give up a TD to Travis Kelce in Week 1.

player.seasonOutlook: Engram signed with Denver after spending his first eight NFL seasons with the Giants and Jaguars. The 2017 first-round pick is coming off a bit of a lost season, as injuries cost him seven games and he found the end zone only once when active. Engram was still heavily targeted (his 25% target share ranked third among TEs) and, even with last season's dud, he has finished top 7 in fantasy PPG in five of his eight seasons. Engram isn't much of a touchdown scorer (he hasn't produced more than four in a season since 2017, but he's joining a good Denver offense led by Sean Payton (who helped Jimmy Graham to three consecutive top-2 fantasy seasons) and impressive second-year QB Bo Nix. Engram remains squarely in the back-end TE1 mix and there's upside for even more.

outlooksByWeek.1: Chris Olave will enter Week 1 as the top wide receiver for the Saints as they take on the Cardinals. Olave has suffered four concussions in his three NFL seasons, which means his next one could be career-ending, and he'll also have to deal with shaky quarterback play this season. The team's WR1 still has efficient skills and produced back-to-back 1,000-yard seasons before being sidelined last year. He has some roadblocks to re-establishing himself as one of the league's top wide receivers this campaign, including a tough Arizona secondary that allowed the eighth-fewest fantasy points to wide receivers last season.
outlooksByWeek.2: Chris Olave will look for big volume once again as the Saints take on the 49ers in Week 2. Olave didn't finish with a huge game in Week 1 versus the Cardinals, but he did register 13 targets and converted them into seven catches and 54 yards. The star wideout should continue to be targeted heavily in new coach Kellen Moore's pass-heavy offense, with hopes for more production if he gets double-digit looks once again. San Francisco did hold Seahawks wide receivers to 139 receiving yards last week, but 124 of these came from Jaxon Smith-Njigba. This means a talented WR1 like Olave could produce a similar performance in his second game of the season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chris Olave will search for his first touchdown of the season as the Saints travel to Seattle for Week 3. Olave has gone two straight weeks with 54 yards, which could've been even higher with the high level of targets that he's gotten so far. New Orleans' offense has also shifted to a pass-heavy emphasis this season, which doesn't look to be changing any time soon. This should give Olave all the volume he needs for a breakout game versus a Seahawks defense that gave up a touchdown to DK Metcalf last week and 108 receiving yards to Ricky Pearsall in Week 1.

player.seasonOutlook: Olave is entering his fourth NFL season following a troubling 2024 campaign in which he played only six full games while battling concussion woes. The good news is that Olave appears healthy for 2025 and he's been productive when active throughout his career. That includes 2024, as he produced 80-plus yards four times in those six games. He handled a 24% target share, which wasn't far off his 27% and 25% rates during his first two seasons. The 2022 first-round pick has yet to reach his ceiling (he's yet to clear five TDs in a season), but he produced top-25 fantasy campaigns in his first two seasons and is set up well to pace New Orleans in targets in 2025. Of course, there's added risk here as the Saints turn to rookie QB Tyler Shough and Spencer Rattler following Derek Carr's retirement. Olave is safest as a WR3/flex, with a hint of post-hype sleeper appeal.

outlooksByWeek.1: Michael Pittman will look to bounce back from a down year in a Week 1 home game against the Dolphins. After averaging 1,053 receiving yards from 2021 to 2023, Pittman dipped to 808 in 2024. The decline was due in large part to the inaccuracy of QB Anthony Richardson, who lost the Colts' QB competition to Daniel Jones this preseason. Pittman's skill set should mesh well with Jones' risk-averse short and intermediate throws, though TE Tyler Warren and WR Josh Downs will also operate in those areas. The Colts will likely take a run-heavy approach, but Pittman's a solid Week 1 flex play as the team's highest-floor WR, especially if Downs doesn't play.
outlooksByWeek.2: Michael Pittman showed excellent chemistry with new Colts QB Daniel Jones in the season opener, racking up six catches for 80 yards and a TD on eight targets. He'll face a tough Week 2 matchup against star CB Patrick Surtain and the Broncos, though Pittman can still be deployed as a fantasy WR3 or flex given his pedigree and encouraging start to the season. The two-time 1,000-yard receiver was the only Colts WR targeted more than three times in Week 1 against the Dolphins, though TE Tyler Warren led the team with nine targets.
outlooksByWeek.3: Michael Pittman had just 40 yards and was outperformed by fellow Colts WRs Alec Pierce and Josh Downs in Week 2 after leading the team with 80 receiving yards and a TD in the season opener. Indianapolis' offense has been humming with Daniel Jones under center, but Pittman could have a hard time delivering consistently strong performances since the Colts like to feed star RB Jonathan Taylor and Jones has been spreading the ball out pretty evenly between Pittman, Downs, Pierce and TE Tyler Warren. Pittman's a low-end fantasy WR3 or flex play for Week 3 against the Titans, as the favored Colts will likely employ a run-heavy approach, potentially limiting Pittman's receiving opportunities.

player.seasonOutlook: Pittman is eyeing a rebound campaign after following up three consecutive top-20 fantasy seasons with a 41st-place finish in 2024. He averaged a healthy 27% target share in 10 full games with Anthony Richardson, but that resulted in an ugly 39-428-0 receiving line on 65 targets. He averaged 8.0 fantasy PPG, reaching double digits once (15.6 in Week 12). Pittman continues to struggle to find the end zone (his career high is six and he's had four or fewer three seasons in a row) and, while that may not have changed with Richardson under center (the Colts had eight pass TDs in his 10 games last season), he'll be in a more fantasy-friendly spot with Daniel Jones winning the Colts' starting gig. Pittman is an underated flex option with WR3 upside.

outlooksByWeek.1: Keon Coleman brings some buzz into his sophomore campaign with the Bills set to host the Ravens in Week 1. Coleman averaged an impressive 19.2 yards per catch as a rookie, and the addition of Joshua Palmer as a deep threat could give Coleman more versatility in his routes, potentially adding volume at the expense of big plays. Josh Allen didn't throw a touchdown pass in two meetings with Baltimore last season, and the floor for Coleman is non-existent, but in a game with a high 50.5 total, Coleman is the high-ceiling Bills receiver in this contest.
outlooksByWeek.2: Keon Coleman will look to build on a breakout game in Week 2 when the Bills face the Jets. Coleman hauled in eight of 11 targets for 112 yards and a touchdown in Week 1, the highest volume of his brief career. It's important to remember QB Josh Allen threw 46 passes, more than in any game last season, and that volume seems unlikely to repeat. The Jets allowed only nine catches to receivers last week, but a massive 12.5 yards per target, giving Coleman some upside even if his looks aren't as plentiful.
outlooksByWeek.3: Keon Coleman's Week 3 potential for the Bills in a Thursday matchup with the Dolphins looks capped by game script. After feasting in a back-and-forth shootout to open the year, Coleman was a non-factor in Week 2's blowout win, catching all three of his targets for 26 yards. With Buffalo heavily favored and continued expectations of splitting targets heavily across the receiving corps, Coleman is a risky WR3 on a short week.

player.seasonOutlook: Coleman is eyeing a Year 2 leap following an uneven rookie campaign in which the second-round pick was limited to 57 targets in 13 regular-season games. Coleman was on the field quite a bit (73% snap share) and started to pick up steam around midseason (consecutive games with at least seven targets and 16 fantasy points), but a wrist injury then cost him four games and he went without a 12-point outing from that point forward (including three playoff games). Coleman's role as a vertical target (his 15.0 aDOT ranked fifth) allowed him many big plays (his 19.2 YPR ranked third), but major volatility (51% catch rate). Coleman was a young rookie at age 21 and showed enough flashes to suggest a Year 2 breakout is possible, especially in a Josh Allen-led offense with Khalil Shakir and Joshua Palmer as his top competition. Coleman is well worth a mid-to-late-round pick.

outlooksByWeek.1: Jordan Love and the Packers will look to kick off the 2025 campaign strong with a Week 1 matchup against the division-rival Lions, whose defense ranked just 26th against QBs last season. Of course, last year saw Detroit lose nearly half their starting defense to injuries, so Love and company will be facing a much-improved unit. For his part, Love is back to full health after having missed part of the preseason due to thumb surgery on his left, non-throwing hand, but his pass-catching corps is less than 100 percent. Jayden Reed (foot) plans to play through  Jones fracture while Dontayvion Wicks (calf) may not be in full form after having missed most of camp. Those factors could lead Love to look for rookie first-round WR Matthew Golden, reliable incumbent starter Romeo Doubs, and TE Tucker Kraft early and often.
outlooksByWeek.2: Jordan Love and the Packers face a quick turnaround on Thursday night against a Commanders defense that just held Russell Wilson and the Giants to 231 total yards combined. Love didn't need to air it out in the Packers' 27-13 win over Detroit, but he was ruthlessly efficient (16-of-22, 188 yards, 2 TDs) despite having missed much of training camp due to left thumb surgery. Even after Washington's impressive Week 1 defensive showing, this is a secondary that ranked sixth-worst in opponent completion percentage (69.5 percent) a season ago. Expect Love's blend of efficiency and scheme-driven opportunities in coach Matt LaFleur's system to elevate his floor beyond what the raw season-opener box score might suggest.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jordan Love and the Packers travel to Cleveland in Week 3, aiming to stay unbeaten. Fresh off a 27-18 win over Washington in which he completed 19 of 31 passes for 292 yards and two touchdowns, Love has now thrown exactly two touchdowns in each of his regular season appearances thus far. In the wake of an injury to Jayden Reed early in the first quarter, Love leaned heavily on Tucker Kraft, who posted a game-high 124 yards and a score, while also hitting Romeo Doubs for 28 yards and a score on three catches. Love has thrived by exploiting one-on-one mismatches, but the Browns have surrendered few explosive plays through two games, forcing opposing QBs to stay patient underneath. That defensive profile caps Love's ceiling somewhat, as does his willingness to play safe and allow Green Bay's defense to close out games, but coach Matt LaFleur's aggressiveness and ability to manufacture chunk gains still provides a fair ceiling even in a difficult road matchup.

player.seasonOutlook: Love is entering his third season as Green Bay's starter. The 2020 first-round pick played well last season (sixth in QBR) despite battling injury issues, but he wasn't much of a fantasy option. He came out strong with a pair of top-3 fantasy outings in his first four games, but had no additional weekly finishes better than 10th for the season. Love was a nonfactor with his legs (83 rushing yards in 15 games) and, after totaling 15 pass TDs in his first five games, threw only 10 in his final 10 outings. Green Bay did score an unusually high percentage of its offensive TDs on the ground (46%, the second highest for a Matt LaFleur offense), but that may not change with Josh Jacobs back in 2025. Love ran more in 2023 and was a solid fantasy starter, so, especially with a better supporting cast led by first-round WR Matthew Golden, there's hope for a rebound, but it is safer to view him as a QB2.

outlooksByWeek.1: Dallas Goedert's health was the chief reason for his subpar 2024 campaign for the Eagles.  Goedert posted his lowest receiving totals since his rookie season, as he played in just 10 contests for the Super Bowl champions.  Goedert will look to start fresh in Week 1 versus a mediocre Cowboys pass defense.  The Cowboys allowed 218.1 passing yards per tilt, which was 17th in the league. The Cowboys also yielded 28 passing scores last season, which was tied for 24th in the NFL. America's Team re-signed cornerback DaRon Bland but traded dynamic pass rusher Micah Parsons, so the defense is unlikely to be better overall in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.2: Dallas Goedert led the Eagles in targets in Week 1. Goedert was targeted seven times by quarterback Jalen Hurts, parlaying those looks into seven catches for 44 yards in the win. Goedert should continue to prove a nice safety valve for Hurts, though wideouts A.J. Brown and DeVonta Smith should have much more involvement in Week 2 than the combined four targets they saw in the season opener. Still, the matchup against Kansas City will still be a favorable one for the passing game overall, as the AFC powerhouse allowed 304 yards passing and three touchdowns in its loss to the Chargers.
outlooksByWeek.3: Dallas Goedert did not play in Week 2 due to a knee injury. Goedert's status will also be in question for Week 3 versus the Rams. The Eagles are 2-0 but the passing game has been woeful to date, making the backups less than ideal while Goedert is sidelined. Grant Calcaterra and Kylen Granson each had just one catch in the 20-17 win over Kansas City. In addition, Los Angeles has been stingy against the pass thus far this year, allowing only 147 yards per tilt through the air, which is fourth in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Goedert is entering his eighth NFL season with some uncertainty, as he's found himself on the trade block. The 30-year-old has finished each of the past six seasons as a top-12 fantasy scorer on a per-game basis, though he's struggled with durability (23 missed games during the six-year span) and TD scoring (he's never cleared five TDs or six end zone targets in a single season). He's otherwise been productive (top 10 in YPRR five of the past six seasons) and, whether he stays put or is traded, he'll surely remain a consistent piece of the passing game. Goedert should be valued as a good TE2.

outlooksByWeek.1: Tyler Loop has big shoes to fill as he takes over for Kyle Tucker as the Ravens' kicker. He was selected in the sixth round of the 2025 NFL Draft, so expectations are high. Loop made nine of his 11 field-goal attempts during the preseason, including two from 50 yards. He should have the chance to be very productive as a rookie given Baltimore's strong offense, but he'll be in a tough environment in Week 1 against the Bills, likely leaving better options at the position.
outlooksByWeek.2: Tyler Loop had a mostly encouraging pro debut as the Ravens' kicker, converting field goals from 49 and 52 yards. He also had a costly missed extra-point attempt following Baltimore's final touchdown, which helped contribute to the team's loss. There's no sign of the team losing confidence in Loop heading into a Week 2 matchup against Cleveland, but there should be better fantasy options available at kicker.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tyler Loop has been solid through two regular-season games, making all three of his field-goal attempts from deeper than 40 yards. He missed an extra point in Week 1 but made all five of his PAT in Week 2. Given the strength of Baltimore's offense, Loop should garner extensive opportunities once again in a Week 3 matchup against Detroit. While he's not a household name yet, Loop is a potential kicker option to consider streaming.

player.seasonOutlook: Fantasy managers piecing a D/ST strategy together could do worse than the Cardinals, who beefed up their defensive line with the signings of DE Josh Sweat and DT Calais Campbell, and face one of the league's most favorable early schedules. Their Weeks 1 and 2 matchups are a dream (@NO, CAR), and they're in similarly good shape through Week 6. Regard the Cardinals as a strong streaming candidate, with the possibility of the unit developing into something more as the season plays out.

outlooksByWeek.1: Blake Corum enters Week 1 against Houston as the Rams' backup to Kyren Williams. That may not lead to copious opportunities, as Williams may take on a workhouse role as he did last year. Los Angeles also added rookie RB Jarquez Hunter in the draft, and he could eventually be a threat to Corum's role. The Texans allowed just eight rushing TDs to RBs last year, so a vulture score isn't a good bet.
outlooksByWeek.2: Blake Corum may struggle to see opportunities for the Rams in Week 2 against Tennessee while working behind workhorse back Kyren Williams. Corum logged just one rush (for two yards) in a Week 1 victory over the Texans, adding one catch on one target for 14 yards. Meanwhile, Williams got 18 carries (which he converted into 66 yards), though he also notched just one catch. No other Rams RB got a carry Sunday, so Corum is at least looking like the team's clear No. 2 RB early on. The Titans struggled against the run in their Week 1 loss to Denver, giving up 70 yards on just six carries by RJ Harvey and 63 yards on 16 carries by J.K. Dobbins.
outlooksByWeek.3: Blake Corum was productive for the Rams in a Week 2 win against Tennessee and will look to carry that momentum over to a Week 3 matchup against the Eagles. Corum rushed just five times Sunday, but he tallied 33 yards and scored his first career touchdown on a one-yard carry. Kyren Williams remains the Rams' workhorse running back, so Corum will likely need to have multiple eye-opening performances in order to carve out a bigger role in the offense. The Eagles struggled a bit against the run in Week 1 but gave up just 55 yards on 19 rushes to a trio of Kansas City RBs in Week 2.

player.seasonOutlook: Corum enters his second NFL season likely to play a larger role after being limited to 65 touches as a rookie. The 2024 third-round pick opened the season third on the Rams' depth chart and, though he eventually passed Ronnie Rivers, he was never a threat to Kyren Williams' feature-back role. Corum wasn't overly impressive as a rookie, but he makes for an intriguing insurance stash, because Williams has totaled a massive 663 touches (third most) over the past two seasons, including the playoffs. Should Williams miss time, Corum would likely share the Rams' backfield with rookie Jarquez Hunter. He's barely worth a late-round flier.

One of 2024's most opportunistic defenses, the Seahawks D/ST scored a league-high five touchdowns (tied with the Broncos), a number that's tough to repeat year over year. Nevertheless, Aden Durde's unit returns largely the same personnel, and even strengthened a sound defensive front with the addition of DE DeMarcus Lawrence. The Seahawks also benefit by drawing the NFC South and AFC South as opponents, giving them one of the more favorable schedules, particularly in the first six weeks (SF, @PIT, NO, @ARI, TB, @JAX).

outlooksByWeek.1: Derrick Henry showed no signs of slowing down in his first season with Baltimore, tallying his highest rushing yardage (1,921) since 2020 and the highest touchdown total (20) of his career. He also recorded at least 100 rushing yards or a touchdown in 16 of 18 regular season contests, giving him remarkable consistency. The Ravens' running back room will be identical to 2024, with Henry clearly remaining the leader. A Week 1 matchup against Buffalo will be tough given its strong defensive line, but Henry should still be started confidently in all fantasy formats.
outlooksByWeek.2: Derrick Henry's lost fumble late in Baltimore's Week 1 loss will be what many remember, but otherwise he put together a strong performance. He showcased his explosive rushing ability by scoring from 46 and 30 yards away and has topped 100 rushing yards or found the end zone in all but two of 20 total games as a Raven. Henry remains a must-start option in a Week 2 matchup against Cleveland.
outlooksByWeek.3: The Ravens took a surprisingly pass-heavy approach in their blowout win over the Browns in Week 2, limiting Derrick Henry to only 11 rushing attempts and 22 yards. The performance marked only the third time across 21 games with Baltimore that Henry failed to either top 100 rushing yards or tally a rushing score. He'll look to bounce back in a Week 3 matchup against a Detroit defense that has allowed a rushing score to their opponent's lead back in each of their first two games of the season. Expect a bounceback performance from Henry, and trust him as a solid RB1.

player.seasonOutlook: Henry was �as advertised� in his first season with Baltimore, pacing all running backs in rushing TDs (16) and finishing no lower than fourth in carries, rushing yards, carries inside the 5 and fantasy points. Henry has now finished top 10 among RBs in rushing yards and TDs each of the last seven seasons, though he remains limited as a receiver (51st among RBs in targets last season). Henry is now 31 years old (ancient for a fantasy-relevant RB), but doesn't seem to have lost a step (top 3 in YPC and YAC last season). Henry's lack of targets limits his ceiling a bit, but his elite rushing output locks him in as a back-end RB1.

outlooksByWeek.1: Nico Collins is set to reprise his role as C.J. Stroud's top target in Week 1 against the Rams. Collins had 2,303 receiving yards and 15 TDs in 27 games over the past two seasons. He missed at least two games due to injuries in each of his four NFL campaigns, totaling 17 absences, but Collins is a set-and-forget fantasy WR1 when healthy, which is the case to begin the 2025 season. The Rams allowed 20 touchdown catches to WRs last season, which tied for fourth-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.2: Nico Collins struggled along with the rest of Houston's offense in the season opener, recording only 25 yards on five targets. Collins averaged 85 receiving yards per game over the previous two seasons, and he has a nice opportunity to get back on track in Week 2 against the Buccaneers, who gave up the seventh-most yards to WRs last season. He still profiles as the top target for C.J. Stroud, and it's too early to push the panic button on Collins, who remains a fantasy WR1 despite his underwhelming Week 1 outing.
outlooksByWeek.3: Nico Collins was held to three receptions (on five targets) for 25 yards in the Week 1 loss to the Rams, but he didn't waste time to make his presence felt in Week 2 and found the end zone in the first possession of the Week 2 loss to the Buccaneers. The touchdown might have saved Collins' output in Week 2, but the fact that he posted a 33.3% catch rate should worry fantasy managers who expected the star receiver to post better numbers on a consistent basis. Despite the low catch rate, Collins has led the Texans in targets in the first two games of the season, and given his rapport with quarterback C.J. Stroud, that's not expected to change in what figures to be an easier matchup in Week 3 against a subpar Jaguars secondary.

player.seasonOutlook: Collins is entering his fifth NFL season having established himself as one of the league's top receivers over the last two years. After breaking out with an 80-1,297-8 receiving line in 15 games in 2023, Collins posted a 68-1,006-7 line in 12 games last season. He was a top-10 fantasy WR on a per-game basis in both seasons. The missed games are a concern (he's missed at least two games in all four seasons), but he offsets that with elite play (top 3 in YPRR two years in a row). With Stefon Diggs gone and Tank Dell uncertain to play in 2025, Collins is ticketed for massive usage as C.J. Stroud's clear No. 1 target. He's a solid WR1 option in fantasy.

outlooksByWeek.1: Jaxon Smith-Njigba is set to lead Seattle's wideout corps in Week 1 against San Francisco. He's joined by the team's new No. 2 wideout Cooper Kupp after the Seahawks traded DK Metcalf to Pittsburgh and saw Tyler Lockett land in Tennessee in the offseason. Smith-Njigba will also be working with a new quarterback in Sam Darnold, with Geno Smith now in Las Vegas. It remains to be seen if the new-look passing game will need time to gel, and San Francisco doesn't represent an easy opponent, as the 49ers gave up just 7.31 yards per target to receivers last year, second-fewest in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.2: Jaxon Smith-Njigba will look to build on his strong season-opening performance when Seattle faces Pittsburgh in Week 2. Against the 49ers on Sunday, Smith-Njigba drew 13 targets from QB Sam Darnold, hauling in nine of them for 124 yards. No other Seattle WR had more than two catches or 15 yards, so Smith-Njigba was able to put up a big line despite a rough overall day for Darnold. The Steelers were shaky against the pass in Week 1 versus the Jets, giving up 218 yards and one touchdown to Justin Fields while notching just one sack.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jaxon Smith-Njigba enters Seattle's Week 3 matchup against the Saints with two triple-digit receiving-yardage games under his belt. He has formed quick chemistry with new QB Sam Darnold, tallying a total of 17 receptions for 227 receiving yards through two weeks. Smith-Njigba has yet to get into the end zone, however, so he'll look to break that scoreless spell in Week 3. He'll go up against a New Orleans defense that has been middle-of-the-pack against wideouts through two games, allowing 255 receiving yards and two TDs to the position.

player.seasonOutlook: Smith-Njigba is entering his third NFL season following a breakout 2024 in which he ranked top 10 among wide receivers in routes, receptions, yardage and fantasy points (19th in PPG). Operating primarily in a short-area role, "JSN" was, however, limited to six TDs and ranked 16th in end zone targets (11).
