The 2023 first-round pick got more downfield opportunities in 2024 than he did as a rookie and perhaps will get even more in 2025 with DK Metcalf and Tyler Lockett out and Cooper Kupp in as his wide receiver running mate. Smith-Njigba will also have a new playcaller (Klint Kubiak) and quarterback (Sam Darnold), which adds some uncertainty, but the bottom line is he's an emerging star and, at 23 years old, younger than some incoming rookies. Smith-Njigba is a WR2 who could crack the top 10 with another leap forward.

outlooksByWeek.1: Omarion Hampton was the second running back off the board in the 2025 Draft, going 22nd overall, and the UNC product couldn't have asked for a better landing spot. The Chargers adopted a run-heavy scheme last year under new head coach Jim Harbaugh and offensive coordinator Greg Roman, and Hampton should immediately step into a prominent role that capitalizes on his size, athleticism and three-down skill set. Former Steeler Najee Harris was also signed as a free agent to work in tandem with the rookie, but an offseason fireworks accident cost him the entire preseason and training camp and could force the team to introduce him into the offense slowly. Hampton could be in line for a big workload in Week 1, but he faces a tough test right away against a Kansas City defense that ranked in the top four in both rushing yards and receiving yards allowed to RBs last season.
outlooksByWeek.2: Omarion Hampton's volume was strong in his NFL debut, but he wasn't able to do much with it. The Chargers' first-round pick in 2025 turned 17 touches into just 61 scrimmage yards, while veteran Najee Harris gained only 10 yards on two touches. Harris' lack of reps in training camp due to a July fireworks accident almost certainly played a part in that, and offensive coordinator's tendency to deploy a backfield committee could see some of that volume shift from Hampton to Harris. Hampton figures to remain the lead back even if Harris' role in the game plan grows. Hampton will take on a Raiders defense in Week 2 that held another dynamic rookie back, the Patriots' TreVeyon Henderson, to 51 yards on 11 touches in its opener, and which ranked 18th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs in 2024.
outlooksByWeek.3: Omarion Hampton is coming off a rough second game in the NFL. After handling the majority of the work in the Chargers' backfield in Week 1, the rookie running back logged a more even split with veteran Najee Harris in Week 2, and Hampton's fumble in the fourth quarter as the Chargers tried to close out a 20-9 win subjected him to the bench the rest of the way. Hampton averaged just 3.1 yards per carry so far, but he might be missing left tackle Rashawn Slater more than Justin Herbert, as Hampton was met in the backfield by defenders coming off the edge more than once in Week 2. Hampton will try to bounce back in Week 3 against a Broncos defense that just got exploited for 215 scrimmage yards and a TD by the Colts' Jonathan Taylor.

player.seasonOutlook: Hampton was selected by the Chargers in the first round of April's draft. He is a big, tough back whose career 3.85 YAC is fourth best in this class. He's more downhill than he is agile, but he impressed in the 40, vertical and broad at the combine. Hampton is a capable pass catcher, and he figures to land a three-down role in the pros. He'll defer some carries to Najee Harris and targets may be limited in the Jim Harbaugh/Greg Roman scheme, but there will be enough volume to allow RB2 fantasy production.

outlooksByWeek.1: Mike Evans, the model of consistency, will begin the road to a hopeful 12th consecutive 1,000-yard season with the Buccaneers against Atlanta in Week 1. Evans went down with a hamstring injury in the 2024 season which almost knocked him off his streak, but he was able to reach 1,004 yards off 74 receptions even if it was his second-lowest yard total of his career. The veteran wideout is fully healthy heading into this campaign, and he's primed to be the WR1 for Tampa Bay yet again. With his long-term teammate Chris Godwin (ankle) likely out until October and quarterback Baker Mayfield now looking to rookies Emeka Egbuka and Tez Johnson in Godwin's place, Evans could be primed for even more reliance from Mayfield.
outlooksByWeek.2: Mike Evans should continue to be the WR1 in Tampa Bay's offense in an away game versus the Texans in Week 2. Evans brought in five of eight targets for 51 yards in the Bucs' season opener against the Falcons, which ended up being a team-high in catches and target totals and second in receiving yards to rookie receiver Emeka Egbuka. Egbuka's huge season opener shouldn't hurt Evans' output too much moving forward, especially considering the Bucs' offense has been traditionally pass-centered with multiple shootouts last season. Houston also gave up 221 receiving yards to the Rams' wide receivers in Week 1, meaning Evans could be primed for an even bigger workload in the away stint.
outlooksByWeek.3: Mike Evans remains the WR1 for Tampa Bay in a Week 3 matchup against the Jets. Evans led the Bucs in targets and receiving yards against the Texans, making it his second straight week of recording team-high targets. The veteran wide receiver has been sharing looks with an already solid rookie Emeka Egbuka, but the pair should both continue to garner a high volume of targets moving forward. Evans should also be able to leverage a volatile Jets secondary in the upcoming home match, which has ranked middle-of-the-pack against wide receivers so far this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Evans is back for his age-32 campaign having now put up 1,000-plus receiving yards in 11 straight seasons to begin his career. The future Hall of Famer missed three games in 2024, but still scored double-digit touchdowns for the fourth time in five seasons. Incredibly, Evans has never finished a season worse than 23rd in fantasy points (26th in PPG). Age aside, there are some concerns here, as Evans was very boom/bust in 2024, having posted six top-10 fantasy outings (second most), while also falling short of 12 points in seven of his other eight games. He also benefited massively from Chris Godwin's season-ending injury, averaging 6.3 targets and 13.6 fantasy PPG with him, but 9.1 targets and 20.7 PPG without. Despite the concerns, Evans hasn't shown signs of slowing down and has a good QB in Baker Mayfield. He's a fringe fantasy WR2.

outlooksByWeek.1: RJ Harvey was fifth running back off the board in the 2025 NFL Draft, going 60th overall to the Broncos; he may have found an ideal landing spot. The UCF product offers both tackle-breaking potential and strong receiving skills, making him a chess piece that coach Sean Payton might be able use to his maximum potential in the same way that he did Alvin Kamara in New Orleans. Harvey's ceiling to begin his career may have been capped when the team signed J.K. Dobbins in June, but the brittle veteran is only on a one-year deal and highly unlikely to play all 17 regular-season games given his checkered injury history. Harvey could hit the ground running on his NFL career at home in Week 1 against a Titans defense that gave up the most receiving TDs (seven) and total TDs (22) in the league to running backs last year.
outlooksByWeek.2: RJ Harvey flashed his big-play potential in his NFL debut, turning six carries into 70 yards in a Week 1 win over the Titans. Veteran J.K. Dobbins logged 18 touches, and Harvey may be stuck in a change-of-pace role until he proves to Broncos head coach Sean Payton that he's ready for a bigger workload. The 2025 second-round pick may also need to sharpen his receiving skills after turning his only target into minus-1 yards. Even on limited carries, Harvey could pop for another couple chunk plays in Week 2 against a Colts defense that gave up 7.9 yards per carry to De'Von Achane in its opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: RJ Harvey couldn't build on his promising NFL debut, managing just eight rushing yards on five carries in a Week 2 loss to the Colts. He did add a 16-yard reception, but the 2025 second-round pick garnered significantly less volume than veteran J.K. Dobbins, and that arrangement in the Broncos' backfield will likely remain in place until Harvey shows head coach Sean Payton he can deliver more consistent production. Harvey also has yet to collect a red-zone touch, with Dobbins handling that role exclusively for Denver through two games. Harvey isn't likely to break out in Week 3 against a stingy Chargers defense that just held Raiders' rookie Ashton Jeanty to 44 scrimmage yards on 14 touches.

player.seasonOutlook: Harvey was selected by Denver in the second round of April's draft. He is on the small side (5-foot-8, 205 pounds), but he plays tough and is productive, having run for 10-plus yards on a class-best 23% of his carries last season. Size and age (24) concerns aside, he showed well at the combine, including a 4.40 40, 38-inch vertical and 127-inch broad jump. Harvey's landing spot is very good, as fellow newcomer J.K. Dobbins is his primary competition for work. The duo may split carries, but Harvey is a good bet to emerge as the primary receiving back, which is notable in a Sean Payton offense that often leans heavily on RBs in the passing game. Harvey is a fringe RB2 target, but there's upside for even more.

outlooksByWeek.1: The Steelers selected Kaleb Johnson in the third round of the 2025 NFL Draft with the purpose of replacing Najee Harris as the lead back. Johnson had an inconsistent preseason, often struggling in pass protection and catching balls out of the backfield. While Johnson is likely to lead the Pittsburgh backfield at some point in 2025, it doesn't appear likely to come in Week 1 against the Jets. Johnson is a worthwhile stash, but he's best left on fantasy benches to begin his career.
outlooksByWeek.2: Kaleb Johnson served as Pittsburgh's No. 3 running back in Week 1, logging only one rushing attempt. He was as the team's primary kick returner, though he also fumbled on his five returns. Kenneth Gainwell was ineffective as the team's backup running back, so there is still hope for Johnson's role to expand relatively quickly. However, he's only a stash on the bench in Week 2 against Seattle.

player.seasonOutlook: Johnson was selected by Pittsburgh in the third round of April's draft. He isn't super-fast (4.57 40-yard dash) or quick (1.62 10-yard split), which limited his output at Iowa (only 34% of runs went for 5-plus yards), but he's one of the biggest backs in this class. He's seemingly a capable receiver, but didn't do it much in college (38 targets) and needs work as a pass blocker, so his fantasy ceiling might be a bit limited. That's especially the case with Jaylen Warren positioned to handle upward of half of the carries and most of the passing-down work. Johnson may eventually emerge as the de facto Najee Harris replacement in run-heavy Pittsburgh, so he's well worth a midround flier, but don't be surprised if he gets off to a slow start.

outlooksByWeek.1: Dak Prescott had an underwhelming 2024 campaign for the Dallas Cowboys, but could be a candidate for a bounce back season in 2025. The Cowboys added talented wideout George Pickens to complement No. 1 receiver CeeDee Lamb, and Dallas also returns tight end Jake Ferguson along with Jalen Tolbert, the latter of which had a career year with 49 grabs for 610 yards and seven touchdowns last season. Likewise, the Cowboys could be playing from behind in many contests, and also be involved in a plethora of shootouts, given the recent trade of dynamic pass rusher Micah Parsons. Unfortunately, the Week 1 matchup against the Eagles is less than ideal.  Philadelphia allowed the fewest passing yards in the NFL last season, just 174.2 yards per clash through the air.
outlooksByWeek.2: Dak Prescott failed to pass for over 200 yards or throw a touchdown in the season opener for the Cowboys. However, the matchup was far from ideal against the defending Super Bowl champs, and Dak was not helped by a couple of drops from CeeDee Lamb and the lack of chemistry with new toy George Pickens. In Week 2, the level of competition drops, as the Cowboys host the bumbling New York Giants. Still, the Giants have a revamped defense, including a stellar pass rush and new additions on the back end, though still allowed 212 passing yards and a touchdown through the air in their season opener. Dak tossed two touchdowns in the only matchup he played between the two division opponents in 2024.
outlooksByWeek.3: Dak Prescott bounced back from a rusty season opener to torch the New York Giants in Week 2. Dak completed 38-of-52 passes for 361 yards, two touchdowns and one interception in the wild, seesaw battle with the G-Men. If the Cowboys defense continues to struggle, Dak could find himself in plenty of shootouts this season, including in Week 3 versus the Chicago Bears. The Bears are allowing the most points in the NFL thus far this season, an average of 39.5 points per tilt. That includes 52 points that the Detroit Lions just hung on them in Week 2.

player.seasonOutlook: Prescott returns for his age-32 campaign following a disappointing and injury-shortened 2024. In eight games, Prescott totaled 11 TDs and eight INTs through the air and wasn't much of a factor with his legs (career-low 54 yards). He averaged 14.6 fantasy PPG (16.8 in the six games he played in full), which was a far cry from the 20.2 (fifth highest) he averaged in 2023. Prescott has now missed multiple games in three of the past five seasons, though he has also been a top-8 fantasy QB (PPG) three times during the span. Adding George Pickens to a supporting cast that also includes CeeDee Lamb and Jake Ferguson is helpful, but because of the concerning dip in rushing, the 10-year vet is best viewed as fringe QB1.

outlooksByWeek.1: Jauan Jennings has been dealing with a calf injury while also seeking a new contract from San Francisco, making his status for Week 1 against Seattle iffy. If he does play, Jennings should be a prominent target for QB Brock Purdy, as Brandon Aiyuk is sidelined until at least Week 5 while recovering from a torn ACL while Deebo Samuel is now in Washington. Jennings was very productive with an increased role late last season, averaging 5.8 catches for 63.4 yards while scoring three touchdowns over the final nine weeks of the campaign. Meanwhile, the Seahawks' secondary returns most of the same players from last season, when the unit gave up 19 receiving TDs to wideouts -- tied for sixth-most in the league.
outlooksByWeek.2: Jauan Jennings will hope to suit up for San Francisco in Week 2 against New Orleans, but he's iffy with a shoulder injury. The wideout was hurt early in the fourth quarter Week 1 against Seattle after catching two of five targets for 16 yards. If he does suit up Sunday, Jennings will be facing a Saints squad that allowed Arizona's top wideout, Marvin Harrison, to collect 71 receiving yards and a touchdown on five receptions Week 1. However, if Jennings can't play, Ricky Pearsall would be San Francisco's clear-cut No. 1 wideout.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jauan Jennings picked up an ankle injury in San Francisco's win over the Saints on Sunday and is iffy to suit up in Week 3 against the Cardinals. If he does play, Jennings will be looking to build upon his five-catch, 89-yard, one-touchdown effort versus New Orleans. That was a much more productive performance than in Week 1, when Jennings tallied just two catches for 16 yards. The 49ers will likely start Mac Jones at quarterback again in Week 3, as Brock Purdy is unlikely to suit up due to toe and shoulder injuries, but Jones and Jennings showed enough chemistry in Week 2 to be optimistic about another strong connection between the pair. The Cardinals present a beatable opponent, as they've given up 320 receiving yards and two scores to wideouts despite a 56.7 percent catch rate through two weeks.

player.seasonOutlook: After three seasons playing a depth role, Jennings enjoyed a breakout in 2024. The 2020 seventh-round pick soaked up a 25% target share en route to a top-30 finish among WRs in targets, catches, yards, TDs, end zone targets and fantasy points (27th in PPG). His 46.5-point effort in Week 3 was the third-highest total posted in a single week last season. Jennings' usage benefited from injuries above him on the depth chart, but with Deebo Samuel Sr. gone and Brandon Aiyuk expected to miss roughly half the season, he's again ticketed for a big role in 2025. Jennings, who ranked 11th among WRs in yards per route run, is a viable flex target, though a slow start is possible after he missed significant chunk of offseason activities.

outlooksByWeek.1: Travis Etienne is likely to be part of a timeshare in Jacksonville's backfield against the Panthers in Week 1. A near-even split with Tank Bigsby is expected, while rookie draft picks Bhayshul Tuten (fourth round) and LeQuint Allen (seventh round) could also crack the rotation. The Panthers allowed the most rushing yards and points in the NFL last season, so Etienne is a strong flex play in this favorable matchup despite the workload concerns. Etienne topped 1,400 scrimmage yards in both 2022 and 2023 before dropping to 812 last season, and he's a far better pass catcher than Bigsby, who had 820 scrimmage yards in 2024 but only 54 through the air.
outlooksByWeek.2: Travis Etienne is back in the fantasy RB2 mix heading into Week 2 against the Bengals after reestablishing himself as the lead back in Jacksonville's season-opening win over the Panthers. Etienne slipped into a timeshare with Tank Bigsby last season, but the former had 143 rushing yards on 16 carries in Week 1, while Bigsby, Bhayshul Tuten and LeQuint Allen combined for nine carries and 30 rushing yards. Bigsby was then traded to the Eagles on Monday. Carolina's run defense was historically bad last season while the Bengals were closer to average, but Etienne's three-down skill set gives him a high touch floor in any matchup. Cincinnati's defense held Cleveland's underwhelming RB group to 40 yards on 21 carries last week, though Dylan Sampson had eight catches and Raheim Sanders scored a rushing TD against the Bengals.
outlooksByWeek.3: Travis Etienne is thriving as Jacksonville's lead back, with 245 scrimmage yards and one touchdown heading into a Week 3 home game against the Texans. Houston has been among the best teams at defending running backs since the start of last season, but Etienne's three-down skill set makes him a trustworthy fantasy RB2 despite the difficult Week 3 matchup. After the Jaguars traded Tank Bigsby to Philadelphia, Etienne handled 16 touches in the 31-27 Week 2 loss to the Bengals, while Bhayshul Tuten collected 10 touches and LeQuint Allen had two.

player.seasonOutlook: Etienne enters his first contract year with eyes on a bounce-back following a rough 2024. After clearing 1,400 yards in both 2022 and 2023 (finishing third among RBs in touches and fantasy points in the latter), Etienne plummeted to career-low marks in touches, yards and TDs last season. After finding the end zone in Weeks 1 and 2, he went without a TD or a fantasy point total above 14.8 the rest of the season. He's still in his prime at age 26, but Etienne's efficiency has been weak two seasons in a row and he's no longer a lock for lead-back duties, with Tank Bigsby ticketed for a big role and fourth-round rookie Bhayshul Tuten now in the mix. Perhaps new coach Liam Coen can get things turned around, but Etienne is best viewed as a bench flier.

outlooksByWeek.1: Tucker Kraft will kick off a potential breakout campaign as the Packers prepare to host the Lions in Week 1. As a rookie two seasons ago, Kraft split playing time with fellow 2023 Day 2 pick Luke Musgrave, but he emerged as Green Bay's clear starting TE in 2024 and played 75-plus percent of snaps in all but two of his 17 appearances. Coach Matt LaFleur's run-heavy approach limited Kraft's production, as he averaged just 3.9 targets per game, but he'll demand more involvement Year 3 after having led all TEs with a tremendous 9.6 yards after the catch. Kraft has a path to opening 2025 with substantially more involvement - LaFleur has expressed a desire to return to a more balanced offense, but beyond Romeo Doubs, one of Green Bay's starting wideouts is playing through a Jones fracture in Jayden Reed, while the other - Matthew Golden - is a rookie and could need time to establish consistency.
outlooksByWeek.2: Tucker Kraft will work to continue establishing himself as a true TE breakout as the Packers take on the Commanders on Thursday night in Week 2. He brought in two of four targets for 16 yards and a score Week 1, one of two touchdowns Jordan Love threw versus Detroit. Green Bay was able to convincingly trounce the Lions without leaning much on the passing game, as after getting out to an early lead the team's stout defense, led by new star DE Micah Parsons, was able to wrap things up. Going back to 2024, however, Kraft has now drawn at least four targets in six of his last eight appearances, and he's solidified not only as the Packers' top tight end above Luke Musgrave (one target Week 1), but alongside Jayden Reed, Romeo Doubs and Matthew Golden as one of Love's clear top targets in the receiving game.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tucker Kraft and the Packers will travel to Cleveland in WeekaA�3, as the tight end looks to build on what's shaping up to be an impressive breakout season. He paced Green Bay's pass catchers with a tremendous 6-124-1 receiving line on seven targets during last Thursday's win over the Commanders and has now scored in back-to-back games to kick off the regular season. Part of the reason for Kraft's dominant performance can be attributed to Jayden Reed leaving on the first drive with a shoulder injury, freeing up opportunities in the short-to-intermediate areas of the field, but that doesn't detract from the obvious gamebreaking abilities the third-year TE has put on tape. The Browns' defense has shown vulnerability to tight ends over the middle, particularly in coverage rotations, providing Kraft with a high ceiling Week 3, especially if Reed is limited or sidelined. He's the Packers' most consistent red-zone weapon aside from RB Josh Jacobs.

player.seasonOutlook: Kraft took over as the Packers' No. 1 tight end in Week 12 of the 2023 season and hasn't looked back. In the 27 games since (including the playoffs), Kraft averaged 4.3 targets and 9.4 fantasy points per game. He played 85% of Green Bay's offensive snaps in 2024 and while his volume was underwhelming (18th among TEs in targets and receptions), he was productive (seventh in yards and fourth in touchdowns). Kraft finished second at the position in yards per reception and yards per target, as well as first in RAC for the second season in a row. Kraft finished 15th in fantasy PPG and he'll need additional volume in 2025 in order to leap into the weekly TE1 mix. The 24-year-old has some upside, but he's safest as a good TE2.

outlooksByWeek.1: Jake Ferguson battled injury and an inconsistent passing game last season, failing to capitalize on his breakout campaign from 2023 with the Cowboys. Ferguson finished the 2024 season with 59 catches for 494 yards and zero touchdowns. Ferguson averaged a career-low 8.4 yards per grab. Ferguson will look to bounce back in 2025, though will likely have some more competition for targets. The Cowboys brought in mercurial wideout George Pickens to complement CeeDee Lamb. Jalen Tolbert also remains following a career season. Though the Cowboys could be involved in plenty of shootouts given the situation regarding the defense, Week 1 is a difficult matchup against the Eagles.  Philadelphia allowed just 174.2 passing yards per tilt in 2024, which led the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.2: Jake Ferguson had a busy season opener for the Cowboys. Ferguson caught five passes on six targets, though gained just 23 yards in the 24-20 loss to the Eagles. The Dallas passing game was largely grounded, though Ferguson still finished second on the squad in receptions and third in receiving yardage for the game. The passing attack as a whole should find more success in Week 2 versus the New York Giants. However, the Giants allowed just 212 passing yards and a single passing touchdown in their season opener against the Washington Commanders.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jake Ferguson was heavily involved in a Week 2 win for the Cowboys, leading the squad in targets in the OT triumph over the Giants. Ferguson received 12 targets en route to nine catches for 78 yards, even outpacing CeeDee Lamb in terms of looks. Ferguson could be in line for another big outing in Week 3 versus a struggling Bears defense. Chicago has allowed the most points in the NFL through two weeks, including a league-worst seven receiving touchdowns.

player.seasonOutlook: Ferguson enters 2025 with eyes on a rebound after he fell from 10th in fantasy PPG in 2023 to 23rd last season. He essentially missed four full games, but still finished ninth among TEs in targets. The main issue was touchdowns, as he fell from five scores and a position-high 10 end zone targets in 2023 to zero TDs and two end zone targets in 2024. His 88 targets were easily the most among all players without a TD catch. Having Dak Prescott back will help, as Ferguson averaged 10.2 fantasy PPG in seven games with Prescott (not far off his 10.4 PPG in 2023), compared to 5.2 PPG in six full games when he was out. Ferguson is a solid TE2 who could flirt with weekly top-12 numbers.

outlooksByWeek.1: Braelon Allen enters Week 1 for the Jets in search of a breakout against the Steelers. All reports indicate he's in line for a split with Breece Hall rather than being a backup. Given that the Jets figure to be one of the heaviest rushing teams in the league with Justin Fields under center, there's likely room for to coexist. It's a bit of a leap of faith to deploy Allen as a flex option in this opener until his usage is visible, but a matchup against a defense that allowed 4.3 yards per carry last season isn't one from which to immediately shy away.
outlooksByWeek.2: Braelon Allen hopes to improve his efficiency for the Jets in Week 2 against the Bills. While Allen scored on an eight-yard run in Week 1, he ended with nine yards on six carries while Breece Hall topped 100 yards while averaging better than five yards per carry. Much of the offseason talk was about a split backfield, but for one week, Allen looks like a touchdown vulture at best, even in a run heavy Jets attack. Buffalo allowed 160 yards and two touchdowns on the ground last week, but Allen will need to show it before he can be trusted as a reliable flex option.
outlooksByWeek.3: Braelon Allen experienced a limited early workload for the Jets heading into a Week 3 matchup against the Buccaneers. Through two weeks, Allen is without a catch and has only eight carries for 20 yards with Breece Hall dominating backfield touches. While always a threat to score if the Jets get inside the 10-yard line, Allen's current usage does not make him fantasy relevant except as Hall's insurance policy, something unlikely to change against a defense that's allowing just 2.8 yards per carry.

player.seasonOutlook: Allen is back for Year 2 in New York after soaking up 111 touches as a rookie. The 2024 fourth-round pick quickly stepped into a change-of-pace role behind Breece Hall and was utilized as both a rusher (5.4 carries per game) and receiver (1.7 targets per game). His efficiency wasn't overly impressive (3.6 YPC, 5.1 YPT) and he eventually deferred some work to 2024 fifth-rounder Isaiah Davis, but it's notable that he's still one of the league's youngest backs at 21-years-old. Despite speculation of a committee approach, Hall figures to remain the lead, or at least �1A' back this season, with Allen and Davis battling for the rest of the touches. That won't be enough for consistent fantasy output. Allen is only worth a late pick in deep leagues.

outlooksByWeek.1: Wil Lutz thrived in his second season with the Broncos, converting all 46 of his extra-point attempts and connecting on better than 90% of his field goals for the first time since 2018, going 31-for-34. He also set a career high with five FGs of 50 yards or more on seven attempts, as kicking at altitude proved to be even more advantageous than kicking indoors in New Orleans. Lutz's PAT volume increased significantly as rookie QB Bo Nix took the reins, and the entire Denver offense could be even more productive in 2025 due to further development from Nix and offseason improvements in the backfield and at tight end. Lutz may be a high-floor, low-ceiling option in Week 1 against a Titans team that allowed the second-most PAT attempts in the league in 2024 but tied for the sixth-fewest FG attempts.
outlooksByWeek.2: Wil Lutz was perfect in the Broncos' Week 1 win, connecting on both his field goals attempts and both his extra point tries. The veteran kicker thrived at altitude the prior two seasons, converting 89.7 percent of his FG chances, including an 8-for-12 performance on kicks from 50 yards or more. Lutz has attempted exactly 34 FGs each of the last two years, but his volume in that area could increase, at the expense of his PATs, if Bo Nix and the Denver offense continue to have trouble finishing off drives. Lutz will face a Colts squad in Week 2 that allowed 7.9 points per game to kickers in 2024, tied for 20th in the leagues.
outlooksByWeek.3: Wil Lutz's first missed field goal of the season proved to be very costly, as he clanked a 42-yard kick off the upright in the fourth quarter in a 29-28 loss to the Colts in Week 2. The veteran kicker has otherwise been perfect in 2025, converting his other two FG attempts and all six of his PAT. Lutz's extra-point volume increased significantly in the second half of last season as Broncos quarterback Bo Nix broke out, and that pattern has held so far to begin the current campaign. It figures to get broken in Week 3 however, as Denver takes on a Chargers team that's given up six FG through two weeks but only two touchdowns.

player.seasonOutlook: In his first season as defensive coordinator, Jeff Hafley squeezed a lot from this unit, which finished third in the league in fantasy points (8.2 per game). All-Pro S Xavier McKinney, LB Edgerrin Cooper and DE Rashan Gary return to comprise the heart of the Packers' defense, which, due to a lack of cornerback depth, should be susceptible to the matchups. The opening two weeks are ones to avoid (DET, WAS), but the season's middle chunks should provide fantasy managers opportunities.

outlooksByWeek.1: Romeo Doubs will kick off Year 4, the final season of his rookie deal, at home in Green Bay versus the division-rival Lions in Week 1. He's positioned to reprise a familiar starting role in the Packers' crowded wide receiver corps, which added significant target competition this offseason via rookie first-rounder Matthew Golden. Still, Golden may need a few games to ramp up his involvement on offense even if his career gets off to a hot start, and fellow starter Jayden Reed (foot) missed much of the preseason and appears to be playing through a Jones fracture. That positions Reed - and TE Tucker Kraft - as arguably the most consistent pass-catchers available for QB Jordan Love, at least to begin the year. The trust Doubs has earned from Love is a fair argument for him to kick off the season averaging more than the 5.5 targets per game he did in 2024.
outlooksByWeek.2: Romeo Doubs and the Packers will take on the Commanders in Week 2, looking to turn his Week 1 fireworks into consistent fantasy value. He turned just four targets into two receptions for 68 yards in Week 1 versus the Lions, including a career-long 48-yard catch. That game saw Doubs lead the team in routes run and log 34 of the team's 48 offensive snaps, 11 more than any other receiver. Washington managed to limit the Giants' passing game to a total of 168 yards, relying heavily on off-man zones to suffocate perimeter speed, but Doubs' versatility will leave him open for opportunities if the team devotes extra safety help to Jayden Reed or rookie speedster Matthew Golden.
outlooksByWeek.3: Romeo Doubs and the Packers travel to Cleveland in Week 3, aiming to extend their undefeated start after a 27-18 win over Washington in which he caught three of four targets for 27 yards and a score. With Jayden Reed having exited early Week 2 due to a shoulder injury, Doubs' role in the offense becomes even more pivotal. The Browns' defense boasts a solid secondary, even if its pass rush gets the most attention, but Doubs' chemistry with Love and his knack for finding the end zone make him a high-upside WR3 in fantasy leagues this week. He's drawn exactly four targets in back-to-back games to kick off the 2025 season.

player.seasonOutlook: Doubs returns to Green Bay for his fourth NFL season. The 2022 fourth-round pick leads the team in targets (237), receptions (147), receiving yards (1,700) and receiving TDs (15) since his arrival, but that's resulted in only 9.5 fantasy points per game. He peaked with a 59-674-8 receiving line in 2023 and has yet to post a top-45 fantasy season (PPG). The 25-year-old has minimal upside (zero top-10 fantasy outings last season) and substantial competition for targets, with rookies Matthew Golden and Savion Williams joining a WR group that also includes Jayden Reed, Dontayvion Wicks and eventually Christian Watson (ACL recovery). Add in an offensive scheme that leans heavily on Josh Jacobs near the goal line and Doubs' inconsistent usage and limited upside makes him no more than a bench option in fantasy.

outlooksByWeek.1: Christian McCaffrey will be one of the centerpieces of San Francisco's offense in Week 1 versus Seattle. McCaffrey missed all but four games last season due to injuries but is reportedly healthy heading into the regular season despite not playing in any exhibition games. As long as he remains uninjured, McCaffrey will likely get plenty of opportunities in a San Francisco offense that is an ideal system for his skill set, though the team did trade for a very capable veteran backup in Brian Robinson. The Seahawks present an exploitable Week 1 matchup, as their defense ranked in the bottom third of the league by giving up 4.6 YPC to RBs last year.
outlooksByWeek.2: Christian McCaffrey could be asked to carry a heavy load for the 49ers in Week 2 against the Saints. The star RB certainly did so in Week 1, tallying 142 yards from scrimmage on 22 carries and nine receptions against Seattle. Talented tight end George Kittle isn't expected to play Week 2 due to a hamstring injury, while starting QB Brock Purdy (toe/shoulder) and starting wideout Jauan Jennings (shoulder) are iffy due to injuries of their own, so McCaffrey could be asked to carry the team even more on offense. He'll face off against a Saints defense that allowed the Cardinals to gain 146 yards on 27 carries in a Week 1 loss, though Arizona starting RB James Conner went for just 39 yards on 12 rushes.
outlooksByWeek.3: Christian McCaffrey will likely again be tasked with carrying San Francisco's banged-up offense into a Week 3 matchup versus the Cardinals. Starting QB Brock Purdy (toe/shoulder) is unlikely to suit up, while star tight end George Kittle (hamstring) is on IR and starting WR Jauan Jennings is iffy due to an ankle injury. That could leave a heavy workload on McCaffrey's shoulders, but the talented tailback has been able to carry the weight so far, recording 50 touches (35 carries and 15 receptions) for 249 yards and a touchdown through two weeks. Arizona's defense has been pretty good against the run so far this year, yielding just 3.68 YPC to the Saints and Panthers, though McCaffrey's skill set as a pass catcher makes him dangerous even if the Cardinals' run defense continues to hold up well.

player.seasonOutlook: McCaffrey returns for his age-29 season eyeing a bounce-back after an injury-plagued 2024 that limited him to three full games. McCaffrey wasn't even his usual, elite self during those weeks (13.0 fantasy PPG), though he did play 88% of the snaps and average 18.7 touches per game. Prior to the 2024 debacle, McCaffrey had finished six straight seasons ranked in the top 5 among RBs in fantasy PPG and he remains positioned for feature back duties in a good 49ers offense. There's obvious risk here considering the injury woes and age, but in weeks he's active McCaffrey will be an elite fantasy option.

outlooksByWeek.1: Brian Thomas begins his sophomore season with a Week 1 home game against the Panthers, who allowed the second-most TD catches to WRs last season. Thomas is the top dog in Jacksonville's receiving corps after posting 87 catches for 1,282 yards and 10 TDs as a rookie, and he remains focused on offense only while rookie second overall pick Travis Hunter is expected to play both WR and CB. One of the few notable players on Carolina's underwhelming defense is CB Jaycee Horn, who could spend most of the game shadowing Thomas, but Thomas is nonetheless locked in as a fantasy WR1 for Week 1, and he's likely to stay in that range all season after finishing his rookie campaign as WR4 overall.
outlooksByWeek.2: Brian Thomas salvaged a quiet receiving day by scoring a rushing TD in Jacksonville's season opener, but the second-year pro will look to get on the same page with Trevor Lawrence in Week 2 against the Bengals. Thomas was limited to one catch on seven Week 1 targets while struggling to separate from top Panther CB Jaycee Horn. Cincinnati has a below-average defense and lacks a defender of Horn's caliber to throw at Thomas, so Thomas has a nice opportunity to bounce back with a performance reminiscent of the ones he put up consistently en route to 87 catches for 1,282 yards and 10 TDs as a rookie last season. Thomas remains locked in as a fantasy WR1 and could be a nice buy-low trade candidate from reactionary fantasy managers.
outlooksByWeek.3: Brian Thomas has just 60 receiving yards on 19 targets through two games, but he has a nice opportunity to get back on track Week 3 against a Texans defense that allowed 21 receiving TDs to WRs in 2024, tied for second-most in the NFL. Thomas scored in both of his games against Houston last season, undeterred by the presence of standout CB Derek Stingley. While Thomas hasn't been on the same page as Trevor Lawrence to begin the 2025 campaign, the 2024 first-round pick continues to garner heavy volume and has the skills to break out at any moment. Thomas should continue to be treated as a fantasy WR1 despite the slow start, as long as the wrist injury he played through last week doesn't worsen.

player.seasonOutlook: Three. That's the number of wide receivers selected before Thomas in the 2024 draft and it's also the number of wide receivers who outscored him in fantasy during his rookie season. The LSU product finished in the top 5 among receivers in both yards and TDs despite ranking 29th in routes and 19th in targets. Thomas' volume will need to increase in Year 2 in order to sustain WR1 fantasy production and, while it's reasonable to expect that boost, it's worth noting he had six 10-plus target games with backup Mac Jones (22.9 fantasy PPG those six weeks) but zero with starter Trevor Lawrence (14.4). The bottom line is Thomas appears to be the real deal and, even with Travis Hunter added to the mix, he has a path to a massive target share in a Liam Coen scheme that was extremely generous to Tampa Bay's wide receivers. Thomas is a good back-end WR1 target.

outlooksByWeek.1: Tyreek Hill will look to turn the page on a down 2024 and tumultuous offseason when the Dolphins face the Colts in Week 1. Hill failed to top 1,000 yards for the first time since 2019 and tied a career-low with six touchdowns last season. Perhaps his speed is fading with age, but Hill appears to be healthy entering this matchup and will likely again offer one of the highest ceilings of any receiver in the league. Given the discount he came with on draft day, Hill likely slots as a WR2 or WR3 in most lineups against a defense that allowed the 13th most fantasy points to opposing receivers in 2024.
outlooksByWeek.2: Tyreek Hill looks to stretch the field for the Dolphins in Week 2 against the Patriots. While Hill's four catch, six target, 40-yard outing is subpar, Hill still led Miami in all categories. Keep an eye on the availability of CB Christian Gonzalez, who missed Week 1. The Patriots allowed 362 passing yards last week, and if Gonzalez is again sidelined, Hill could be in for an outing reminiscent of his salad days.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tyreek Hill and the Dolphins face the Bills in Week 3 Thursday night. Hill is coming off of his first 100-yard game of the season and is averaging 18.2 yards per reception. Buffalo allowed the 10th fewest fantasy points to wide receivers in the early going, and Hill didn't flash against them last year, posting just seven catches on 11 targets for 104 yards. With steady volume and a game script that figures to force Miami to pass often, Hill should remain a low end WR2/top end WR3.

player.seasonOutlook: Hill is eyeing a rebound campaign following what was undoubtedly the most disappointing season of his career. Granted, he wasn't fully healthy, but Hill appeared in all 17 games and still managed to see a massive dip in targets, catches, yardage, TDs and fantasy points, compared to his first two seasons in Miami. Hill finished 31st among WRs in fantasy PPG after ranking no lower than 11th the prior seven seasons. It didn't help that Tua Tagovailoa missed six games (Hill averaged 9.0 PPG in those weeks), but he wasn't his usual, elite self even with Tagovailoa (14.9 PPG). Hill was the No. 2 fantasy WR three of four seasons before the 2024 dud, so a potential rebound season is worth factoring in, but it's not a lock as he enters his age-31 campaign. He's safest as a WR2 with upside.

outlooksByWeek.1: Patrick Mahomes is coming off his least productive NFL season in 2024, passing for 3,928 yards over 16 regular-season games on 6.8 yards per attempt with 26 touchdown passes, all career lows. Kansas City's front office has invested draft capital in trying to give the QB the weapons necessary to revive the passing game, but while 2024 first-round pick Xavier Worthy showed flashes of upside and game-breaking speed, 2023 second-round pick Rashee Rice played only four games last year due to a knee injury and is set to miss the first six in 2025 due to a suspension. Mahomes' veteran partner in crime, tight end Travis Kelce, also saw his yards per target crater in 2024 as the 35-year-old enters the twilight of his career. Mahomes and company will head to Sao Paulo in Week 1 to take on the Chargers, whose defense finished in the top 10 in fewest passing yards allowed and most interceptions last year.
outlooksByWeek.2: Patrick Mahomes posted respectable numbers in Week 1 despite more attrition in Kansas City's wide receiver corps. The veteran quarterback threw for 258 yards and a touchdown while adding another 57 yards and a TD on the ground, but he watched Xavier Worthy leave the game with a shoulder injury after a collision with Travis Kelce. Worthy joins a suspended Rashee Rice on the sidelines, and while he may avoid surgery for his dislocated shoulder, he's almost certain to miss some time while rehabbing and adjusting to wearing a brace. Mahomes will try to make do with a patchwork group of targets led by Kelce and Hollywood Brown in Week 2 against an Eagles defense that held Dak Prescott and the Cowboys' passing game in check in its opener, and which ranked second in passing yards allowed in 2024.
outlooksByWeek.3: Patrick Mahomes produced one passing and one rushing touchdown in each of Kansas City's first two games, but his passing yardage and completion percentage are both below his usual rates while the team deals with multiple absences in its receiving corps. The veteran quarterback showed some chemistry with Hollywood Brown in Week 1 and found Tyquan Thornton for a deep TD in Week 2, but that hasn't been enough to get the team into the win column. Xavier Worthy could return for a Week 3 contest against the Giants, but he's unlikely to be 100% as he attempts to play through a shoulder injury. After facing two tough defenses to begin the year, Mahomes should have an easier time against a Giants unit that just surrendered 361 passing yards to Dak Prescott in an OT loss to the Cowboys.

player.seasonOutlook: Mahomes enters his age-29 season no longer an elite fantasy option, but rather a solid mid-to-back-end starter. After five straight seasons as a top-6 fantasy QB (PPG), he's finished 13th and 11th the past two seasons. Mahomes has evolved into a quarterback who still attempts a ton of passes (exactly third in pass attempts four years in a row), but is more conservative (career-low 6.4 aDOT and 6.8 YPA in 2024) and doesn't throw as many TDs as in years past (26 last season was his fewest since 2019). Perhaps he'll rebound a bit in that area with the Xavier Worthy/Rashee Rice/Hollywood Brown trio together, but in the meantime Mahomes adds just enough with his legs (between 300 and 400 yards five seasons in a row) to keep him in the fantasy starter conversation.

outlooksByWeek.1: Aaron Jones and new backfield mate Jordan Mason will lead Minnesota's rushing attack on the road at Chicago in Week 1. The Bears allowed the third-most rushing yards in the league last season, so in what will be quarterback J.J. McCarthy's regular-season debut, and the first week of WR Jordan Addison's three-game suspension, it wouldn't be surprising to see Minnesota lean especially heavily on the run. While Mason figures to work in on early downs and be the favorite in short-yardage situations, Jones is fresh off a 2024 campaign in which he suited up for all 17 regular-season games and rushed for a career-best 1,138 yards, and he should remain the team's clear RB1.
outlooksByWeek.2: Aaron Jones will continue working alongside Jordan Mason out of the backfield as the Vikings prepare for a Week 2 primetime matchup against the Falcons. The veteran rushed eight times for 23 yards in Week 1's narrow win over the Bears but flashed more as a receiver, securing all three of his targets for 44 yards and a score. Mason, meanwhile, led the backfield with 15 carries and appeared definitely ahead of Jones in terms of between-the-tackles work. A 30-year-old veteran coming off a career-high 225 carries in 2024, Jones now appears positioned for more of a complementary role alongside Mason, which could play well to his strengths. For Jones to be a high-end producer while surrendering significant rushing volume to Mason, however, he'll need new quarterback J.J. McCarthy to regularly pass for more than the 143 yards he did in his debut.
outlooksByWeek.3: Aaron Jones is expected to sit out the Vikings' matchup against the Bengals in Week 3 due to a hamstring injury sustained in Week 2. He was quiet before being forced out in the fourth quarter of that loss to Atlanta, rushing just five times for 23 yards while failing to haul in his only target. Jordan Mason wasn't much more effective versus the Falcons, finishing the game with just nine carries for 30 yards. If Jones isn't able to go in Week 3, Mason will inherit a clear bell cow role versus an exploitable Cincinnati defense.

player.seasonOutlook: Jones re-signed with Minnesota after a successful 2024 campaign, in which he appeared in all 17 regular-season games and ranked top 10 among RBs in carries, targets, touches and yards. Jones, who played a career-high 64% of the offensive snaps, was effective as a rusher and receiver but had the league's worst touchdown luck (seven TDs, 12.8 expected), which limited him to a 20th-place finish in fantasy PPG. Scoring regression is a strong bet in 2025, but Jones is now 30 years old, working in a pass-first scheme and will defer work (perhaps substantial work) to newcomer Jordan Mason. Jones should be viewed as a flex option.

outlooksByWeek.1: Travis Kelce caught more than 90 passes for the seventh straight season in 2024, becoming only the third tight end in NFL history with more than 1,000 career receptions after Tony Gonzalez and Jason Witten. The rest of Kelce's numbers showed serious signs of decline, including a career-worst 8.5 yards per catch, and the 35-year-old appears to be nearing the end of the road. He's still a vital part of the Kansas City passing game and Patrick Mahomes' favorite security blanket, but he's lost a step and can no longer threaten defenses for consistent big gains. Kelce seems unlikely to make a big splash on a trip to Sao Paulo in Week 1 to face a Chargers defense that gave up only two touchdowns to TEs last season, tied for the lowest mark in the league.
outlooksByWeek.2: Travis Kelce caught his first touchdown in 2025 in Week 1 as part of a 2-47 line on four targets, but his biggest impact came in the first quarter when he collided with Xavier Worthy and knocked the wideout from the game. The low target volume continues a worrying trend for Kelce, as he notched double-digit targets only twice in his final 10 games last season including the playoffs. The veteran tight end should still have a consistent role in the Kansas City passing game given the team's injuries at WR and his established rapport with Patrick Mahomes. Kelce will take on an Eagles defense in Week 2 that gave up the fewest receiving yards in the league to tight ends last year.
outlooksByWeek.3: Travis Kelce isn't enjoying the same kind of target volume he did in his prime, but the 35-year-old tight end has still produced solid numbers to begin the 2025 season for Kansas City. Through two games, he's turned 10 targets into a 6-108-1 line, including four catches for 61 yards in a Week 2 loss to the Eagles. He missed a chance at a second TD early in the fourth quarter against Philadelphia, with his bobble turning into a costly red-zone INT in an eventual 20-17 loss. Kelce will look for redemption in Week 3 against a Giants defense that just surrendered nine catches and 78 yards to the Cowboys' Jake Ferguson, one week after giving up a touchdown to the Commanders' Zach Ertz.

player.seasonOutlook: Kelce is a future Hall of Famer, but his days as an elite fantasy tight end may be over. Kelce's targets and receptions actually increased from 2023 to 2024, but he saw a big dip in yards (823), TDs (three), yards per target (6.1) and RAC (3.5), all of which were career lows. After finishing no lower than third in fantasy points (second in PPG) in eight straight seasons, Kelce fell to fifth (seventh in PPG) in 2024. He will continue to benefit from Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs' pass-heavy offense, but especially with the team's WR upgrades, the 35-year-old is now more of a midrange TE1.

outlooksByWeek.1: Cooper Kupp will make his Seahawks debut against a familiar foe in the 49ers in Week 1. Kupp is set to be Seattle's new WR2 behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba after the Seahawks traded DK Metcalf to Pittsburgh and saw Tyler Lockett go to the Titans in the offseason. Kupp will look to stay healthy this year after playing in no more than 12 regular-season contests over his final three campaigns with the Rams. Since he stayed within the NFC West, Kupp should have plenty of familiarity with the 49ers, who gave up the fewest receiving yards to wideouts last season.
outlooksByWeek.2: Cooper Kupp had a quiet debut for Seattle but will look to rebound in Week 2 against the Steelers. Kupp saw just three targets from QB Sam Darnold on Sunday versus San Francisco, catching two of them for 15 yards. Meanwhile, Jaxon Smith-Njigba tallied a 9-124-0 line, suggesting that he could dominate targets to Kupp's detriment. Still, Kupp has a chance to rebound in Week 2, as Pittsburgh gave up 144 receiving yards to wideouts in Week 1 against the Jets.
outlooksByWeek.3: Cooper Kupp will look to carry the momentum from a big Week 2 performance against Pittsburgh into Seattle's Week 3 matchup versus New Orleans. After recording just two catches for 15 yards in the season opener, Kupp rebounded with seven receptions on nine targets for 90 yards in Week 2. Jaxon Smith-Njigba remains the unquestioned top target for QB Sam Darnold, but Kupp showed Sunday that he can be a factor alongside the emerging young wideout. The Saints allowed San Francisco's top three wideouts to combine for 177 yards on 12 receptions in Week 2.

player.seasonOutlook: Kupp signed with Seattle after spending his first eight NFL seasons with the division rival Rams. He has been an elite fantasy contributor in years past (he was No. 1 in PPG in both 2021 and 2022), but durability has been an issue (two full seasons in his career and exactly five missed games each of the past two years) and he's now 32 years old. Kupp remained a good fantasy contributor during most of last season (18.4 PPG in his first nine games), but it's concerning how quickly he faded down the stretch (4.9 PPG in his final five outings). Perhaps Kupp has one more big season left, and there are plenty of targets available opposite Jaxon Smith-Njigba, but there is certainly risk here. He's best viewed as a flex.

outlooksByWeek.1: Austin Ekeler looks like the starting running back for the Commanders in Week 1, though the trade of last year's starter Brian Robinson may speak more to the organization's confidence in rookie Jacory Croskey-Merritt.  Affectionately known as Bill, the rookie was a seventh round pick in the 2025 draft but impressed in camp, so much so that the Commanders felt confident to let Robinson go. In Week 1, Bill may still split touches with Ekeler against the Giants, though the latter should be used more in passing situations. In Week 1, the Commanders will face a Giants run defense that was gutted in 2024 on the ground to the tune of 136.2 yards per tilt, which was 27th in the NFL. However, the Giants drafted Abdul Carter at No. 3 to help shore up the defensive line, so that unit could be better this season. The Giants were far better against the pass in 2024, and then added Jevon Holland and Paulson Adebo in the secondary to further improve the unit.
outlooksByWeek.2: Austin Ekeler received the starting nod for the Commanders in Week 1, but was thoroughly outperformed by rookie Jacory McCroskey-Merritt. Ekeler rushed six times for 26 yards, while McCroskey-Merritt racked up 82 yards and a touchdown on 10 carries. Naturally, Ekeler made an impact in the passing game, reeling in three passes for 31 yards, but it would not be surprising to see the rookie overtake Ekeler as the early-down back in Week 2 against the Packers. Unfortunately, the matchup is stiff for whomever touches the ball out of the backfield, as Green Bay allowed a league-low 46 yards rushing in their season opener.

player.seasonOutlook: Ekeler is returning for his ninth NFL season, including his second in Washington. Ekeler played eight full games with Brian Robinson Jr. last season (including the playoffs), with Ekeler handling 5.5 carries and 4.5 targets per game while playing 51% of the snaps. In those eight games, he wasn't much of a fantasy factor (10.0 PPG, clearing 12.8 once), which can somewhat be traced to a nonexistent role near the goal line (zero TDs or carries inside the 5). With Robinson traded, Ekeler's role may increase slightly this season, but that's not a sure thing with rookie Jacory Croskey-Merritt in the fold. Ekeler was productive when Robinson was sidelined last season (3 TDs -- all from the 1-yard line -- and 15.4 PPG), so while he's now 30 years old, he has the look of a low-ceiling flex.

outlooksByWeek.1: Deebo Samuel is coming off arguably the worst season of his NFL career, though will get a fresh start in Washington. He will be the No. 2 wideout behind Terry McLaurin, which could impact his touches. In Week 1, Washington will face a Giants defense that was solid against the pass in 2024, allowing 227.6 passing yards per tilt, which was 10th in the NFL. The Giants also added No. 3 pick Abdul Carter to the pass rush, as well as Jevon Holland and Paulson Adebo to the secondary, so the unit has the chance to be even better in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.2: Deebo Samuel made an immediate impact in his debut for the Commanders.  Samuel caught seven passes on 10 targets en route to 77 yards receiving in the 21-6 win over the Giants. Samuel also took a 19-yard rush to paydirt, finding the end zone for his first score in a Washington uniform. Terry McLaurin struggled after missing a large portion of camp due to a contract dispute, and the extra time Daniels spent with Samuel appears to have paid off early. However, a far more difficult task lurks in Week 2 against the Green Bay Packers. The Packers allowed just 246 combined yards to an impressive Lions offense in Week 1, the fifth-best mark in the entire NFL.
outlooksByWeek.3: Deebo Samuel has 18 targets and two touchdowns through two games for the Commanders, but in Week 3 he could be playing without his starting quarterback. Jayden Daniels is nursing a knee sprain, leaving his status in question for a clash with the Raiders. The only saving grace for Samuel, even if backup Marcus Mariota is lining up under center, is that Las Vegas has been suspect against the pass thus far in 2025.  The Raiders are giving up 256 passing yards per tilt, which is 27th in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Samuel was traded to the Commanders after spending his first six pro seasons with the 49ers. One of the league's most versatile offensive players, Samuel has 50-plus catches and 37-plus carries in each of the past four seasons. The fantasy output has been volatile, however, as he was a top-12 in PPG in 2021 and 2023, but outside the top 25 the other four seasons. Durability has been an issue, as he's yet to play a full regular season. With Terry McLaurin as his only notable target competition, Samuel has a path to similar usage to what he saw in San Francisco. That should allow starting-caliber fantasy production, but the high likelihood of missed action pushes him down to a midround draft-day target.

outlooksByWeek.1: Nick Chubb looks like the next man up for Houston in Week 1 against the Rams, as Joe Mixon (foot) will miss at least the first four weeks of the season after being placed on the NFI list. Dameon Pierce and rookie fourth-round pick Woody Marks are also vying for carries, and Dare Ogunbowale and British Brooks remain on the roster at RB as well. Chubb averaged just 3.3 yards per carry in eight games with the Browns last season after returning from a devastating knee injury that limited him to two appearances in 2023, but the 29-year-old RB still has a robust career average of 5.1 yards per carry. If Chubb can hold off the other contenders for carries, he'll be a solid volume-based flex play during Mixon's absence.
outlooksByWeek.2: Nick Chubb handled the bulk of Houston's Week 1 backfield workload and acquitted himself fairly well in a 14-9 loss to the Rams, producing 60 rushing yards on 13 carries while no teammate had more than 35 scrimmage yards. Chubb is a low-end fantasy RB2 heading into Week 2 against the Buccaneers. He has a solid touch floor in the continued absence of Joe Mixon (foot) and should get the goal-line opportunities, but Houston's entire offense was stuck in the mud in Week 1, and Chubb's ceiling is capped by his lack of contributions as a pass catcher. The Buccaneers limited Atlanta's Bijan Robinson and Tyler Allgeier to just 48 rushing yards on 22 carries in Week 1, though they also allowed six catches for 100 yards and a TD to Robinson.
outlooksByWeek.3: Nick Chubb is making the most of Joe Mixon's absence (foot/ankle), and with no precise return date for the latter, Chubb should continue to capitalize on the opportunities he'll receive in the running game. The Texans aren't known for being a run-heavy offense, and the offensive line struggles to create enough holes for Chubb to run through, but the veteran has done a decent job with what he has. After averaging 4.6 yards per rush in Week 1 and finding the end zone in Week 2, both losses for Houston, Chubb should remain as the Texans' go-to option in the running game in this Week 3 matchup against the Jaguars, especially since he has a clear edge in touches over the next RB in the depth chart, Woody Marks.

player.seasonOutlook: Chubb signed with the Texans during the offseason. Once one of the league's best rushers, Chubb has been riddled by injuries over the past two seasons. He missed all but two games in 2023 due to a major knee injury and, after returning for eight games in 2024, a broken foot cost him the final three games of the season. Chubb was not his usual, elite self when active last season, averaging 3.3 yards per carry while playing only 40% of Cleveland's offensive snaps. Now more than a year removed from the knee injury, perhaps Chubb can get back on track in 2025, but that will be a tough road at age 29 and without much contribution as a receiver. Joe Mixon will miss, at least, four games to open 2025, so Chubb has a shot at flex value during that team. He's worth a late flier.

outlooksByWeek.1: Jayden Reed intends to suit up and start for Green Bay's regular-season opener at home against the Lions in Week 1, pain or no pain. After missing most of training camp and the preseason, Reed returned to practice more than a week in advance of Week 1, but it's been reported that he's nursing a Jones fracture. Even if he plays through the injury without setbacks, that could be enough to prevent Reed from finally improving his snap count and handling more work in two-wide sets. Consistent involvement has always capped Reed's ceiling despite his per-target efficiency, as last season he saw more than six targets just once after Week 4. The addition of rookie first-rounder Matthew Golden could, at least, cause opposing defenses to focus more attention elsewhere, leaving Reed in position to take advantage of athletic mismatches.
outlooksByWeek.2: Jayden Reed and the Packers host Washington in Week 2 on Thursday night. Reed turned 5 targets into a 3-45-1 line in the Week 1 win over Detroit, reaffirming premier role as a top designed-touch candidate in coach Matt LaFleur's offense. Washington's secondary is fresh off holding Russell Wilson and the Giants to a total of  168 yards passing yards, though 55 of those (on six catches) went to slot specialist Wan'Dale Robinson. Despite the fact that Reed is playing through a Jones fracture in his foot, his profile as a YAC specialist capable of thriving with low aDOT or in the intermediate area of the field positions him to potentially operate as the focal point of Green Bay's aerial attack on Thursday, especially if top Commanders cornerback Marshon Lattimore focuses his attention elsewhere.

player.seasonOutlook: Reed is entering his third NFL season, having produced at least 79 touches, 956 yards and seven TDs during each of his first two seasons in Green Bay. Despite the solid numbers, Reed has yet to emerge as a consistent fantasy producer. He came out hot with a pair of 27-plus-point games during Weeks 1-4 last season, but averaged 9.2 PPG the rest of the season, with zero 20-point efforts. Reed has struggled with drops (eight last season), but he's otherwise been productive (11.4 YPT last season ranked third at WR) and he's also a plus contributor as a rusher (282 yards and three TDs on 31 career carries). Perhaps Reed will make a Year 3 leap, but he's yet to deliver a top-25 fantasy season (PPG) after his 40th-place finish in 2024 and now has to compete with rookies Matthew Golden and Savion Williams for work. He has the look of a low-ceiling flex.

outlooksByWeek.1: Najee Harris jumped ship from the Steelers to the Chargers as a free agent this offseason, a move that landed him in an even more run-friendly offense scheme but also put him in competition with 2025 first-round pick Omarion Hampton for touches. Unfortunately for Harris, any shot he might have had of beginning the season with the top job ended when he suffered damage to his eyes in a Fourth of July fireworks accident. The veteran back missed all of training camp and the preseason, and while he should be cleared to play in Week 1 in Sao Paulo, his role figures to be limited as he gets up to game speed. Harris will likely struggle to make much of the snaps he collects against a Kansas City defense that ranked in the top four in both rushing yards and receiving yards allowed to RBs last season.
outlooksByWeek.2: Najee Harris was used sparingly in his Chargers debut, getting only two touches and turning them into 10 scrimmage yards. The veteran back's volume was affected by the time he missed in training camp due to a July fireworks accident, but he appeared to be 100% healthy when he rotated in. Rookie Omarion Hampton dominated the workload out of the backfield, and while Harris' role should grow as he ramps up, he may be stuck as the team's No. 2 RB rather than pushing for more of a 1A/1B split. He'll try to earn more touches in Week 2 against a Raiders defense that looked stout up front against the Patriots in its opener, and which ranked 18th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs in 2024.
outlooksByWeek.3: Najee Harris continues to put his July fireworks accident in the rearview mirror. After garnering only two touches in his Chargers' debut in Week 1, his workload increased to 10 touches in a Week 2 win over the Raiders, although he turned them into just 48 scrimmage yards. Rookie running back Omarion Hampton committed a fumble late in the win over Las Vegas, which gave Harris additional work on the final drives, and his perceived reliability might tip the workload scales further in his favor. The former Steeler will look to break out in Week 3 against a Broncos defense that just surrendered 215 scrimmage yards and a TD to the Colts' Jonathan Taylor.

player.seasonOutlook: Harris signed with the Chargers after spending his first four seasons in Pittsburgh. He is as durable as they come, as he's the only tailback who has appeared in 100% of his team's games over the past four seasons. He has yet to finish a season lower than seventh in the league in carries (255-plus each season), but that figures to change this season with first-round rookie Omarion Hampton likely to handle lead-back duties in Los Angeles. Harris also figures to be very limited as a receiver, as Jim Harbaugh and Greg Roman have a long history of low RB usage in the pass game, in addition to the fact Harris has finished outside the top 20 RBs in targets each of the past two seasons. Harris has ranked in the 20-to-30 range in fantasy PPG each of the past three seasons, but even if he splits carries with Hampton, he'll be hard-pressed to produce consistent flex numbers.

outlooksByWeek.1: Hollywood Brown barely got onto the field in his first season with Kansas City in 2024, as shoulder surgery sidelined him until Week 16. He wound up catching only 14 passes across five games between the end of the regular season and the playoffs, but the team saw enough to bring him back on another one-year contract. The 28-year-old wideout has a 1,000-yard season on his resume with the Ravens back in 2021, but his career has been on a downward trajectory since. Provided that the ankle injury which kept him out for the entire preseason cooperates, Brown could fill a big role early in the 2025 campaign with Rashee Rice suspended for the first six games, and in Week 1's tilt in Sao Paulo he might make a splash against a Chargers secondary that finished in the bottom 10 in touchdowns allowed to WRs in 2024.
outlooksByWeek.2: Hollywood Brown took over as Patrick Mahomes' top downfield option in Week 1 after Xavier Worthy left the game in the first quarter with a shoulder injury. Brown wound up logging a massive 16 targets, turning them into 10 catches for 99 yards. The veteran wideout is injury-prone himself, having played only 16 regular-season games over the prior two campaigns, but with Worthy likely to remain sidelined in Week 2 and Rashee Rice still suspended, Brown should remain the focal point of the Kansas City passing game. He faces a tough test in Week 2 against an Eagles secondary that finished third in receiving yards allowed to WRs in 2024.
outlooksByWeek.3: Hollywood Brown didn't gather the same massive volume in Week 2's loss to the Eagles that he did in Kansas City's opener, but he did catch all five of his targets for 30 yards. The veteran wideout has taken advantage of the absences of Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy to post a 15-129-1 line through two games on 21 targets, and while Worthy could return from a shoulder injury as soon as Week 3, Rice's suspension runs through Week 6. Brown figures to remain a primary option for Patrick Mahomes in Week 3 against a Giants defense that just got torched for 361 passing yards by the Cowboys.

player.seasonOutlook: Brown re-signed with the Chiefs after a lost 2024 in which he appeared in only five games (including the playoffs). It didn't take long for Brown to play a significant role (he had a season-high eight targets in his debut), but he didn't make much noise, maxing out at 46 yards and 9.5 fantasy points. Brown has now missed game action in five of his six NFL seasons, including three or more games in three straight years. He has yet to produce a top-20 fantasy campaign in six tries and his lone top-35 finish came in 2021. Kansas City's wide receiver room is suddenly a bit crowded on paper and Brown may find his way to an every-down role only during Rashee Rice's six-game suspension. The 28-year-old Brown is best valued as bench option in deeper leagues, though he'll have WR3/flex appeal while Rice is out.

outlooksByWeek.1: After being plagued by injuries in his first two years as a pro, Rashod Bateman has played in 33 games combined across the last two campaigns. He established himself as a key part of the Baltimore offense in 2024, emerging as a big-play threat, logging 11 receptions of more than 20 yards while catching nine touchdowns. Bateman was rewarded with a three-year extension this offseason, cementing his importance to the team and setting him to potentially take another step forward in 2025. A Week 1 matchup at Buffalo is tough overall, though the Bills secondary is plagued by injury. Consider Bateman a FLEX option in most fantasy formats.
outlooksByWeek.2: Despite the high-scoring nature of Baltimore's Week 1 loss to Buffalo, Lamar Jackson attempted only 19 passes. With Zay Flowers the clear top target, Rashod Bateman was left as only a peripheral contributor, tallying two receptions for 10 yards. A Week 2 matchup against Cleveland isn't likely to push Baltimore into a pass-heavy gameplan, meaning it could be another quiet performance for Bateman. He's a very risky FLEX option, better left on fantasy benches.
outlooksByWeek.3: Rashod Bateman has yet to gain traction in the Baltimore offense, recording only four receptions for 25 yards combined in the first two games of the season. Instead, Zay Flowers has taken a step forward in the offense and has commanded a majority of targets from Lamar Jackson. Fantasy managers are best served to keep Bateman on the bench for a Week 3 matchup against Detroit, and moving forward until his role in the offense ticks up.

player.seasonOutlook: Bateman is entering his fifth season (all with Baltimore) following a big leap forward in 2024. Bateman appeared in all 17 regular season games for the first time and, though his 15.4% target share was the second lowest of his career, he posted career-best marks in yardage, touchdowns and fantasy points. Targets remained inconsistent, however, and led to extremely boom/bust production (eight single-digit fantasy point games and a 47th-place finish in PPG, the latter of which is a career best). The 25-year-old is a capable situational deep threat (he's ranked top 12 in aDOT two years in a row), but he's a good bet for touchdown regression to the mean (4.6 expected TDs last season) and his usage is too volatile to allow weekly flex consideration.

The Buccaneers D/ST fell almost entirely into the hands of its matchups in 2024, and their 2025 should deliver more of the same. S Antoine Winfield Jr., DT Vita Vea and LB Lavonte David provide a strong core, and the addition of DE Haason Reddick can only help strengthen the defensive front. Consider the Buccaneers for in-season matchups, including their pair of divisional games against the Saints and Panthers and Week 3 against the Jets.

outlooksByWeek.1: Matt Gay was surprisingly released by the Colts in the offseason, allowing him to latch on with Washington. Gay hit all 28 of his attempts from inside 50 yards, though was just 3-of-9 from boots 50 and beyond. Washington's offense averaged 28.5 points per game in 2024, which was fifth in the league, and the Commanders added Deebo Samuel to go along with Terry McLaurin as weapons for the dynamic Jayden Daniels. In Week 1, Gay will face a Giants defense that allowed 24.4 points per tilt in 2024 but should be improved in 2025 with the additions of Abdul Carter, Jevon Holland and Paulson Adebo.
outlooksByWeek.2: Matt Gay connected on all three of his extra points in Washington's season-opening win over the New York Giants.  He did not attempt a field goal. In Week 2, the Commanders travel to Lambeau Field to take on the Green Bay Packers. The Packers allowed just 13 points to the vaunted Detroit Lions offense in Week 1, meaning the scoring opportunities could be limited for Gay.
outlooksByWeek.3: Matt Gay connected on just 1-of-3 field goals from 50-plus yards last game for Washington. Though Gay connected from 51 yards out, he missed two other attempts from 52 and 58 yards. Jayden Daniels is also dinged up and may not play in Week 3 versus the Raiders, which could also negatively affect Gay's potential output. Las Vegas has also been surprisingly stingy through two games, surrendering just 16.5 points per contest, which is fifth in the NFL.

outlooksByWeek.1: Malik Nabers has been banged up for the Giants this preseason, and injuries could be the only knock on him following a standout rookie campaign. Despite dreadful quarterback play, Nabers still caught 109 passes for 1,204 yards and seven touchdowns in 2024. The explosive playmaker should once again be heavily targeted as a sophomore, this time by new quarterback Russell Wilson.   The Week 1 matchup Sunday with Washington will be difficult, though.  The Commanders allowed only 189.5 passing yards per tilt in 2024, which was third in the league. However, Nabers did have 127 yards and a touchdown in the first meeting between the two squads last season.
outlooksByWeek.2: Malik Nabers was heavily targeted in Week 1, though could only provide modest production for the Giants. Nabers saw 12 targets from new quarterback Russell Wilson, though the duo was only able to connect five times for 71 yards in the dismal 21-6 loss to Washington. Wilson passed for just 168 yards for the game and failed to lead a single touchdown drive. Nabers could be catching passes from rookie Jaxson Dart sooner than anticipated, though the switch is not likely to occur in Week 2 versus the Cowboys. Dallas held up surprisingly well in Week 1 versus the Eagles, allowing only 144 yards passing and zero touchdowns through the air.
outlooksByWeek.3: Malik Nabers continues to see a plethora of targets on a weekly basis for the New York Giants. Nabers managed at least 12 targets for the second straight game, parlaying those looks into nine grabs for 167 yards and two touchdowns. Nabers has a staggering 25 targets through just two outings. In Week 3, the Giants will face a hungry Kansas City squad that is also 0-2 to start the season, with a defense that was picked apart by Justin Herbert in Week 1, but bounced back in Week 2 by allowing just 101 passing yards and zero throwing scores to the Eagles.

player.seasonOutlook: Nabers is coming off one of the best seasons by a rookie receiver in some time. The 2024 No. 6 overall pick led the NFL with a 35% target share and finished seventh or better among receivers in targets, receptions, yards and fantasy points despite missing two games and dealing with New York's offensive struggles. Nabers' massive target share allowed him a high floor, as he was a top-30 fantasy scorer in 13 of 15 games, including 10 straight to end the season. He appears to be the real deal and his outlook is even better in 2025 with Russell Wilson (and perhaps Jaxson Dart and/or Jameis Winston) under center. Nabers is on the short list of receivers who could lead the position in fantasy points and is a solid WR1 target in fantasy.�

outlooksByWeek.1: Jonathan Taylor bounced back after a pair of injury-riddled campaigns to rush for 1,431 yards and 11 TDs in 14 games last season. He's locked in as the most important member of the Colts' offense heading into Week 1 against Miami, as expectations are limited for Indianapolis' passing game with Daniel Jones under center. Taylor should get all the touches he can handle against a Dolphins defense that ranked in the middle of the pack at defending RBs in 2024. He's a set-and-forget fantasy RB1 in any matchup when healthy.
outlooksByWeek.2: Jonathan Taylor was surprisingly overshadowed by QB Daniel Jones (one passing TD, two rushing TDs) last week, but the workhorse Colts RB still mustered 98 scrimmage yards on 21 touches in a blowout win. Taylor averaged 102 scrimmage yards per game last season, and the star RB has one of the highest touch floors in the NFL. Finding running room won't be easy in Week 2 against a Denver defense that allowed the third-fewest rushing yards last season and looked sharp in Week 1, but Taylor has proven to be virtually matchup-proof. Still, he's on the lower end of the fantasy RB1 range for Week 2 given the tough opposition.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jonathan Taylor is locked in as a top five fantasy RB for Week 3, facing a Titans defense that allowed 300 rushing yards and three TDs on the ground through two weeks. The Colts have yet to punt this season, and while Taylor has yet to score a rushing TD in 2025, the star RB has racked up 236 yards on the ground, as well as 77 yards and a TD as a pass catcher. Mobile QB Daniel Jones already has three rushing scores and remains a threat to vulture TD in close, but Taylor's poised to benefit from a run-heavy Week 3 game script with the Colts heavily favored against a Titans team that's 0-2 with a minus-22 point differential in 2025 after going a league-worst 3-14 in 2024.

player.seasonOutlook: Taylor enters his age-26 campaign as one of the few remaining clear feature backs. The five-year vet finished last season top 5 among RBs in carries and rushing yards, averaging a healthy 4.72 YPC along the way. Taylor did miss three games due to injury and has now managed just one full season in his career (2021). He's also struggled to make much of an impact as a pass catcher, having never finished a season top 20 in targets. Taylor's heavy rushing workload allowed him to produce good fantasy numbers regardless of who was under center last season and, while the lack of receiving will limit his ceiling, we should expect the same in 2025. Taylor is best valued as a midrange RB1.

outlooksByWeek.1: Jalen Hurts and the defending champion Philadelphia Eagles open their 2025 season on Thursday as they host division rival Dallas.  The Cowboys had one of the worst rushing defenses in the NFL last season, allowing a league-worst 25 touchdowns on the ground.  This bodes well for Hurts in Week 1; he rushed for two scores in his only appearance versus Dallas in 2024.  Hurts also tossed two additional touchdowns in a 34-6 rout.
