The Cowboys dealt Micah Parsons last week and gained back a run-stuffer in Kenny Clark, though the defense is still unlikely to be better in 2025 without one of the most dynamic pass rushers in all of football.
outlooksByWeek.2: Jalen Hurts did most of his damage on the ground in the season opener for the Eagles, but may have to switch up his tactics in Week 2 versus Kansas City. Hurts threw for just 152 yards and zero touchdowns against Dallas in Week 1, though also rushed for 62 yards and two touchdowns in the victory. Meanwhile, Kansas City was torched for 304 yards and three touchdowns through the air by Justin Herbert in their Week 1 loss to the Chargers. In the Super Bowl last year against KC, Hurts combined for nearly 300 yards and three touchdowns in the Eagles win.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jalen Hurts gained just 116 total yards last game for the Eagles, though he still managed to come away with the win versus Kansas City. Hurts did find the end zone on the ground in the contest, something he has done three times in the first two contests of the 2025 campaign. However, Hurts has yet to throw a touchdown, and he may have a difficult time in Week 3 versus the Rams. Los Angeles has allowed just one offensive touchdown thus far this season. In addition, the Rams are giving up just 147 passing yards per clash, which is fourth in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Hurts returns for his fifth season as the Eagles' starting QB. He averaged 22.2 fantasy points per game during his 14 full regular-season outings in 2024, which ranked third among QBs and was the second highest of his career. He wasn't asked to do much with his arm (20th or lower in pass attempts, completions, yards and TDs), but he dominated on the ground (he's led all QBs in rushing attempts, TDs and carries inside the 5 four seasons in a row). Hurts is entering his age-27 season with essentially the same elite supporting cast he had in place during last season's top-10 fantasy campaign (his fourth in a row). The reigning Super Bowl MVP is a top-5 fantasy option.

outlooksByWeek.1: James Conner will lead Arizona's ground game in Week 1 against the Saints. The veteran RB should again function as a workhorse for the Cardinals, though Trey Benson could slightly cut into his workload in time if he continues to develop. Conner is coming off a career-best 2024 campaign in which he set a new personal-best mark with 1,094 rushing yards on 236 carries (4.6 YPC). In Week 1 he'll face a Saints defense that gave up 4.84 YPC to running backs last year, fourth-worst in the league.
outlooksByWeek.2: James Conner will aim to get into the end zone for a second time this season when Arizona faces the Panthers in Week 2. Conner scored his TD through the air in Week 1 versus the Saints, though he finished with just 12 carries for 39 yards on the ground. Meanwhile, Trey Benson tallied nine touches for 75 yards, suggesting that Conner may not be asked to work as a true workhorse this year. Carolina does present a great opportunity for improvement in Week 2, as the Panthers gave up 143 yards on 16 carries to Trevor Etienne in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: James Conner will look to get going on the ground in the Cardinals' Week 3 NFC West battle against San Francisco. Through two games, Conner has recorded just 73 rushing yards on 23 carries (3.2 YPC), but he's managed to get into the end zone twice (once on a rush and another time on a reception). No. 2 RB Trey Benson has been much more efficient with 83 rushing yards on 11 carries, but he somewhat surprisingly got only three totes in Week 2 versus Carolina. Benson could eat into Conner's workload in time, but for now it appears Conner remains the team's clear lead back. He'll have his work cut out for him against the 49ers, who have allowed running backs to average just 3.63 yards per carry through two weeks.

player.seasonOutlook: Conner returns as the lead back in Arizona. Despite having never played a full regular season in eight tries, Conner has produced at least 220 touches, 1,080 yards and eight TDs in four consecutive seasons. That includes 1,508 yards on 283 touches in 16 games (all three are career highs) in 2024. Productive as both a rusher and receiver, Conner ended the 2024 season with three-plus targets and two-plus receptions in 12 straight games. He has finished as a top-20 fantasy back in four straight seasons (top 15 in PPG each year) and is well positioned for another solid RB2 campaign in his age-30 campaign.

outlooksByWeek.1: Jaylen Waddle begins a rebound campaign for the Dolphins in Week 1 at Indianapolis. Waddle had a career-low 744 yards and two touchdowns in 2024 after turning in three straight 1,000-yard efforts to begin his career. Though he remains second fiddle to Tyreek Hill, Waddle is a stable if unsexy option in all formats. Facing a defense that was mid-tier against opposing receivers a year ago slots, Waddle into WR3 territory with potential for more.
outlooksByWeek.2: Jaylen Waddle and the Dolphins passing game looks to get on track in Week 2 against the Patriots. Waddle collected just five targets in Week 1 but caught four of Tua Tagovailoa's 14 completions. For as bad as Miami's offense looked, there remains a clear funnel in the passing game with Waddle, Tyreek Hill and De'Von Achane. New England allowed 362 yards passing last week to Geno Smith and were without Christian Gonzalez. If Gonzalez remains out, Hill and Waddle can rebound, and if Gonzalez is back, he could shadow Hill, further adding appeal to Waddle. It's a lot of ifs, but there's a viable path for Waddle to rebound and flash.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jaylen Waddle is a volatile option for the Dolphins in Week 3 against the Bills on Thursday night. Waddle found the end zone for the first time in Week 2 but recorded only 11 targets in Miami's first two games, turning them into 98 yards. In two games against Buffalo last season, Waddle amassed just six catches for 37 yards, but working in his favor is that Buffalo was exploited by Baltimore's Zay Flowers underneath and in the middle of the field in Week 1. Game flow should be in Waddle's favor with Miami expected to operate from behind, but the current lack of volume leaves Waddle a risky Week 3 WR3 play.

player.seasonOutlook: Waddle enters his fifth NFL season after a somewhat inexplicable down year in 2024. Granted, he wasn't fully healthy at times (and missed two games), but Waddle's target share dipped from 20%-plus during his first three seasons to 16% last season (56th among WRs). He posted career-low marks in every key category and ranked 52nd in fantasy PPG after finishing 21st or better in each of his first three seasons. Same as Tyreek Hill, Waddle seemingly suffered from Miami facing two-high safeties at a league-high rate, and with both back for 2025, we may see more of the same. Waddle has the talent to allow a bounce-back campaign (especially with Hill entering his age-31 season), but he can't be trusted as more than a WR3.

outlooksByWeek.1: J.K. Dobbins revived his career with a strong 2024 campaign with the Chargers. While the 26-year-old running back couldn't stay healthy for a full season, missing four games due to a knee injury, he was productive when on the field and averaged 4.6 yards per carry while topping 1,000 scrimmage yards and scoring nine rushing touchdowns. Dobbins signed with the Broncos in June on a one-year deal to share the backfield with rookie RJ Harvey, but coach Sean Payton's offensive scheme has a long history of allowing two RBs to thrive at the same time from his New Orleans days. Dobbins' Denver tenure will begin with a Week 1 tilt against a Titans defense that gave up the most receiving TDs (seven) and total TDs (22) in the league to running backs last year.
outlooksByWeek.2: J.K. Dobbins functioned as the Broncos' lead back in his Week 1 debut for the team, racking up 63 yards and a touchdown on 16 carries while adding five receiving yards on two catches. Rookie RJ Harvey, his primary competition for work in the backfield, garnered only six carries, but he erupted for 70 rushing yards, and his big-play potential could allow him to move to the top of the depth chart quickly. Dobbins should remain part of a timeshare as long as he's healthy, and he's better suited for goal-line work than Harvey. Dobbins will face a Colts defense in Week 2 that kept the Dolphins out of the end zone in its opener, but which gave up 7.9 yards per carry to De'Von Achane.
outlooksByWeek.3: J.K. Dobbins handled the lead role in the Broncos' backfield again in Week 2, turning 15 touches into 85 scrimmage yards and a rushing touchdown in a loss to the Colts. Rookie RJ Harvey struggled to find running room after an impressive Week 1 effort, and as long as Dobbins is providing more consistency, he should continue to gather more volume. Dobbins has found the end zone in back-to-back games to begin his Denver tenure, and his heavy red-zone usage is especially encouraging. He'll face a stingy Chargers defense in Week 3 that just held Raiders' rookie Ashton Jeanty to 44 scrimmage yards on 14 touches.

player.seasonOutlook: Dobbins signed with Denver in June. After struggling with injuries throughout most of his first four NFL seasons, Dobbins was handed the keys to the Chargers' backfield last season. He ran well (4.6 YPC, 1.9 YAC) but struggled as a receiver (his 3.8 YPT ranked 38th among 39 qualified RBs) and was an inconsistent fantasy producer (15-plus points seven times, but below 11 in the other six games). Dobbins missed four games (he's yet to play a full season), but he still managed 1,058 yards and nine TDs. He's now 26 years old and is expected to team up with second-round rookie RJ Harvey. The two very well could split carries, with Harvey taking the lead in passing situations. Dobbins is unlikely to see quite the volume he enjoyed in Los Angeles, but he'll have a respectable role in an ascending Denver offense. He's a fine mid-to-late-round target.

outlooksByWeek.1: Josh Downs has seemingly recovered from a mid-August hamstring injury ahead of a Week 1 home game against the Dolphins. Downs could be the Colts' co-No.1 WR alongside Michael Pittman after all three of Downs, Pittman and Alec Pierce posted between 803 and 824 receiving yards in 2024. Pierce was much more reliant on deep passes and could have a hard time sustaining his success with Daniel Jones under center rather than Anthony Richardson, while Downs and Pittman will likely get a steady diet of short and intermediate passes from Jones. A healthy Downs should be in the weekly flex conversation, though his recent hamstring injury lowers his Week 1 floor a bit.
outlooksByWeek.2: Josh Downs was held to 12 yards even as the Colts put up 33 points in their season opener, and bouncing back won't be easy in Week 2 against a Broncos secondary that limited WRs to a league-low 11 TDs in 2024. It's possible Downs' effectiveness was limited by a hamstring injury that bothered him until shortly prior to Week 1. He had just three targets in Week 1 compared to Tyler Warren's nine and Michael Pittman's eight. Downs had nearly identical production to Pittman in 2024, with 803 yards on 107 targets to Pittman's 808 yards on 111 targets. While Downs could still work his way back into the weekly flex conversation, it's hard to trust him heading into Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Josh Downs bounced back with six catches for 51 yards in Week 2 after posting only two catches for 12 yards in the season opener, when he may have still been limited by the vestiges of a training camp hamstring injury. While Downs is healthy heading into Week 3 against the Titans, he'll be a low-ceiling flex option while sharing targets with Michael Pittman, Alec Pierce and Tyler Warren in a Colts offense that's likely to lean primarily on star RB Jonathan Taylor against a Titans defense that has been much worse against the run than the pass so far.

player.seasonOutlook: A third-round pick in 2023, Downs has emerged as a quality short-range/slot target, but that has yet to allow consistent fantasy output. The Colts' QB play has been an issue, as in seven full games with Anthony Richardson, Downs averaged 5.9 targets and 10.7 fantasy points per game, but in seven outings with Joe Flacco, he averaged 9.4 targets and 15.5 PPG. Downs, same as other Colts receivers, has struggled to produce with Richardson under center and it's no sure bet he'll be better if Daniel Jones wins the job. Downs is a good player, so he's worth late-round consideration, but the team's QB uncertainty will make him tough to plug into your lineup.

outlooksByWeek.1: Darnell Mooney looks to be the second option in Atlanta's passing game against Tampa Bay in Week 1. The former Bears receiver has been dealing with a shoulder problem this offseason, but he should be ready to go for the season opener. Mooney saw a huge improvement in 2024 after joining the Falcons, logging over 1,000 receiving yards even with a rough quarterback room. Quarterback Michael Penix will now lead the squad, which could be even better for Mooney if the second-year quarterback is any better than Kirk Cousins was. Mooney will have to play against a Buccaneers secondary in Week 1 that wasn't too tough for wide receivers in 2024.
outlooksByWeek.2: Darnell Mooney could make his season debut for the Falcons against the Vikings in Week 2. Mooney had to sit out of Atlanta's Week 1 opener as he's still dealing with a shoulder injury, but he could return to the field as soon as this upcoming week if he has a healthy slate of practices. The sixth-year wide receiver is now joined on the injury report by position mate Drake London, who suffered a shoulder sprain in Week 1. Mooney's return could be at a perfect time, given that Minnesota gave up 210 passing yards to quarterback Caleb Williams and 147 total receiving yards to Chicago's top-three pass catchers this past week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Darnell Mooney will aim to get more looks in Atlanta's offense during a Week 3 matchup at Carolina. Mooney totaled just four targets and brought in two for 20 yards in his season debut against the Vikings in Week 2. The Falcons did emphasize the run game in the defensive-dominated outing, and they finished the game with 38 carries among the two running backs. This ground-and-pound technique likely won't be utilized every week, and Mooney should garner a solid chunk of targets from quarterback Michael Penix when the passing game is at the forefront. With that being said, the Panthers have allowed the fourth-least fantasy points to wide receivers so far this season, so Mooney is a fringe flex play for the away game.

player.seasonOutlook: Mooney is entering his sixth NFL season, including his second with the Falcons. Year 1 in Atlanta was a relative success despite Mooney playing behind Drake London in a run-heavy offense. The veteran receiver handled a 21% target share and had his best showings in targets, catches and yards since his breakout 2021 season. He also caught a career-high five touchdowns. Though Mooney played well, the production wasn't enough to allow his first top-30 fantasy campaign (PPG). Mooney remains locked into the No. 2 WR role in a Falcons' offense that very well could make a leap with Michael Penix Jr. entering his first season as the full-time starting quarterback. That's enough to put him on the flex radar, but his upside is limited.

outlooksByWeek.1: C.J. Stroud could be asked to do more with his arm in Week 1 against the Rams, as the Texans begin the season without starting RB Joe Mixon (foot). Stroud underwent a bit of a sophomore slump last season, as his TD:INT dipped from 23:5 in 2023 to 20:12 in 2024. Houston improved its WR depth behind Nico Collins by trading for Christian Kirk and drafting former Iowa State teammates Jayden Higgins and Jaylin Noel in Rounds 2 and 3, though Tank Dell (knee) is on the PUP list. Given the depth of the QB position, Stroud's a borderline fantasy starter for Week 1 as he faces a Rams secondary that ranked in the middle of the pack last season, though there's almost certainly a spot for him in superflex or two-QB lineups.
outlooksByWeek.2: C.J. Stroud will try to bounce back from a tough season opener when the Texans host the Buccaneers on Monday Night Football in Week 2. Stroud failed to lead a touchdown drive while throwing for just 188 yards with an interception in Houston's Week 1 loss to the Rams. Tampa Bay allowed the fourth-most passing yards last season and gave up 298 passing yards to Michael Penix in Week 1, making this a favorable matchup. Stroud's a strong rebound candidate and deserving of a starting spot in superflex or multi-QB formats, but he'll be tough to trust as a fantasy starter in standard lineups until he gets on the same page with star WR Nico Collins, who had just 25 yards on five targets in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: If there was any buzz regarding C.J. Stroud as a steady option under center for fantasy purposes this season, his performances over the first two games should exercise some caution. Stroud has averaged 197.5 passing yards per game with a 1:1 TD:INT, with the Texans losing back-to-back games to the Rams and Buccaneers. Perhaps the biggest issue with Stroud is that he's struggled to finish drives, notably failing to capitalize on a golden opportunity in Week 2 on the Bucs' one-yard line early in the fourth quarter when he missed on two consecutive throws to turn the ball over on downs. He has no risk of losing his starting role, but based on what he's shown in the first two outings, fantasy managers could look at better options than Stroud for the Week 3 matchup against the Jaguars, a team that has evidenced a fair share of issues defensively after a Week 2 loss to a Bengals team that didn't have Joe Burrow (toe) under center.

player.seasonOutlook: Stroud enters his third NFL season looking for a rebound following a bit of a step back in 2024. Stroud had one of the best seasons ever by a rookie QB in 2023 (12th in QBR, eighth in pass yards, ninth in fantasy PPG), but he plummeted to 26th in QBR, 14th in pass yards and 28th in PPG last season. He opened the season with two seventh-place fantasy weeks in his first four games, but proceeded to finish 14th or worse each of the 13 remaining weeks. He reached 20 fantasy points only once (Week 4). Still only 23, Stroud is still on the ascent, but he'll need to produce more through the air in order to offset mild-to-moderate rushing contributions. He's best viewed as a serviceable QB2 with limited upside.

A sure-to-be-popular D/ST sleeper, the Texans are led by several individual defensive stars: All-Pro CB Derek Stingley Jr., DEs Will Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter (each had double-digit sacks), and free-agent addition LB E.J. Speed. Should all stay healthy, or some of the team's depth pieces materialize, this could be a sneaky, every-week unit. The Texans face a tougher early schedule (@LAR, TB in Weeks 1-2, @BAL in Week 5, Week 6 bye), but have several intriguing late-season matchups worth exploiting.

outlooksByWeek.1: Hunter Henry could surprise for the Patriots in Week 1 against the Raiders. Las Vegas allowed the third most fantasy points to tight ends a season ago. The concern is the presence of Austin Hooper, as well as a busy and deep receiving corps, so there's no established target funnel. A touchdown wouldn't surprise, but also can't be relied upon, making Henry a fringe fantasy TE for the opener.
outlooksByWeek.2: Hunter Henry appears to be trending upward for the Patriots ahead of a Week 2 matchup with the Dolphins. Henry logged eight targets in his season debut, converting them into 66 yards. While New England likely won't throw 46 passes again, the Dolphins also allowed 96 yards to the tight ends last week, rendering Henry a low-end starter in deep leagues.
outlooksByWeek.3: Hunter Henry looks for a consistent role in Week 3 when the Patriots host the Steelers. Henry logged an attractive eight targets in Week 1 but followed that up with just three in Week 2. Pittsburgh has surrendered seven catches to the position through two games, including a touchdown, so there remains hope as the Patriots haven't established a clear offensive gameplan. Henry is a fringe Week 3 candidate.

player.seasonOutlook: Henry is entering his fifth season in New England fresh off a career year in most categories. He set career-best marks in target share (20%), targets, catches and receiving yards, but still finished 16th in fantasy PPG due to a lack of TDs. Henry found the end zone only twice, which matches a career low. The veteran tight end hasn't finished a season better than 15th in PPG since 2020 (his final season with the Chargers) and though he was better with Drake Maye on the field, he'll now need to overcome more target competition with Stefon Diggs and rookie Kyle Williams in the lineup. Henry, 30, is likely to post midrange TE2 numbers, but there's a shot for more if Maye makes a big Year 2 leap.

outlooksByWeek.1: Chris Boswell emerged as one of the most consistent kickers in the league, converting 90% or more of his field-goal attempts in five of the last six seasons. In 2024, he made an excellent 13 field goals from 50 yards away or more. The only problem is that he is associated with the slow-paced and likely low-scoring Steelers' offense, potentially limiting his opportunity. Boswell's accuracy dictates that he should be a top-end fantasy kicker, so he's still a reasonable starting option in Week 1 against the Jets.
outlooksByWeek.2: Chris Boswell made 20 field goals from 40 yards or deeper in 2024, and he picked up where he left off in Week 1. He sealed a victory for Pittsburgh with a career-long 60-yard kick with just over a minute remaining, which came after he converted a 56-yard attempt in the second quarter. Boswell remains one of the better fantasy kickers heading into a Week 2 matchup against Seattle.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chris Boswell remained perfect on the season by making three field goals from 45 yards or deeper in Pittsburgh's Week 2 loss. He is one of the most accurate kickers in the league, with his last miss coming in Week 13 of the 2024 season. Boswell also converted multiple field goals in both games this season, making him a reliable starting kicker in Week 3 against New England.

outlooksByWeek.1: Kareem Hunt returned to Kansas City in 2024, the team he won a rushing title with as a rookie in 2017, and for a brief period he turned back the clock. The 30-year-old galloped for 345 yards and five touchdowns over a four-game stretch beginning in Week 5 while replacing an injured Isiah Pacheco, but Hunt wore down quickly after that and averaged just 3.5 yards per carry over his final eight regular-season contests. With Pacheco healthy to begin the 2025 campaign, Hunt will fill a complementary role, but the fact that he also disappeared as a receiving option for Patrick Mahomes down the stretch last year isn't encouraging. Hunt will head to Sao Paulo in Week 1 to face a Chargers defense that allowed a league-low four rushing scores to RBs but was vulnerable to backs through the air, finishing 28th in catches allowed to the position.
outlooksByWeek.2: Kareem Hunt equally split the workload in the Kansas City backfield with Isiah Pacheco in Week 1. Both backs had five carries and two receptions on three targets, with Hunt's 26 scrimmage yards just a hair behind Pacheco's 28. Hunt doesn't have the younger backs' physicality or explosiveness, but with Pacheco having missed over half the 2024 campaign due to injuries, the veteran figures to maintain a significant role in the game plan. Hunt will face an Eagles defense in Week 2 that gave up two goal-line TDs to the Cowboys' Javonte Williams in its opener, but only after star DT Jalen Carter got himself ejected immediately following the opening kickoff.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kareem Hunt has had a sluggish start to the season, cobbling 60 scrimmage yards and zero touchdowns on 16 touches through two games. Those are only slightly better numbers than Isiah Pacheco, and the duo will likely continue to split the workload in the Kansas City backfield, at least until one of them heats up. The entire offense has sputtered so far, but facing two tough defenses in the Chargers and Eagles likely contributed to that lack of production. Hunt could make a splash in Week 3 against a Giants defense that just coughed up 130 combined yards and a touchdown to Javonte Williams.

player.seasonOutlook: Hunt re-signed with the Chiefs following a successful reunion with the team last season. He stepped in for an injured Isiah Pacheco in Week 4 and went on to average 21.5 touches, 89.0 yards and 14.8 fantasy points over the next eight games. Pacheco returned in Week 13 and then neither were viable fantasy options from that point forward, as they were near even in snaps, carries and targets, with Samaje Perine also in the mix as a passing-down specialist. Hunt was not particularly effective as a rusher or receiver and he's now 30 years old, so it's fair to expect a healthy Pacheco to lead this backfield in 2025. Hunt is only a late-round consideration.

outlooksByWeek.1: Jonnu Smith is reunited with Arthur Smith, who coached him with both Tennessee and Atlanta, after being dealt from Miami to Pittsburgh this offseason. He isn't likely to repeat his 88 catches and 884-yard performances from 2024, but Smith will have a role in the Steelers' offense. He could reasonably be Aaron Rodgers' second favorite target behind DK Metcalf while sharing the field with Pat Freiermuth in two tight-end sets. Even so, there are a lot of unknowns about this offensive scheme heading into a Week 1 matchup against the Jets, so Smith is a better stash than start, though that has the chance to change as fantasy managers get a better feel for the target priority.
outlooksByWeek.2: Jonnu Smith led the Steelers' tight ends in snaps and targets in his team debut, and he finished tied for second overall in opportunities. He was used exclusively in short areas of the field, picking up only 15 yards from scrimmage while salvaging his day with a touchdown. Heading into Week 2 against Seattle, Smith will likely remain very involved in the offense. However, he'll be tough to rely on until his usage includes more downfield routes, making him a low-end fantasy option in deeper formats.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jonnu Smith has posted two very similar stat lines in his first two games with Pittsburgh, accruing 10 targets but only 42 yards. As those numbers imply, he's used primarily in short areas of the field, though Pat Freiermuth's involvement in the offense cuts into Smith's volume. Smith is a touchdown-or-bust fantasy option in Week 3 against New England. There should be better candidates available at tight end.

player.seasonOutlook: Smith was traded to the Steelers in June following a career year in Miami in which he finished top 5 among tight ends in targets, receptions, yards, fantasy points and touchdowns. This after never finishing better than 15th in the former four categories during his first seven NFL seasons. Smith's season actually started slowly (4.9 targets per game and one game with 12-plus fantasy points during Weeks 1-10), but he averaged 8.5 targets and a position-high 18.6 PPG from Week 11 on. Smith is now reunited with Arthur Smith, which isn't necisarily a good thing, as averaged single-digit fantay points during three prior seasons with Smith calling the plays. Pittsburgh is shaky at wideout, so Smith will play plenty, but his target ceiling is much lower with Pat Freiermuth also in the mix. Smith is best valued as a mid-to-back-end TE2.

outlooksByWeek.1: Miles Sanders looks like the backup for the Cowboys at running back in Week 1, but the rest of the situation involving carries out of the backfield remains murky. Javonte Williams looks like the starter, but rookie Jaydon Blue will also compete for touches, and all three could see work in the season opener. The Cowboys could also simply ride the hot hand in this committee approach. In Week 1, Dallas will face an Eagles defense that was rather stingy against the run in 2024. Philadelphia allowed just 104.2 yards per clash on the ground, which was 10th in the league. The Eagles also yielded just nine rushing scores last year, which second in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.2: Miles Sanders looked like the backup running back in Week 1 for the Cowboys.  While Javonte Williams rushed 15 times for 54 yards and two scores in the narrow 24-20 loss to the Eagles, Sanders received only four carries and fumbled one of them. Sanders did manage 53 yards despite the limited touches, though clearly played second-fiddle to Williams. On the plus side, Jaydon Blue was a healthy scratch, and no other running back on the roster received a carry for the game. If Sanders can see a few more touches in Week 2, he will have a tasty matchup against a Giants run defense that was gutted in its season opener. New York allowed a staggering 220 yards and two touchdowns on the ground in a 21-6 loss to the Commanders.
outlooksByWeek.3: Miles Sanders did manage to find the end zone for the Cowboys last game. Unfortunately, Sanders had just 19 scrimmage yards, and starting running back Javonte Williams garnered four times as many touches as Sanders. Williams rushed for 97 yards and a touchdown of his own, while also catching six passes out of the backfield. Sanders will need the game to get out of hand against the Bears in Week 3 to play a significant role in the offense. That could be a possibility, though, as Chicago is allowing 148.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is 27th in the NFL. Likewise, Chicago has allowed the most points in the league through two weeks, including 52 last game against the Lions.

player.seasonOutlook: Sanders signed with Dallas after failing to pan out during his two seasons in Carolina. Signed to a multiyear contract prior to 2023, Sanders was handed the Panthers' lead-back gig, but lost it to Chuba Hubbard within a matter of weeks. He went on to average 8.3 touches per game and score a total of two touchdowns in 26 outings prior to putting up a 116-yard, 2-TD showing with Hubbard sidelined last season. Perhaps that proves he still has some gas left in the tank, but now 28 years old and not much of a contributor as a pass catcher, it's unlikely Sanders will find his way to the fantasy radar. He'll battle Javonte Williams and rookie Jaydon Blue for work in Dallas, and is only worth a late flier in deep leagues.

outlooksByWeek.1: Dyami Brown will make his Jaguars debut in Week 1 against the Panthers after spending four years in Washington. He didn't have more than 308 receiving yards in a season with the Commanders but enjoyed a strong playoff run last season, recording 229 yards and a TD in three postseason games. Brown and Parker Washington are competing for the third spot on the WR depth chart behind Brian Thomas and Travis Hunter, whom the Jaguars selected with their last two first-round picks. Outside of deeper formats, Brown is off the fantasy radar for now.
outlooksByWeek.2: Dyami Brown is in the deep-league flex conversation for Week 2 against the Bengals. He had a solid Jaguars debut last week, turning four targets and two carries into 58 scrimmage yards while working as the team's No. 3 wide receiver behind Brian Thomas and Travis Hunter. Brown hasn't topped 308 receiving yards in four previous seasons but appears poised to easily surpass that mark in a larger role with his new team.
outlooksByWeek.3: Dyami Brown recorded 58 scrimmage yards in his Jaguars debut and followed that up with 66 scrimmage yards and a touchdown in Week 2. He should have captured a second receiving TD in Week 2 but had an egregious drop in the end zone. That error aside, Brown's involvement early in the season has been encouraging. His strong start has Brown in the Week 3 flex discussion at home against a Texans secondary that allowed 21 receiving TD to wide receivers last season, tied for the second-most in the NFL.

outlooksByWeek.1: Ashton Jeanty was widely expected to be the first running back off the board in the 2025 Draft, and when the Raiders called his name at sixth overall, he became the highest-drafted RB since Saquon Barkley went No. 2 in 2018. Jeanty offers the power and contact balance to break tackles, but he can also simply run by defenders using his elite speed, and his three-down skill set should fit perfectly as the centerpiece of new offensive coordinator Chip Kelly's ground-heavy scheme. The rookie has little competition for touches in the Las Vegas backfield, and stud tight end Brock Bowers might be his only serious competition for volume overall. Jeanty could make a splash in his NFL debut, facing a Patriots defense in Week 1 that ranked 30th in rushing yards allowed to RBs last season.
outlooksByWeek.2: Ashton Jeanty found the end zone in his NFL debut, but he turned 19 carries into just 38 yards, while adding two receiving yards on two catches. The sixth overall pick in the 2025 Draft is the Raiders' unquestioned No. 1 RB, as Zamir White was the only other RB to garner action in Week 1 with a meager three carries. Jeanty will need the team's rebuilt offensive line to gel in a hurry if he's going to live up to his pre-draft hype, but his big-play potential is evident. He'll look to break out in Week 2 against a Chargers defense that just held the Kansas City backfield in check, giving up a league-low four rushing TDs to running backs in 2024.
outlooksByWeek.3: Ashton Jeanty failed to gain much yardage again in Week 2, managing just 44 scrimmage yards on 14 touches, and he didn't get into the end zone as he did in his NFL debut. The sixth overall pick in the 2025 Draft has faced a couple tough defensive fronts in the Patriots and Chargers to begin his career, but he also hasn't contributed yet as a pass-catcher with the Raiders adjusting to a new QB, new RB and new offensive coordinator. Once Geno Smith and Jeanty get on the same page, the rookie back's skills should begin to show. Jeanty could get going in Week 3 against a Commanders defense that just gave up 84 rushing yards and a TD to the Packers' Josh Jacobs.

player.seasonOutlook: Jeanty was selected by Las Vegas with the No. 6 overall pick in April's draft. He is the No. 1 fantasy prospect in this rookie class following a dominant tenure at Boise State. Incredibly, he ranked first in this class in YAC and broken tackle rate both last season and during his collegiate career. Jeanty's elite playmaking ability and a three-down skill set supply him with the upside to be the next elite NFL running back. He's positioned for a feature-back role right out of the gate and should be valued as a midrange RB1.

outlooksByWeek.1: Puka Nacua will begin his third NFL campaign for the Rams with a Week 1 matchup against Houston. Nacua remains Los Angeles' projected WR1 despite the offseason addition of Davante Adams. Nacua has shown that he can be plenty productive with another top-flight WR next to him, as he shined in his first two campaigns playing alongside Cooper Kupp. The Rams' wideouts could be in for a big Week 1 against a Texans defense that ranked 20th in receiving yards allowed to wide receivers last year.
outlooksByWeek.2: Puka Nacua shined in the Rams' season-opening win and will look to continue doing so against Tennessee in Week 2. Nacua racked up 10 catches on 11 targets for 130 yards against Houston in the season opener, though he wasn't able to get into the end zone. The presence of newcomer Davante Adams didn't negatively impact Nacua's attention from veteran QB Matthew Stafford at all, though Adams fared decently with a 4-51-0 line on eight targets. Tennessee gave up a modest 120 yards through the air to WRs in Week 1 against Denver, but Nacua certainly has the talent to surpass that mark on his own this coming Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.3: Puka Nacua will look to continue what has been a productive two games for the Rams in Sunday's Week 3 matchup against Philadelphia. Nacua tallied 130 total yards in Week 1 and 136 total yards in Week 2, though a big portion of that latter total came on a 45-yard rushing touchdown. Regardless, Nacua continues to form a strong bond with QB Matthew Stafford, as he's racked up 18 catches on 20 targets for 221 receiving yards through two weeks. Nacua may be challenged to keep up that efficiency in Week 3 -- though Philadelphia got torched by Dallas' top wideout CeeDee Lamb for seven catches and 110 yards in Week 1, it took Lamb 13 targets to record those stats, and no Kansas City wideout managed more than 59 receiving yards against the Eagles in Week 2.

player.seasonOutlook: After exploding for 1,486 yards on 105 catches as a fifth-round rookie in 2023, Nacua produced 990 yards on 79 catches last season despite missing six games and a substantial chunk of two others. Once he was full-go in Week 10, Nacua went on to handle a massive 37% target share (11.3 per game) and his average of 22.3 fantasy points during the span would have ranked second over the full season. He led all receivers in yards per route run (3.7). The one concern with Nacua is touchdowns, as he has only 10 in 28 career games, and he was limited to six end zone targets (53rd at WR) in 2024. That said, with Cooper Kupp out and Davante Adams in, Nacua remains well positioned for a massive target share in a good Rams offense that has led the NFL in WR targets each of the last two seasons. After finishing sixth in fantasy PPG as a rookie and third in 2024, Nacua should be off the board in the first round.

outlooksByWeek.1: Jayden Daniels was simply spectacular as a rookie last season in Washington, winning Rookie of the Year and leading the Commanders to the NFC Championship Game. Daniels passed for 3,568 yards and 25 touchdowns, while rushing for an additional 891 yards and six more scores on the ground. The dual-threat ability of Daniels was always going to be in the cards, but his accuracy as a passer as well as his ability to take care of the ball was far better than advertised. In Week 1, Daniels and company will face a much-improved Giants defense that added No. 3 pick Abdul Carter to an already ferocious defensive line, as well as safety Jevon Holland and cornerback Paulson Adebo to the secondary. Daniels failed to throw for over 230 yards in either matchup against the Giants in 2024.
outlooksByWeek.2: Jayden Daniels appeared to pick up where he left off from last season in Week 1 for the Commanders.  Daniels threw for 233 yards and a touchdown and ran for 68 more yards, albeit against an inferior opponent in the form of the New York Giants. The competition stiffens in Week 2 when Washington travels to Green Bay. The Packers dominated the Lions in their opener, allowing just 200 yards passing and 46 yards rushing; the latter figure was tied for the lowest mark in Week 1. Daniels is also not sneaking up on anyone this time around after his dynamic rookie campaign.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jayden Daniels tossed two touchdowns against the Packers last game but suffered a mysterious knee injury, casting a shadow over Washington's Week 3 clash with the Las Vegas Raiders. Daniels rushed for just 17 yards in the contest, and while the Green Bay defense deserves kudos for holding Daniels in check, there may have been more going on than just a stiff front seven. Daniels has yet to run for a touchdown this season and completed under 60-percent of his throws through two contests, so there may be cause for concern here. Washington will face a lackluster Raiders pass defense in Week 3, though Marcus Mariota could end up being the quarterback under center for this tilt.

player.seasonOutlook: Daniels is entering his second NFL season after what was arguably the greatest rookie season ever by a quarterback. The dual-threat playmaker was productive as a passer and even better as a rusher, ranking no lower than third among QBs in carries, rushing yards, rush TDs, carries inside the 5 and scrambles. Daniels produced 355.8 fantasy points, which trails only Cam Newton (370.3) for most by a rookie. He showed a high ceiling, having delivered 24-plus points in eight games, including his final five full regular-season outings). Entering Year 2 with an even better supporting cast that now includes Deebo Samuel Sr. and Laremy Tunsil, Daniels has a strong case to be the first QB off the board in fantasy drafts.

outlooksByWeek.1: Alvin Kamara enters his ninth season with the Saints, leading the backfield versus Arizona in Week 1. Kamara bounced back in 2024 after seeing declining numbers in every year since 2020, and New Orleans has made no moves that suggest the veteran won't be a focal point of the offense once again. The 30-year-old RB's skill and likely volume should still make him a fantasy asset, especially against a Cards defense that was shaky against running backs last season.
outlooksByWeek.2: Alvin Kamara will look to lead the Saints' backfield again in Week 2 versus the 49ers. Kamara wasn't as much of a workhorse as expected against the Cardinals in Week 1, but he still rushed for 45 yards and a touchdown off 11 carries and nabbed two catches for 12 yards. The overall touches for the veteran show that he's still the clear-cut RB1, and he looks ahead of Kendre Miller and rookie Devin Neal. Given that Kellen Moore's new offense also looks to heavily lean on the passing game, Kamara should continue to be a consistent dual-threat running back even against a tough 49ers defense.
outlooksByWeek.3: Alvin Kamara will aim to expand on a 120-yard performance as the Saints travel to Seattle in Week 3. Kamara was a force in a close loss to the 49ers in Week 2, totaling 99 rushing yards and 21 receiving yards off 27 total touches. The veteran rusher still has full command of New Orleans' backfield by a long shot, and he should continue to command the RB role both as a rusher and receiver moving forward. Kamara should have the capacity to combine his already consistent rushing upside with a big receiving game in his third game of the season. Seattle's defense has also given up  159 combined receiving yards to the Steelers' Jaylen Warren and the 49ers' Christian McCaffrey to begin the season.

player.seasonOutlook: Kamara returns to New Orleans for his ninth NFL season following an impressive, albeit injury-shortened 2024 campaign. Appearing in 14 games, Kamara soaked up 228 carries (12 off his career high) and led all backs in targets. He has yet to finish a season lower than fifth among RBs in targets, or lower than ninth in catches and receiving yards. That has translated in fantasy, as he's finished eighth or better in fantasy PPG in seven of his eight seasons. On the concerning side is durability, as Kamara hasn't played a full regular season since his rookie year (2017) and is now 30 years old. Additionally, the Saints' offense figures to struggle following Derek Carr's retirement. Kamara's clear path to touches and elite receiving work keeps him in the fringe RB1 discussion, but there's obvious risk here.

outlooksByWeek.1: T.J. Hockenson is locked and loaded as Minnesota's clear top tight end heading into a road Week 1 matchup against Chicago. Across the 10 games he suited up for in 2024 after recovering from ACL surgery, Hockenson's production never returned to his pre-injury totals, as he racked up just 455 yards and zero TDs on the year. Now after an additional offseason to fully regain his explosiveness, and to build chemistry with new QB J.J. McCarthy, Hockenson appears positioned to hit the ground running, especially as the three-game suspension of Jordan Addison frees up a clear path for the TE to operate in an expanded role alongside star WR Justin Jefferson.
outlooksByWeek.2: T.J. Hockenson will look to increase his involvement as the Vikings take on the Falcons in prime time Week 2. He secured three of four targets for 15 yards during the team's narrow Week 1 win over the Bears, though in the red zone J.J. McCarthy interestingly looked the way of Josh Oliver, whose only catch for five yards didn't go long enough to actually hit paydirt. Hockenson's four targets were second on the team behind Justin Jefferson (five targets), and it wouldn't be surprising if this 143-yard passing debut ends up being McCarthy's lowest total of the season. Brighter days, in other words, figure to be around the corner for the No. 1 tight end.
outlooksByWeek.3: T.J. Hockenson will work to bounce back as the Vikings travel to Cincinnati in Week 3. Through two appearances this season, Hockenson has tallied just four catches for 27 yards on seven targets. Now, with J.J. McCarthy considered week-to-week due to a high-ankle sprain, Hockenson will need to both find his own groove and establish chemistry with a new QB under center. Jordan Addison (suspension) will be eligible for reinstatement beginning Week 4, at which time Hockenson's involvement in the receiving game will be at risk of taking a further step back.

player.seasonOutlook: Hockenson is eyeing a bounce-back following a 2024 season in which he missed Weeks 1-7 and was limited a bit upon his return while rebounding from a torn ACL suffered in 2023. Hockenson appeared in 10 regular-season games, but was limited to 60% of the snaps and averaged 6.1 targets and 8.7 fantasy points per game. That's a far cry from his 80% snap share, 8.5 targets per game and 14.6 PPG the season prior. Hockenson entered last season having finished seventh or better among TEs in fantasy PPG four years in a row (top 5 in both 2022 and 2023), so it's reasonable to expect him to return to that level in 2025. New QB J.J. McCarthy is a wild card, but Kevin O'Connell's pass-friendly offense should help keep Hockenson in the weekly TE1 mix.

outlooksByWeek.1: Garrett Wilson expects to be a target monster for the Jets entering Week 1 against the Steelers. While he didn't record a catch in the preseason, there's established chemistry with quarterback Justin Fields from their college days, and the lack of receiving depth behind him suggests he'll be a true alpha. The Steelers allowed just 7.2 yards per attempt last season however, suggesting Wilson will need to rely on volume to produce a WR2 return.
outlooksByWeek.2: Garrett Wilson figures to remain a target monster for the Jets in Week 2 against the Bills. Wilson saw nine targets in Week 1, collecting seven of them for 95 yards and a touchdown, tripling the volume of any other New York receiver. While it remains a low volume passing scheme, Wilson's workload looks unquestioned, and he'll face a defense that allowed a 7-143-1 line to Baltimore's Zay Flowers last week. All signs confidently point to a solid outing.
outlooksByWeek.3: Garrett Wilson remains a target monster regardless of who is under center for the Jets in Week 3 at Tampa Bay. Wilson has logged nine and eight targets to open the season and is averaging 13.2 yards per reception, his highest rate since his rookie 2022 campaign. Justin Fields (concussion) is uncertain to play, but Tyrod Taylor can also force looks Wilson's way against a defense that hasn't allowed more than 55 yards to an opposing wide receiver to open the year, suggesting Wilson comes with stable expectations.

player.seasonOutlook: Wilson is entering his fourth NFL season having produced at least 148 targets, 83 catches and 1,042 yards in each of his first three campaigns. Despite the presence of Davante Adams for two-thirds of last season, Wilson posted career highs in catches, yards and TDs. He finished sixth or better among WRs in targets all three seasons, but has yet to finish a season better than 20th in fantasy PPG due to underwhelming TD totals (14 in 51 games). Wilson's assured of a hefty target share, which will keep him fantasy-relevant, but his overall volume may suffer with dual-threat Justin Fields now under center. Wilson will need a lot to go right in order to produce at a WR1 level, so the 25-year-old is best viewed as a fringe top-20 receiver.

outlooksByWeek.1: Rome Odunze and the Bears will kick off Week 1 at home against a Vikings defense that ranked 31st against opposing WRs last season. Both Odunze and QB Caleb Williams will look to get off to a hot start and begin putting their disappointing rookie campaigns in the rear-view, a goal which new head coach Ben Johnson's scheme should be immensely helpful in facilitating. Odunze's path to a Year 2 breakout is clear, as replacing Keenan Allen with a pair of rookies, WR Luther Burden and TE Colston Loveland, bolster's Chicago's offense while allowing the 2024 first-round pick to remain entrenched as the most experienced Bears wideout other than DJ Moore. Moore, Burden and Loveland admittedly represent crowded target competition, but all project to be best utilized in the short and intermediate areas of the field, leaving Odunze as Chicago's clear top downfield threat.
outlooksByWeek.2: Rome Odunze and the Bears will travel to Detroit in Week 2, as he aims to build on a steady debut. The second-year pro caught six of a team-high nine targets for thirty-seven yards and a touchdown in the team's Week 1 loss to Minnesota. While Odunze couldn't break off any chunk plays in the opener, his red-zone score highlighted Caleb Williams' trust in him as a go-to option in short-area situations. That role could be pivotal against a Lions defense that looked vulnerable in coverage rotations near the goal line during their Week 1 loss to the Packers. Odunze's floor is tied to red-zone usage, but he still has untapped downfield potential that coach Ben Johnson figures to prioritize unlocking sooner rather than later.
outlooksByWeek.3: Rome Odunze will work to keep up his momentum as the Bears prepare to host the Cowboys in Week 3. The second-year pro caught seven passes for 128 yards and two touchdowns in Chicago's 52-21 loss to Detroit, operating as the focal point of the team's offense. Odunze displayed his trademark big-play ability versus Detroit, especially in the red zone, hauling in both of Caleb Williams' touchdowns and showing strong separation on intermediate routes throughout the game. With all of DJ Moore, Olamide Zaccheaus, Luther Burden, Cole Kmet and Colston Loveland demanding attention, Odunze should continue to see favorable one-on-one matchups. The Cowboys' secondary has shown some vulnerable zones and allowed chunk gains in early plays this season, making Odunze a fair candidate to log another strong performance.

player.seasonOutlook: Odunze is entering his second NFL season with hopes for a leap forward after an uneven rookie campaign. The 2024 No. 9 overall pick was on the field a ton (eighth among WRs in routes) and was busy near the goal line (11th in the NFL with 13 end zone targets), but he ended up 35th or lower at the position in targets, catches, yards and TDs. Odunze had some poor scoring luck (three TDs, 6.7 expected), which was partially to blame for him scoring single-digit fantasy points in 13 of 17 games. There are a lot of mouths to feed in Chicago, but with Caleb Williams entering Year 2 and Ben Johnson now running the offense, Odunze is an extremely logical breakout candidate. He should be one of your favorite midround targets.

outlooksByWeek.1: Jordan Addison will miss the Vikings' first three games of the regular season due to a suspension, beginning Week 1 on the road against Chicago. In his absence, Adam Thielen and Jalen Nailor figure to benefit from increased targets behind Justin Jefferson and TE T.J. Hockenson.
outlooksByWeek.2: Jordan Addison will serve the second contest of his three-game suspension as the Vikings prepare for a matchup against the Falcons on Sunday Night Football in Week 2. In his stead, Adam Thielen and Jalen Nailor will handle increased roles behind top wideout Justin Jefferson. By the time Addison is back on the field, quarterback J.J. McCarthy will have had a chance to have gotten more comfortable at the NFL level, though it'll be notable that the two will have missed crucial opportunities to build chemistry across the first month of the regular season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jordan Addison will serve the final contest of his three-game suspension as the Vikings prepare for a matchup against the Bengals in Week 3. In his stead, Adam Thielen and Jalen Nailor will continue increased roles behind top wideout Justin Jefferson. With J.J. McCarthy a candidate to miss Week 3 due to a high-ankle sprain, however, it remains to be seen whether he or Carson Wentz will be lining up under center by the time Addison is back in action.

player.seasonOutlook: Addison returns for Year 3 in Minnesota having finished 23rd and 21st, respectively, in fantasy PPG during his first two NFL campaigns. Addison has been a TD machine, scoring 10 times in both seasons, which has helped offset underwhelming volume. He finished both seasons 25th or lower among WRs in targets, receptions and yards, as well as 40th or lower in target share. That led to boom/bust production last season, as he scored 43% of his fantasy points in three games and was held to single digits in seven of 15 outings. Addison is suspended three games to begin the 2025 season, but once he's on the field, he will continue battling for looks with Justin Jefferson and T.J. Hockenson. His late-season target surge (eight-plus in seven of his final eight games) provides optimism that he can sustain WR3 numbers, especially in Kevin O'Connell's pass-friendly scheme.

outlooksByWeek.1: Javonte Williams looks like the starter for the Cowboys at running back in Week 1, but the rest of the situation involving carries out of the backfield remains murky. Dallas also brought in Miles Sanders along with rookie Jaydon Blue to compete for touches, and all three could see work in the season opener. The Cowboys could also simply ride the hot hand in this committee approach. In Week 1, Dallas will face an Eagles defense that was rather stingy against the run in 2024. Philadelphia allowed just 104.2 yards per clash on the ground, which was 10th in the league. The Eagles also yielded just nine rushing scores last year, which second in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.2: Javonte Williams scored twice in the season opener for the Cowboys, cementing himself as the lead back in Dallas. Williams rushed 15 times for 54 yards and the two scores in the narrow 24-20 loss to the Eagles. Fellow rusher Miles Sanders did rush for 53 yards, though received only four carries and fumbled one of them. Jaydon Blue was a healthy scratch, and no other running back on the roster received a carry for the game. In Week 2, Williams will have a tasty matchup against a Giants run defense that was gutted in its season opener. New York allowed a staggering 220 yards and two touchdowns on the ground in a 21-6 loss to the Commanders.
outlooksByWeek.3: Javonte Williams has scored three times in two games for the Dallas Cowboys. Williams took advantage of a porous Giants run defense en route to 97 yards and the score on the ground. Williams was also a key contributor in the passing game, reeling in six balls for an additional 33 yards. Williams is the surefire starting back for Dallas heading into a Week 3 clash with a bumbling Bears defense. Chicago is allowing 148.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is 27th in the NFL. Likewise, Chicago has allowed the most points in the league through two weeks.

player.seasonOutlook: Williams signed with Dallas after an up-and-down four seasons in Denver. The 2021 second-round pick exploded out of the gate with 1,219 yards and seven TDs as a rookie, but was never able to match either number the following three seasons. Sean Payton's scheme helped Williams to 72 targets (fifth most among RBs) last season, but that wasn't enough for Williams to log his first top-25 fantasy campaign on a per-game basis. Perhaps Brian Schottenheimer can reignite Williams' career (Miles Sanders and fifth-round rookie Jaydon Blue are his only competition for touches), but the 25-year-old is unlikely to emerge as anything more than a flex.

outlooksByWeek.1: Chris Godwin is not expected to play for the Buccaneers in Week 1 at the Falcons because of an ankle injury. He opened training camp on the active/PUP list in recovery from a 2024 season-ending dislocated left ankle that required surgery. The veteran pass catcher has since been activated off the list, but an October season debut is most likely than Week 1. Rookie Emeka Egbuka should be the No. 2 wide receiver behind Mike Evans.
outlooksByWeek.2: Chris Godwin is not expected to play for the Buccaneers in Week 2 at Houston as he works back from an ankle injury. The veteran pass catcher was activated off the active/PUP list in late August, but he's still unlikely to see the field until Week 5. His absence should open up more opportunities for Emeka Egbuka and Sterling Shepard, as it did in Tampa Bay's season opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chris Godwin is not expected to play for the Buccaneers in Week 3 versus the Jets as he works back from an ankle injury. The veteran pass catcher was activated off the active/PUP list in late August, but he's still unlikely to see the field until Week 5. His absence should continue to open up opportunities for rookie Emeka Egbuka and veteran Sterling Shepard, as it did in the first two weeks.

player.seasonOutlook: Godwin has had some big seasons during his eight years in the league, but he was well on his way to his best one yet in 2024 prior to suffering a season-ending ankle injury in Week 7. In his seven games, the veteran receiver averaged 19.7 fantasy PPG and caught 79% of his passes, both of which ranked second at the position. Perhaps most notably, Godwin scored five TDs in seven games, which was somewhat unsustainable (2.1 xTD) but nonetheless a step forward after he totaled 10 TDs the prior three seasons (46 games). Godwin is still in his prime at age 29 and now seemingly Baker Mayfield's top target, but he's going to miss games to open the season. Once back, he's well positioned for a big comeback season and could rise as high as WR1 territory. He's best valued as a midround lottery ticket.

outlooksByWeek.1: Cameron Dicker continues to earn his Dicker the Kicker nickname. The 25-year-old set a career high with nine field goals from 50 yards or longer on 11 attempts Smith-Schuster, en route to career-high volume with a 39-for-42 performance. Over 44 games since joining the Chargers in 2022, Dicker has converted 93.7% of his FG attempts and 96.8% of his PAT attempts. He may need to take advantage of all his opportunities during a Week 1 trip to Sao Paulo against a Kansas City team that allowed only 6.0 points per game to kickers in 2024, tied for fourth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.2: Cameron Dicker was perfect in the Chargers' Week 1 win, drilling two short field goals and three extra points. The 25-year-old has been one of the most accurate kickers in the NFL the last two seasons, and there's no sign of decline to begin 2025. Dicker attempted a career-high 42 FGs last year, but bigger volume could be headed his way if the Chargers offense is more potent this season thanks to the return of Keenan Allen and the addition of first-round pick Omarion Hampton. Dicker will face a Raiders team in Week 2 that gave up 9.1 points per game to kickers in 2024, the second-worst mark in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.3: Cameron Dicker remains perfect on the season, kicking multiple field goals and multiple extra points in each game as the Chargers jump out to a 2-0 start. Dicker has yet to attempt a FG of 40 yards or longer, but length has never been an issue, going 16-for-20 on attempts of 50-plus yards over the prior two seasons. With Justin Herbert and the passing game looking more dangerous than expected, there should be plenty of volume available for Dicker. He could be very busy in Week 3 against a Broncos team that's allowed nine FG attempts, but only two TDs, through the first two weeks.

player.seasonOutlook: Despite the early loss of DE Aidan Hutchinson, the Lions' defense managed to score the 12th-most fantasy points in 2024. That said, the unit faded badly down the stretch, ultimately finishing 32nd in pass defense, and defensive coordinator Aaron Glenn is now heading up the Jets (replaced by former linebackers coach Kelvin Sheppard). Hutchinson's healthy return will help, but the Lions' schedule is a doozy, with six games against projected top-eight offenses. They have top-10 talent, but their soft matchups are few and their downside is greater than most.

outlooksByWeek.1: Kyle Pitts will look to turn his career around with Atlanta starting in Week 1 versus the Buccaneers. Pitts has consistently disappointed since setting expectations extremely high with 1,026 receiving yards as a rookie. The 24-year-old will luckily have a change at the quarterback role with second-year Michael Penix under center, but this may not mean too much for the tight end. While Penix has committed to giving Pitts a bigger role this season, similar hype has been given to the tight end in previous years. This makes it tough to gauge Pitts' week-to-week upside, although Tampa Bay wasn't great against tight ends last year.
outlooksByWeek.2: Kyle Pitts will look to build off some momentum as the Falcons take on the Vikings in Week 2. Pitts finished second in receptions, targets and receiving yards for Atlanta in an eventual Week 1 loss against Tampa Bay, bringing in seven of his eight targets for 59 yards. This reception total was equal to or more than every single outing last season, and yardage total was at-par or better than all but four of his games last season. This could mean Pitts is in for a high-volume role this season, especially with new quarterback Michael Penix under center. Pitts could most definitely continue this role against a Minnesota defense that gave up three catches for 43 yards to Bears tight ends, and struggled early on against Chicago's passing game this past week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kyle Pitts looks to be a top target in Atlanta's offense once again at Carolina in Week 3. Pitts brought in four receptions for 37 yards off five targets this past week against Minnesota. This stat line looks relatively small, but the fifth-year tight end actually tied his team in targets and had the most catches. After two weeks, Pitts has 11 grabs for 96 yards and has been a top option for young quarterback Michael Penix. The Panthers have also let tight ends Brenton Strange (5-59-0) and then Trey McBride (6-78-0) be the top pass catchers for their squads in back-to-back weeks, which could bode well for Pitts in the upcoming away game.

player.seasonOutlook: We're now four years into the Kyle Pitts experience and it's safe to say things aren't going as well as expected. The 2021 No. 4 overall pick exploded out of the gate with 1,026 yards and an 11th-place finish in fantasy PPG as a 20-year-old rookie, but he's yet to come close to those marks since, peaking at 667 yards and 17th in PPG (both in 2023). Pitts did post career highs in TDs (four) and end zone targets (seven) last season, but his 14% target share was a career low and ranked 25th among TEs. He wasn't even playing half the snaps during the final month of the season, leaving his role very much in question for 2025. He has the pedigree and is still only 24 years old, but Pitts can't be trusted as anything more than a bench lottery ticket.

outlooksByWeek.1: Quinshon Judkins remains unsigned after experiencing some legal troubles this offseason. He will not be criminally charged but could face a suspension and did not participate in training camp or the preseason. Judkins could make a difference for the Browns at some point in 2025, but it will almost certainly not come in Week 1 against Cincinnati.
outlooksByWeek.2: Quinshon Judkins appears to be putting a tumultuous offseason behind him, as he inked his rookie contract with the Browns last week. He can remain on the Commissioner's Exempt List for two games, meaning he'll be able to practice but not play so long as he isn't activated. Even if Judkins does suit up in Week 2 against Baltimore, he'll likely need some ramp-up time to earn enough touches to be considered for fantasy purposes.
outlooksByWeek.3: Quinshon Judkins made his much-awaited NFL debut in Week 2 and immediately took over as the Browns' top rusher. He accounted for over half of his 61 yards on one carry late in the fourth quarter in a blowout loss, but Judkins' role was still encouraging. The poor state of the Browns' offense and a tough matchup in Week 3 against Green Bay should give fantasy managers pause in the short term. Consider Judkins a mediocre FLEX option.

player.seasonOutlook: Judkins was selected by Cleveland in the second round of April's draft. He is a big, tough runner who showed well at the combine, including an RB-best 132-inch broad jump and a 4.48 40 at 221 pounds. He figures to be busy near the goal line in the pros, as he was in college (16-plus TDs in all three seasons). He can catch the ball a bit, but wasn't overly impressive in that area at Ole Miss and Ohio State. Judkins figures to eventually step in as Cleveland's lead back, though he may defer some work to Jerome Ford and fellow rookie Dylan Sampson, especially as he deals with the ramifications of a July arrest. Once fully integrated into the offense, Judkins will be a solid bet for weekly RB2 fantasy production, but the off-field trouble may lead to little-to-no early season work.

outlooksByWeek.1: Tre Harris parlayed consistent college production at Ole Miss into a second-round selection in the 2025 Draft, and there's a path for him to make his mark in the NFL right away. Quentin Johnston has been a disappointment through two seasons for the Chargers, and Harris offers similar size and downfield ability without the drops. Jim Harbaugh's offense prioritizes the run though, and even if he beats out Johnston for a role, Harris would be behind Ladd McConkey and likely returning veteran Keenan Allen for targets. The rookie's big-play ability could come in handy in a Week 1 trip to Sao Paulo against a Kansas City secondary that ranked sixth in receiving yards allowed to WRs but tied for 24th in receiving TDs allowed to the position.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tre' Harris was a little more involved in the Chargers' passing game in Week 2 than he was in his NFL debut, catching two of three targets for 34 yards in a win over the Raiders. The 2025 second-round pick remains firmly behind Ladd McConkey, Keenan Allen and Quentin Johnston on the WR depth chart, but Justin Herbert has put the ball in the air more often than expected to begin the season, which could create more opportunities for Harris even without injuries at the position. Despite the fact that he's beginning to trend in the right direction, Harris isn't likely to make a splash in Week 3 against a Broncos secondary that has yet to allow a receiving touchdown to a wide receiver this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Harris was selected by the Chargers in the second round of April's draft. He is a tall, fast, perimeter WR whose absurd 5.20 YPRR last season was more than a yard higher than any other WR in this class. His 3.04 career mark also topped this class and came on a hefty 1,164 routes across 51 games. Harris' path to rookie-season work is tricky. While he easily could emerge as the team's top perimeter receiver, he could also begin his career behind behind Keenan Allen, Quentin Johnston and slot Ladd McConkey in target priority. Harris is a fine late-round flier, but has work to do in order to become a weekly fantasy starter.

outlooksByWeek.1: Caleb Williams will look to bounce back strong from his disastrous rookie campaign as the Bears kick off Week 1 at home against Minnesota. Opening the year with a tough matchup against Minnesota defensive coordinator Brian Flores' aggressive scheme isn't exactly ideal for Williams, especially with growing pains to be expected as he adapts to new head coach Ben Johnson's complex offensive scheme, but Chicago spent the offseason bringing in enough support that the second-year quarterback should have the tools to overcome any obstacles he encounters. In addition to drafting TE Colston Loveland 10th overall and WR Luther Burden 39th overall, adding them to a skill-position group that already included DJ Moore, Rome Odunze and D'Andre Swift, the Bears have remade the O-line into what should be a top-10 unit.
outlooksByWeek.2: Caleb Williams and the Bears will travel to Detroit in Week 2, ready to bounce back after a gritty Week 1 loss to the Vikings. Williams completed 21 of 35 passes for 210 yards and a score versus Minnesota, adding another touchdown on the ground while rushing six times for a team-high 58 yards. Crucially, he protected the ball with no turnovers despite facing constant pressure from Brian Flores' defense.The Packers managed to dissect Detroit's secondary in Week 1, and Jordan Love finishing with just two touchdowns and 188 passing yards was much more a product of the team getting out to a 17-3 lead in the second quarter and closing out the game with a run-focused approach.  New head coach Ben Johnson figures to similarly take advantage of creative pre-snap movement to exploit vulnerabilities of the Loins' pressure-first scheme, putting Williams in fair position to bounce back.
outlooksByWeek.3: Caleb Williams and the Bears host the Cowboys in Week 3, searching for their first win of the season. Chicago is looking to rebound after a rough 52-21 loss to the Lions in which Williams completed 19 of 30 passes for 207 yards, two touchdowns and one interception. Williams was under heavy duress throughout the game, taking four sacks while struggling to find consistency against Detroit's pressure packages. He now faces a Dallas defense with a Micah Parsons-sized hole in it, but which just added Jadeveon Clowney to try and fill it. While Williams' playmaking ability gives him upside in broken plays, and it could simply be a matter of time before he fully finds his footing in coach Ben Johnson's offense, he has to be considered a volatile fantasy option until such time as Chicago's scheme proves that it's developed cohesion.

player.seasonOutlook: Williams is entering his second NFL season with hopes for a leap forward under new head coach and playcaller Ben Johnson. The 2024 No. 1 pick had a few big games (22-plus fantasy points five times), but way too many major duds (nine games with fewer than 12 points) during his first season. Efficiency was an issue (outside of the top 35 in QBR, YPA and completion %) and he took a league-high 68 sacks, but he got experience (QB2 in dropbacks), avoided INTs (seven) and added value with his legs (seventh at QB in carries, rush yards and YPC). With Johnson designing the offense, a much-improved interior offensive line and a good supporting cast led by DJ Moore, Rome Odunze, Colston Loveland and Luther Burden III, Williams has no excuses as he enters a critical Year 2. He's safest when drafted as a fringe QB1, but he has a very high ceiling.
